ONU : la Quatrième Commission adopte la résolution sur le Sahara marocain
items.description: La Quatrième Commission de l’Assemblée générale des Nations Unies a adopté, ce jeudi, sa résolution annuelle sur la question du Sahara Marocain, par 152 voix pour, dont celle du Maroc, deux voix contre et sept abstentions. Présenté par le Président sénégalais de la Quatrième Commission, ce projet de résolution est traditionnellement adopté sans vote, conformément à une pratique consensuelle établie depuis 2006. Cette année, le texte a exceptionnellement fait l’objet d’un scrutin, à la suite d’une demande de dernière minute formulée par la délégation des Etats-Unis, portant sur l’ensemble des 23 projets de résolution soumis à l’examen de la Quatrième Commission, sans exception, y compris celles traditionnellement adoptées par consens ou sans vote. Cette démarche américaine traduit l’orientation du Département d’Etat américain visant à exiger un vote sur l’ensemble des résolutions des six Grandes Commissions de l’Assemblée générale, sans exception aucune, y compris celles relatives aux questions de sécurité et de désarmement, de développement durable, humanitaires et des droits de l’Homme, ainsi que les questions juridiques et du budget des Nations Unies. Le Maroc a voté en faveur de ce texte, aux côtés des 151 autres Etats membres de l’ONU, et ce, pour plusieurs raisons. Premièrement , cette résolution de la Quatrième Commission confirme la résolution historique 2797 du Conseil de Sécurité, qui a consacré l’Initiative Marocaine d’Autonomie comme base dans le cadre de la souveraineté marocaine. Cette même résolution réaffirme la responsabilité des quatre parties, le Maroc, l’Algérie, la Mauritanie et le « polisario », et les appelle à s’engager de bonne foi dans le processus politique. La référence à la résolution 2797 revêt une importance particulière, parce que son adoption, le 31 octobre 2025, était intervenue après l’examen annuel de la question du Sahara Marocain par la Quatrième Commission, permettant ainsi, pour la première fois, sa prise en compte dans la résolution qui vient d’être adoptée ce matin. Deuxièmement , cette résolution est identique à celles adoptées depuis vingt ans. Elle n’apporte aucun élément nouveau, à l’exception de l’importante référence à la résolution 2797 du Conseil de Sécurité. Troisièmement , cette résolution soutient le processus politique mené par l’Envoyé personnel du Secrétaire général des Nations Unies, sous les auspices de ce dernier, en vue de parvenir à une solution politique réaliste, pragmatique, durable et mutuellement acceptable, conformément aux résolutions pertinentes du Conseil de Sécurité, notamment ses quatre dernières résolutions, telles que rappelées dans le rapport du Secrétaire général. Quatrièmement , cette résolution réitère ses « félicitations de ce que les parties se sont engagées à continuer de faire preuve de volonté politique et de travailler dans une atmosphère propice au dialogue afin d’entrer, de bonne foi et sans conditions préalables, dans une phase de négociation plus intensive, en prenant note des efforts consentis et des faits nouveaux survenus depuis 2006 ». Ce qui implique, particulièrement, les faits nouveaux et inédits, en l’occurrence l’adoption de la résolution 2797 et la tenue de trois rounds de négociations à Washington et Madrid, durant lesquelles le Maroc a présenté le statut développé de l’Autonomie. Cinquièmement , cette résolution ne préjuge en rien du statut du Sahara, dès lors qu’elle soutient la dynamique politique impulsée par le Conseil de Sécurité dans le cadre du Chapitre VI de la Charte des Nations Unies, qui inscrit la question du Sahara Marocain dans une logique de paix et de sécurité internationales, devant être réglée par le dialogue et la négociation. The post ONU : la Quatrième Commission adopte la résolution sur le Sahara marocain appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Unchecked imports and the Middle East crisis threaten Ghana’s fragile food inflation anchor
items.description: The Middle East crisis has significantly affected global fuel and other import prices. Between March and September this year, headline inflation increased by two percentage points, while aggregate food inflation rose by 1.7 percentage points. These figures suggest that the managers of the Ghanaian economy are on the right path toward price stabilisation. Indeed, the economic management team has been heavily leveraging the USD/GHS exchange rate as a transmission mechanism to maintain this stability. However, if the Middle East crisis is prolonged for several months, and if Brent crude and refined petroleum product prices, especially, remain high, this stabilising trend can be expected to reverse. Consequently, Ghanaians must prepare for another prolonged episode of sharp currency depreciation, similar to what was witnessed at the onset of the Russia-Ukraine war, which would inevitably cause huge spikes in aggregate food inflation. As a specialist in Applied Econometrics and Agribusiness, I have spent a considerable amount of time assessing these potential inflationary pressures on local food prices since the escalation of the US-Israel-Iran conflict. Food inflation volatility Over the past three decades, Ghana’s food market has become highly volatile. Observation of Ghana’s food inflation data spanning this period has revealed very interesting facts. Food inflation is averaging around 8.9% over the long run, with a baseline volatility of 4.9%. Food inflation has gathered strong momentum in recent decades; a high inflation rate in one month heavily influences a high inflation rate the next. I also observe that random monthly economic shocks have a lingering effect on the immediate subsequent period, and seasonality no longer significantly affects food inflation. Approximately 18.24% of a given month’s unexpected inflation shock is instantly carried over as increased uncertainty and price volatility the following month. Furthermore, about 81.65% of the previous month’s volatility carries over directly into the current month. Ultimately, these volatility shocks are highly persistent and dissipate very slowly over time. Seasonality in the food market The nation experienced major price shocks in 2001 and 2023, with a long period of stability between the two crisis periods. The historical food inflation hike in 2001 (76.8%) was significantly higher than the recent spike in 2023 (61%). During December, September, February, November, October, January, and June, food prices are slightly higher than the yearly average. Conversely, during August, April, May, March, and July, food prices are slightly lower than the yearly average. The month of December typically pushes food inflation up by approximately 0.26 percentage points, while the month of August pushes it down by approximately 0.20 percentage points. Evidence of a new food inflation regime Ghana’s food markets may be experiencing a new inflation regime-or what economists call a structural break. Since 1999, Ghana’s food inflation has experienced two unexpected, permanent shifts: first in 2004 and again in 2022. External shocks and macroeconomic policy interventions triggered both shifts, creating three distinct eras of food inflation between 1999 and 2026. The first regime lasted 65 months (January 1999 to May 2004), the second spanned 213 months (June 2004 to February 2022), and the most recent regime began in March 2022. This observation is critical for agricultural policy, as interventions that rely on outdated relationships will likely fail if they do not account for these structural breaks. Impact of fuel prices on food inflation Historically, Ghana’s food inflation has experienced a nuanced relationship with key variables like energy and the exchange rate. In the short term, food prices in the country shoot up rapidly like a rocket when ex-pump diesel prices rise, but drift down slowly like a feather when fuel prices drop. For instance, within the same month, a 1 GHS spike in diesel prices triggers an aggressive pass-through, increasing food inflation by 1.67 percentage points. Conversely, a 1 GHS decrease in diesel prices results in a much weaker downward movement, dropping insignificantly by only 0.46 percentage points. Similar to diesel, whenever petrol prices go up, food inflation shoots up like a rocket. Within the same month, a 1 GHS increase in petrol prices can trigger a surge of 1.41 percentage points in food inflation- representing an immediate, aggressive pass-through. Conversely, when petrol prices drop, food inflation drifts down slowly and invisibly like a feather. This downward pass-through of 0.27 percentage points is so weak and uncertain that it is statistically insignificant, confirming that market vendors in Ghana rarely lower food prices when fuel becomes cheaper. Additionally, the data show strong inflation inertia: a 1 percentage point increase in the previous month’s food inflation automatically carries over to increase the current month’s inflation by 0.49 percentage points. Micro-level evidence of erosion of cocoa farmer purchasing power To demonstrate how recent upticks in month-to-month inflation manifest on the ground, one can look at its direct impact on the purchasing power of cocoa farmers—a critical source of Ghana’s foreign exchange earnings. In July 2026, an initial assessment indicated that the government needed to adjust the cocoa producer price upward by approximately GHS 1,000 to compensate for severe purchasing power losses recorded in the first half of the year. Although this adjustment has recently been implemented, its arrival may be too late to shield farmers from the fresh wave of inflation triggered by ongoing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. When the government reduced the producer price in February 2026 from GHS 58,000 to GHS 41,392 per tonne, farmers suffered an immediate 29% loss in purchasing power relative to the January baseline. Subsequently, purchasing power eroded by an additional 1.38% leading up to the recent policy intervention, which raised the price by GHS 1,008 per tonne. While this upward adjustment marginally improves cocoa farmers’ purchasing power by roughly 2% relative to the February 2026 price, it falls short of compensating for the steep losses sustained since January. Crucially, this modest 2% gain remains highly fragile and could be swiftly eroded by mounting inflationary pressures from expensive crude oil and refined petroleum products. Exchange rate stability: the fragile anchor During this period of global oil price shocks, the Bank of Ghana and the Ministry of Finance are heavily leveraging the USD/GHS exchange rate as a transmission mechanism to stabilise ex-pump fuel prices. Whether this coordinated approach is largely driven by monetary or fiscal policy, it appears to be working effectively to tackle food inflationary pressures from the crisis. However, high Brent crude oil prices inevitably exert severe currency pressures, which could trigger sustained spikes in food inflation. If Brent crude and refined petroleum products remain expensive, they will automatically trigger a sustained scramble for US dollars in the forex market. Consequently, the country must prepare for another prolonged episode of sharp currency depreciation, similar to what was witnessed at the onset of the Russia-Ukraine war. Historically, Ghana has been heavily dependent on imports of crude oil and refined petroleum products, meat, rice, among others. Therefore, if the country does not curb the imports it can control and better allocate its scarce forex reserves, history may repeat itself. For example, let us look at meat imports into the country. I estimated two composite index trading models to track the historical performance of Ghana’s meat imports and local production using official figures from MoFA. I observe that Ghana’s frozen meat imports composite index for the period 2020 to 2024 shows a sharp rise of 5,600 basis points (56% growth rate), with poultry alone weighing 87%. By comparison, my performance tracking index for local meat production rose slowly by 2,900 basis points (29% growth rate) for the period 2015 to 2024. So, we can expect that the Agriculture Minister has a lot to do to reverse the heavy reliance on imports in order to reduce the pressures on the currency. The price of Brent crude oil exerts direct and significant pressure on the Ghanaian Cedi (GHS) against the US Dollar (USD). An analysis of Ghana Statistical Service (GSS) and Bank of Ghana (BoG) data spanning the July 2015 to June 2024 sample window yielded an interesting observation. It can be expected that changes in global oil prices will take nearly five months to pass through to the local foreign exchange market. Specifically, across the full sample period, the Cedi-USD exchange rate exhibits a significant response, depreciating by GHS 0.16 for every $1 hike in the Brent crude price. The structural relationship between global oil prices and the Ghanaian Cedi has fundamentally shifted over the last few years, driven by global crises and macroeconomic policy changes. For instance, the May 2021 global oil price spike triggered a massive chain reaction that severely fractured the Cedi’s stability between March 2021 and November 2022. Should the escalating crisis in the Middle East continue to drive crude prices upward, the fragile exchange rate stability Ghana has recently achieved could rapidly erode. This vulnerability threatens to plunge the economy back into a painful cycle of currency depreciation and prolonged food inflation. To insulate the nation during this crisis period, the government must aggressively curb non-essential imports and optimise the allocation of our scarce foreign exchange reserves. AUTHORED BY DR. Dans un discours prononcé lors d’une réception organisée par l’ambassade d’Espagne à Nouakchott à l’occasion de la fête nationale espagnole, l’ambassadeur a précisé que la coopération entre la Mauritanie et l’Espagne couvre de nombreux secteurs, notamment le développement, l’agriculture, la santé et le secteur maritime, ainsi que la coopération économique, commerciale et en matière d’investissement. Il a indiqué que les deux pays s’emploient à renforcer leur partenariat et à mettre en œuvre la feuille de route issue de la réunion de haut niveau entre leurs gouvernements, qui s’est tenue à Nouakchott le 16 juillet 2025, afin de favoriser l’élargissement des domaines de coopération bilatérale. Il a également souligné l’importance de développer le partenariat entre la Mauritanie et l’Union européenne et de l’élever à un niveau stratégique et global, saluant le rôle joué par la Mauritanie dans le renforcement de la stabilité régionale et la lutte contre l’immigration clandestine et la traite des êtres humains. L’ambassadeur a réaffirmé la solidité des relations entre Nouakchott et Madrid, en s’appuyant sur les liens historiques et les intérêts communs qui unissent les deux pays, dans le cadre d’une volonté d’élargir la coopération dans les domaines prioritaires pour les deux parties.

items.title: 2027 Presidency: It’s too late for Atiku, others to upset Tinubu
items.description: By Soni Daniel, Editor Northern Region It is too late for former Vice President, Atiku Abubakar and the other opposition figures in Nigeria to team up and upset President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in next year’s election, Otunba Segun Showunmi, a member of the Communication and Strategy Committee of the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council, has said. Showunmi, who was named to the council by President Tinubu early this week, said that Atiku and his political allies wasted time in coming together to plan how they could defeat President Tinubu, adding that the current attempt to coalesce into a force against Tinubu was an exercise in futility. Showunmi, who described himself as a card-carrying member of the People’s Democratic Party, said that he was convinced that Atiku and other opposition party would lose the forthcoming presidential election, but asked them to accept the result in good faith. He said: “Atiku’s condition is already late because they are merely chasing shadows and the truth is that they cannot work together with a view to mustering the capacity to defeat President Bola Tinubu in the forthcoming election. “But they should be wise to accept the results as announced by the INEC because if they attempt to rig the election or cause problems they would be charged for treason and punished according to the laws of the land. On the decision by President Tinubu not to be physically present at all campaign locations, Showunmi justified it, saying that there was no need for the president to leave the serious business of governance for campaign. Showunmi pointed out that the president had already made himself acceptable to Nigerians and does not need further physical engagement in order to win the election. “President Tinubu does not need further introduction in order to defeat Atiku and the rest because he has already done enough to deserve the support and goodwill of most Nigerians. The former PDP governorship candidate in Ogun pointed out that Tinubu had won the hearts of Nigerians by withdrawing the fuel subsidy in order to make more money for state and local government development more than any other administration. Showunmi said that only uneducated Nigerians would dare to complain about the withdrawal of fuel subsidy by President Tinubu, arguing that even the ADC presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, had always wanted to remove fuel subsidy before now. “No educated Nigerian would oppose what President Bola Tinubu has done on fuel subsidy. It is only people who do not mean well that would kick against it,” the campaign council member insisted. He also listed the establishment of six regional development commission to facilitate the transformation of Nigeria and the improvement of security, which has resulted in quick release of captured Nigerians as some of the achievements of the Tinubu administration. “We have all seen that Tinubu has brought the nation together by settling all the regions as our founding fathers had wanted and this is a big achievement,” he said. items.title: Ecobank Junior Saver Big Pitch to reward 10 winners with GH¢2,000 each
items.description: Ecobank Ghana Limited is set to reward 10 winners with GH¢2,000 each under its Junior Saver Big Pitch initiative, which encourages children to share their future ambitions while promoting early savings and financial planning. Head of Retail Banking, Consumer and Commercial Banking at Ecobank Ghana, Yaa Kesewaa Nyanor, said the initiative was designed to make saving more engaging by giving children an active role in planning for their future, rather than leaving the responsibility entirely to their parents. Speaking on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show, she said the Big Pitch would allow children to express their dreams creatively, while parents support them financially and help them understand the steps needed to achieve their goals. “For those who will win, Ecobank is going to credit their accounts with GH₵2,000 each,” she said, adding that the bank was initially looking at 10 winners. Ms Nyanor said what set the Junior Saver Big Pitch apart from other savings initiatives was the direct involvement of children in explaining their ambitions and how they hoped to achieve them. She explained that the initiative was intended to give children an opportunity to demonstrate their creativity and communicate their dreams, while encouraging parents to take a more active role in planning for their future. “It’s not just the parents saving for the child. Now the child is telling us his big dream or her big dream.” According to her, parents often speak proudly about their children’s intelligence and abilities, but the Big Pitch offers an opportunity for children to demonstrate those qualities themselves. “When you go to work, they are telling us how intelligent their children are. This is the time. We want the child to come out there and show us how intelligent the child is,” she said. She added that the initiative would make saving more exciting by allowing children to participate in decisions about their future, rather than simply being recipients of money saved on their behalf. Ms Nyanor said parents would not need to take their children to a bank branch to participate. Instead, they would record videos of their children explaining what they wanted to become and the steps they believed were necessary to achieve their ambitions. A child who wanted to become a seamstress, for instance, could explain why they had chosen that career, what they hoped to achieve and the support they would need. The bank is encouraging parents to allow children to express themselves creatively, rather than impose a particular format on their presentations. “We want the child to be creative. So we leave the creativity to the child and the parents,” she said. Ms Nyanor said the exercise was also expected to strengthen the relationship between parents and children by creating opportunities for conversations about their future. “This period is going to bond the parents and the children. And it’s also going to help the parents think about their future with their children,” she added. Ms Nyanor outlined two main steps for parents who wish to take part in the campaign. The first is to open an Ecobank Junior Saver account for the child and make a deposit. The second is to record a video of the child explaining their future ambitions and how they hope to achieve them. She said a child who wanted to become a doctor, for example, could talk about why they had chosen the profession, what they knew about it and the journey towards becoming a doctor. Parents are then expected to post the videos on their social media accounts and tag Ecobank, using the relevant campaign hashtags. Ms Nyanor stressed the importance of including the correct tags so the bank could identify entries submitted for the initiative. Parents must tag Ecobank and use the hashtags #EcobankJuniorSaver and #EcobankBigPitch when sharing their videos. She said the campaign would give children an opportunity to share their ambitions with a wider audience, potentially exposing them to opportunities beyond their immediate families. “Your child gets to tell the world about what they want to do,” she said. Ms Nyanor encouraged parents to begin saving for their children even if they could not afford to deposit large amounts, saying the process could start with as little as GH¢50. “Many parents think that you have to put in a huge amount, but you can start with just 50 cedis,” she said. She added that parents should make regular weekly or monthly deposits rather than open an account and leave it without further contributions. One option, she said, was to set up a standing order to transfer money regularly from the parent’s account to the child’s account. She explained that parents did not necessarily need to bank with Ecobank to open a Junior Saver account for their children. They could also arrange deposits from an account held with another bank or transfer money from a mobile money account. Ms Nyanor said regular contributions could help families build savings over time and prepare for future expenses, including education and other important milestones. She encouraged parents to begin early so they would be better prepared to meet their children’s needs as they grew older. “It’s a very nice initiative so that, by the time the child is old, you don’t have to start looking for money,” she said.

items.title: AMA demolishes unauthorised pigsty obstructing Agbogbloshie waste evacuation exercise
items.description: The Accra Metropolitan Assembly (AMA) has demolished an unauthorised pigsty at Agbogbloshie after its operators failed to comply with a final warning to remove the structure obstructing the ongoing National Emergency Waste Evacuation Exercise. The demolition was intended to clear access for heavy-duty equipment and personnel engaged in removing accumulated waste from the area as part of efforts to restore environmental cleanliness. The Assembly said the enforcement action followed a final warning issued on Thursday, October 8, 2026, when the Mayor of Accra, Michael Kpakpo Allotey, and the Metropolitan Coordinating Director, Douglas N.K. Annoful, led officials to inspect the ongoing waste evacuation exercise. Speaking after the demolition, Mr Allotey said the operators had been given an opportunity to remove the structure but failed to comply, leaving the Assembly with no option but to take enforcement action. He disclosed that the pigsty had been established and operated without the requisite permit or approval from the AMA, in violation of the Assembly’s by-laws governing animal-rearing activities within the metropolis. The Mayor cited the AMA’s Control of Animals By-law, 2017, which prohibits the keeping of swine, cattle, sheep, goats and other specified animals within the Assembly’s jurisdiction without a permit. He said the regulations were intended to control animal-rearing activities, protect public health, prevent environmental nuisances and ensure that livestock were kept under appropriate sanitary conditions. Mr Allotey stressed that the waste evacuation exercise required unrestricted access for payloaders, excavators, tipper trucks and other heavy-duty machinery deployed to collect and transport accumulated waste from Agbogbloshie. He reiterated that individuals seeking to engage in livestock farming or other commercial activities within the metropolis must obtain the necessary permits and operate only in locations approved by the relevant authorities. The Mayor also cautioned residents and business operators against erecting unauthorised structures or undertaking activities that obstruct public access, disrupt sanitation operations or undermine development interventions. He reaffirmed the Assembly’s commitment to enforcing its by-laws and supporting the National Emergency Waste Evacuation Exercise to restore environmental cleanliness, improve public health and promote orderliness across the metropolis.

items.title: I was filled with disbelief – Akosua Achia Sarpong Esq. shares her first reaction
items.description: The 2026 Overall Best Law Student of the Ghana School of Law, Akosua Achia Sarpong, Esq., has shared her initial reaction to being named the overall best student in her cohort. In an interview with Nikki Samonas on Joy Prime’s Changes show, she revealed that she had never envisioned herself emerging as the overall best student, although she had hoped to win an award in a specific course category. Having witnessed the intelligence of her colleagues throughout their studies at the school, she believes that everyone deserved the award, making her victory a favour from God. During the conversation, Nikki asked, “How did you feel when your name was mentioned?” “I was in so much disbelieve and I was also very excited and also very grateful to God. I just kept looking back at the journey; the late nights, all the intensive studying and I was just really so grateful to God because I believe that everybody that has been called to the Bar learnt well. So for me to have come out as the best, I just know it was the special work of God. I was just too grateful,” she responded. She added that she had doubted her ability to achieve such a milestone, considering that she was not the valedictorian of her cohort at Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), yet she found herself in law school among students who had achieved such distinctions. “There are a lot of brilliant minds and intelligent people in KNUST and in the legal profession; and in my time at KNUST, I wasn’t valedictorian. I mean I was part of the top 10 but I wasn’t valedictorian so looking at all those brilliant and intelligent people, I just was not imagining myself being the best of them all.” Although she experienced moments of doubt, the thought of giving up never crossed her mind. According to her, the strong support she received from her family back home motivated and strengthened her to study harder. Speaking about competition, the lawyer said she never viewed any of her colleagues or friends as competitors, as she believes collaboration and togetherness are key to achieving excellence in the study of law. She explained that group studies played an important role in her academic journey, helping her and her colleagues gain a better understanding of the subject. She added that she believes in achieving success together. “I know that the legal profession isn’t really one where you have to compete with people. It’s more like you have to corporate and then collaborate. So competition isn’t really something that I felt or something that I think came up. It was more like let’s all corporate and get called to the Bar successfully because truthfully, if you compete with your colleagues and get called to the Bar alone, it’s not nice,” she said. Akosua Achiaa Sarpong, a graduate of the KNUST Faculty of Law, was named the overall best student at the 63rd Call to the Bar. She won the John Mensah Sarbah Award for the best all-round performance in the Professional Law Examinations, as well as the prize for Best Student in Civil Procedure. Her achievement marks the 11th time a graduate of the KNUST Faculty of Law has won the Sarbah Award since 2011. It is also the fourth consecutive year that a KNUST law graduate has received the award, following wins in 2023, 2024 and 2025.

items.title: NAFDAC seizes N200m fake drink packaging in Aba
items.description: By Chioma Obinna The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control, NAFDAC, has seized counterfeit packaging materials valued at more than ₦200 million from five shops at Old Court Road Market, Aba, Abia State, during an enforcement operation targeting the alleged production of fake alcoholic drinks and other regulated products. The agency said the materials included counterfeit labels, corks and outer packaging bearing the names of popular international and local brands, raising concerns about the possible circulation of fake wines, spirits and other consumer products. In a statement issued on Thursday, October 15, by its Deputy Director and Head of Public Relations, Christiana Obiazikwor, NAFDAC said its Investigation and Enforcement Directorate carried out the operation following credible intelligence. The agency described the market as a major centre for the alleged production of counterfeit packaging materials for branded spirits, wines and other regulated products. Brands whose packaging materials were reportedly recovered included Jameson, Glenfiddich, Four Cousins, Lord’s Dry Gin, Imperial Blue, Goya Oil, Chelsea, Squadron and Seaman’s Aromatic Schnapps. NAFDAC said its operatives encountered stiff resistance from traders during the operation, including threats and attempts to intimidate them. “The operation was met with stiff resistance, threats and violent disposition from traders,” the statement said. The agency added that some traders pursued the vehicle conveying the seized materials and threatened people who volunteered to assist with loading the items. “Despite the intimidation and incisive utterances, the resilience and boldness of the I&E operatives ensured the evacuation of as much contraband as possible,” NAFDAC said. According to the agency, the owners of the five shops visited fled during the operation, while the affected premises were placed on hold and the suspected counterfeit packaging materials evacuated. NAFDAC said investigations were ongoing to identify and apprehend those allegedly behind the counterfeiting operation. The agency did not disclose whether any arrests had been made or provide details of the suspected shop owners. The seizure comes amid concerns over the circulation of counterfeit alcoholic beverages and other regulated products, which may expose consumers to potentially unsafe substances and make it difficult to verify the authenticity and contents of products sold under established brand names. items.title: Ogun Gov Poll: Lawyers petition INEC over omission of PDP candidate
items.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA — Lawyers representing the candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) for the 2027 governorship election in Ogun State, Mr. Topa Olusegun Peter, have petitioned the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) over the omission of his name from the final list of candidates. In the letter dated October 14 and addressed to the Chairman of INEC, Prof. Joash Amupitan, SAN, Peter’s legal team, led by Mr. Anderson Asemota, said his name was omitted from the list INEC published on October 10, even though the party had earlier forwarded his nomination particulars in accordance with Section 77 of the Electoral Act, 2026. Insisting that the omission has immediate and serious consequences, the petitioners vowed to proceed to court should the electoral body fail, within 48 hours, to provide a substantive response or restore his name as a candidate for the governorship poll scheduled for February 6. “It is our Client’s case that he duly participated in the party’s primary, and the party forwarded his nomination particulars to the Commission in accordance with the Act. “He further states that his name appears at entry No. 15783 on the PDP membership register submitted to the Commission in compliance with Section 77 of the Electoral Act, 2026. “That on 10th October 2026, INEC published the Final List of candidates for the Governorship election, wherein it failed, refused and/or neglected to publish any name for the Peoples Democratic Party in Ogun State. “Surprisingly, our Client’s name was omitted. So far as our Client is aware, he has not been furnished with written reasons for the omission, nor has he been notified of any objection or afforded an opportunity to respond to any concern relied upon by the Commission. “The omission has immediate and serious consequences. It prevents the public from seeing our Client identified on the official list as the candidate he says was nominated by the PDP, and creates uncertainty for the party, its supporters and the electorate. “The matter therefore requires prompt attention and a reasoned response,” the letter added. Stressing that Section 77(4)–(6) of the Electoral Act, 2026 regulates the submission and use of political party membership registers, the petitioners urged INEC to verify whether their client was on the register submitted to it by the PDP, as well as whether the applicable statutory requirements were met. “We acknowledge the Supreme Court decision identified as INEC v. Zenith Labour Party, SC/CV/495/2026, delivered on 24th September 2026, concerning Sections 77(5), (6) and (7) and Section 84(2) of the Act. “Our Client does not invite the Commission to disregard that decision. Rather, the Commission is requested to apply the provisions, as authoritatively interpreted by the Supreme Court, to the actual facts and records relating to the PDP and our Client. “In particular, the Commission should verify whether our Client’s name was on the register submitted by the PDP, whether the applicable statutory requirements were met, and whether any order of a court or other lawful basis exists for the omission. “The legal consequences of any established noncompliance must be those prescribed by the Act and the binding judicial authorities; they should not be extended by administrative assumption beyond their proper scope. “The principles discussed in Ugwu v. Ararume (2007) 12 NWLR (Pt. 1048) 367 and Amaechi v. INEC (2008) 5 NWLR (Pt. 1080) 227 underscore the importance of giving effect to lawful party nomination processes and of ensuring that electoral authorities act within the law. “The Commission is invited to consider those authorities alongside the applicable provisions of the Electoral Act, 2026 and any subsequent binding decision directly relevant to the present facts. “In the circumstances, we hereby formally request that the Commission, within forty-eight (48) hours of receipt of this letter, verify the PDP membership-register entry relied upon by our Client, together with the primary-election and nomination records in the Commission’s custody; “Where the Commission’s records confirm that our Client was duly nominated and no lawful basis exists for excluding him, promptly correct the published list by issuing and displaying a supplementary or amended list containing the name of Mr. Topa Olusegun Peter as the gubernatorial candidate of the PDP in Ogun State, and publish the correction on its website in the manner required by the Act; and confirm in writing, within the same forty-eight (48) hour period, the steps taken and the outcome of the Commission’s review. “This letter is written without prejudice to our Client’s rights and remedies. If the Commission fails to provide a substantive response within forty-eight hours of receipt, or if the omission persists without a lawful and adequately explained basis, our Client has instructed us to consider instituting appropriate proceedings before a court of competent jurisdiction, seeking such declaratory, mandatory and consequential reliefs as may be available on the facts and in law, together with costs. “For the avoidance of doubt, we do not ask the Commission to usurp the adjudicatory function of the court. “We ask it to review the relevant records and perform its statutory functions lawfully. Any issue reserved by law for judicial determination may be placed before a court of competent jurisdiction. “In view of the documentary basis asserted by our Client and the statutory framework governing membership registers, primaries, nomination and publication, we urge the Commission to treat this matter as urgent, conduct the necessary verification without delay, and take the corrective action required by law,” the letter further read. items.title: Le Fmi affiche son optimisme
items.description: Ce 14 octobre 2026, lors des Assemblées annuelles du Fmi et de la Banque mondiale à Bangkok, Kristalina Georgieva s'est montrée optimiste quant aux négociations sur la dette du Sénégal tout en précisant que le lieu de l'événement et certains détails géographiques ou organisationnels nécessitent des rectifications. Les négociations entre le Sénégal et le Fonds monétaire international se sont invitées à Bangkok où se tiennent les Assemblées annuelles de la Banque mondiale et du Fmi. Dans une vidéo, la directrice générale du Fmi, Kristalina Georgieva, a affiché son optimisme quant à l’aboutissement rapide des pourparlers. Elle s'est dite confiante à la capacité de Dakar à trouver un accord avec ses créanciers. À son avis, le Sénégal pourrait démontrer que les procédures internationales de traitement de la dette sont devenues plus efficaces. Mme Georgieva fait ainsi allusion au Cadre commun du G20 lancé en 2020 pour coordonner le Plan de traitement de la dette (Ptds). D’ailleurs, c’est le Fmi qui a joué les bons offices le 6 octobre dernier, lors du premier rendez-vous entre Dakar et ses créanciers. Cette entrevue avait permis aux autorités de faire le point auprès des créanciers extérieurs sur la situation économique et financière du Sénégal, le programme de réformes économiques et la stratégie de traitement de la dette. Le plan d'engagement auprès des créanciers, le calendrier et les prochaines étapes en font également partie. Par ailleurs, les services du FMI ont présenté les grandes lignes de l'accord conclu au niveau des services avec les autorités sénégalaises. Cet accord concerne une nouvelle Facilité élargie de crédit (Fec) ainsi que les éléments pertinents des politiques et cadres de prêt. Cette rencontre avec les investisseurs entre dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre du Plan de traitement de la dette du Sénégal (Ptds). Une stratégie qui constitue une réponse adaptée aux caractéristiques de la dette du Sénégal. Face à ses créanciers, le gouvernement, représenté par le directeur général des Financements et de la dette, Babacar Touré, avait exprimé son souhait de poursuivre le traitement de sa dette conformément aux principes du Cadre commun du G20 tout en cherchant à tirer les enseignements et à relever les défis identifiés lors de cas précédents. Les engagements dans ce sens concernent le suivi d'un calendrier accéléré et prévisible pour le traitement de leurs créances, sans oublier la clarification rapide des éléments clés qui sous-tendent le Ptds, y compris l'évaluation des contributions. Dans le cadre des négociations, le Sénégal prend novembre 2026 comme délai cible pour l'aboutissement des différents cadres du partenariat avec le Fmi. Cela devra se matérialiser par l'approbation du programme par le Conseil d'administration. Dans cette optique, une réunion se tiendra au cours du mois de novembre. En décembre, l'État prévoit de signer des accords de principe avec les Comités des créanciers officiels (Occ) et le groupe ad hoc des détenteurs d'obligations. Ensuite, le Sénégal procédera, en début 2027, à la mise en œuvre des accords. Le Sénégal mise sur le Ptds pour rendre viable sa dette. Il devrait permettre de restaurer durablement le profil de la dette publique, ramener le poids du service de la dette sur le budget de l'État aux normes admises en la matière et dégager progressivement les marges de manœuvre nécessaires au financement des investissements publics dans les secteurs prioritaires, principalement les secteurs sociaux. Le stock de la dette extérieure du Sénégal est de 18.300 milliards de FCfa dont 8.500 milliards dus aux banques de développement. La dette commerciale s'élève à 5.440 milliards de FCfa et celle bilatérale à 4.369 milliards. Demba DIENG

items.title: Election Watch Ghana calls for constitutional reforms to strengthen Electoral Commission independence
items.description: Election Watch Ghana has congratulated Dr Joseph Kwaku Asamoah and Emelia Afi Agbenyo on their appointment and inauguration as Deputy Chairpersons of the Electoral Commission (EC) of Ghana, while calling for constitutional reforms to strengthen the Commission’s independence, credibility and public confidence. In a statement issued on Wednesday, October 14, the organisation wished the two officials success in their new roles, emphasising the importance of institutional independence, technological innovation and public trust to Ghana’s democratic development. It also commended the President for promoting women’s representation in leadership and national decision-making, noting that inclusive governance creates opportunities for capable individuals to contribute meaningfully to national development. However, Election Watch Ghana stressed the need to review the constitutional and legal framework governing appointments to the EC, arguing that recurring public concerns about the actual or perceived political affiliations of appointees make a transparent, merit-based and broadly consultative process essential. The organisation called on the President, Parliament, political parties, civil society organisations and other stakeholders to support reforms that would strengthen the Commission’s impartiality and independence. It noted that political affiliation alone does not determine an individual’s ability to serve fairly, but maintained that the appointment process must inspire public confidence and minimise perceptions of partisan influence. On electoral technology, Election Watch Ghana said credible elections require more than administrative experience, highlighting the growing importance of information technology, cybersecurity, election operations and digital systems management. Although it would have welcomed greater emphasis on demonstrable expertise in these areas during the selection process, the organisation encouraged the new Deputy Chairpersons to pursue professional development, including specialised training and certifications in election technology, database management, electronic results management, data integrity and cybersecurity. It further urged the EC to subject its electoral technologies to rigorous testing and appropriate independent audits, with safeguards against errors, manipulation, cyberattacks and unauthorised access. These measures, it said, would help ensure that election results remain secure, transparent and verifiable. Election Watch Ghana also urged the new appointees to discharge their responsibilities without fear, favour or political interference, stressing that their primary allegiance must be to the Constitution, electoral laws and the Ghanaian people. The organisation encouraged constructive engagement with political parties, civil society groups, election observers, the media and voters, while maintaining the Commission’s independence and ensuring that every eligible Ghanaian can participate in elections and every valid vote is accurately counted. It concluded that the Deputy Chairpersons’ legacy would depend on their integrity, willingness to learn and ability to improve the Commission’s operations, reiterating its congratulations and wishing them wisdom, courage and success in their new responsibilities.

items.title: Umahi reopens First Niger Bridge adorned with Tinubu’s pictures
items.description: By Chimaobi Nwaiwu The Minister of Works, David Umahi, on Thursday reopened the First Niger Bridge linking Onitsha, Anambra State, with Asaba, Delta State, following rehabilitation works, with photographs of President Bola Tinubu and other political figures displayed on the bridge. The bridge, built in 1965, was closed to traffic on September 7, 2026, for emergency rehabilitation and maintenance initially scheduled to end on September 21. The closure was extended beyond the original deadline following persistent rainfall and other unforeseen circumstances that delayed the work. The rehabilitation followed the discovery of vandalised structural components, including steelwork around the bridge’s expansion joints. At the reopening, Umahi praised Tinubu’s administration for what he described as its commitment to infrastructure development in the South-East and South-South regions. He said the attention being given to the Third Mainland Bridge in Lagos was similar to the rehabilitation and maintenance work being carried out on the Second Niger Bridge and other major bridges across the country. According to the minister, the South-East and South-South would also benefit from the administration’s infrastructure projects. Umahi, who intermittently sang “On Your Mandate We Shall Stand” during his address, also criticised Labour Party’s 2023 presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and the Obidient Movement, while expressing confidence in the All Progressives Congress, APC, ahead of the 2027 elections. “I am not into regional politics; I am following who is performing. Can anybody give us the alternative to Tinubu, President Tinubu, who has salvaged the country from a catastrophic situation? Can Peter Obi do what Tinubu is doing?” he asked. He said the projects being executed by the Federal Government would soon be extended to other parts of Anambra State. “The President has approved the dualisation of Oba-Okigwe Expressway. Why are people not seeing all these? Democracy is about development and infrastructure. We are here to demonstrate that the South-East is for President Tinubu,” Umahi said. The minister acknowledged that the South-East had not voted massively for Tinubu in the 2023 presidential election, attributing the outcome to what he described as the poor treatment of the region under the administration of former President Muhammadu Buhari. He, however, expressed confidence that the region would support Tinubu in 2027. Umahi also said no individual or group had the right to erect billboards on federal highways without the necessary authorisation. “No one has the right to put billboards on the federal highways. Tell Peter Obi and the Obidient Movement that if they pay, they will be allowed to put their billboards on the highways,” he said. The bridge reopening was marked by the display of photographs of Tinubu, Vice-President Kashim Shettima and Anambra State Governor Chukwuma Soludo, alongside APC banners placed on the bridge railings. Some sections of the railings had been repainted, while painters were still carrying out finishing touches. The road markings had also been repainted, and closed-circuit television cameras installed at various sections of the bridge, alongside other infrastructure components. Umahi had, during an earlier inspection, directed that illegal advertisements be removed from the bridge and that Tinubu’s photographs be displayed following completion of the rehabilitation. He had said the display was intended to recognise what he described as the President’s contributions to infrastructure development in the South-East. The post Umahi reopens First Niger Bridge adorned with Tinubu’s pictures appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: NACOC, Postal and Courier Services Regulatory Commission intensify efforts to curb drug trafficking
items.description: The Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC) has strengthened its collaboration with the Postal and Courier Services Regulatory Commission to prevent illicit drug trafficking through Ghana’s postal and courier services. The renewed partnership is aimed at tightening security within the sector, improving the detection of illicit drugs in parcels and supporting efforts to make Ghana a drug-free society. NACOC Director-General Major General Maxwell Obuba Mantey gave the assurance when the Acting Executive Secretary of the Postal and Courier Services Regulatory Commission, Cosmas Anpengnuo, and members of his management team paid a working visit to him on Tuesday, October 13, 2026. Major General Mantey reaffirmed NACOC’s commitment to working with relevant stakeholders to combat drug trafficking, assuring the delegation of technical, training and intelligence-gathering support to strengthen the Commission’s operations. “NACOC is ever ready to provide strategic support to the Postal and Courier Services Regulatory Commission in diverse ways, mainly to enable it achieve its goals. The support would be directed in the form of technical, training and intelligence gathering,” he said. He welcomed the Commission’s proposed move to ensure that courier and postal service providers conduct background checks on their employees, saying the exercise would help companies establish the backgrounds of their staff. The NACOC Director-General also expressed concern about the growing use of digital platforms to facilitate drug trafficking, noting that some courier and postal service providers were being exploited by traffickers. He said the renewed collaboration was timely, stressing that drug trafficking networks involved multiple connections and required a coordinated, professional response. Major General Mantey urged the Commission to strengthen its operational measures, particularly the enforcement of parcel verification procedures, to help prevent illicit drugs from passing through the courier and postal system and protect service providers from the consequences of trafficking-related incidents. For his part, Mr Anpengnuo commended NACOC for its support and collaboration in the fight against illicit drug trafficking. He said the Commission had enhanced its traceability mechanisms as part of efforts to improve oversight of courier and postal service providers. He also highlighted the introduction of an application programming interface (API) integration platform, to which all companies had been linked, saying it had improved the Commission’s monitoring of the sector. Mr Anpengnuo stressed that courier and postal service providers that failed to comply with the API integration system would not have their licences approved or renewed. According to him, the platform had strengthened the Commission’s monitoring and control mechanisms by enabling it to track the parties involved in deliveries handled by service providers each day. He assured NACOC of the Commission’s continued partnership and support to eliminate drug trafficking through Ghana’s postal and courier service points.

items.title: Ga Mantse chairs committee to drive Accra Green and Clean City Initiative
items.description: The Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Mahama Ayariga, has inaugurated a steering committee to coordinate efforts to transform Accra into a cleaner, greener and healthier city through partnerships with corporate organisations. The committee, inaugurated at the Ministry’s conference room on Thursday, October 15, 2026, is chaired by the Ga Mantse, King Nii Tackie Teiko Tsuru II. Its membership includes representatives of key technical agencies, the Greater Accra Regional Coordinating Council and Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies. A central component of the Accra Green and Clean City Initiative is the Adopt-a-Street/Adopt-a-Corridor Programme, which will encourage corporate organisations to partner with the Ministry and local assemblies to maintain designated streets, road medians, roundabouts and public spaces. Participating organisations are expected to undertake regular cleaning, landscaping and tree planting as part of their corporate social responsibility activities. Mr Ayariga charged the committee to develop an implementation framework, identify priority corridors, mobilise corporate partners and establish monitoring mechanisms to track progress. The initiative is intended to promote sustainable partnerships that will improve the appearance of public spaces and support a cleaner, greener and more attractive Accra.

items.title: Power Division projects Rs2.56 per unit increase in Nov bills, says bigger hike averted due to load management
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Power Division on Thursday projected a Rs2.56 per unit increase in November bills for electricity consumers on account of fuel cost adjustment (FCA) for September, citing the use of expensive fuel for electricity generation. The increase is expected to bring in around Rs33bn for the Power Division, which said in a statement that the additional FCA could have been significantly higher, by around Rs3.44 per unit, but targeted load shedding helped contain the increase. “The Ministry of Energy (Power Division) has averted a potential Rs5-6 per unit hike in the September fuel price adjustment (FPA) through timely measures, including targeted load management, limiting the projected adjustment to Rs2.56 per unit despite rising international fuel prices and constraints on LNG supplies,” the statement said. “Targeted load management and other measures helped limit the impact of expensive fuels used for power generation, saving consumers from an additional burden of up to Rs3.44 per unit,” the Power Division said. It added that targeted load management for approximately two to two-and-a-half hours during September helped reduce reliance on costly alternative fuels, including furnace oil and high-speed diesel, and contained the anticipated increase in the FPA. The division maintained the provision of imported re-gasified liquefied natural gas (RLNG) for power generation at domestic gas prices had further eased the burden on consumers by 83 paisa per unit. However, it noted that international fuel prices had risen sharply amid the Middle East conflict and disruptions to fuel supply chains following the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Against this backdrop, despite Qatar’s declaration of force majeure, Pakistan continued efforts to meet its RLNG requirements through available contracted supplies and additional spot cargoes, wherever necessary, the statement said. The Power Division claimed that the combined impact of fuel price adjustments and quarterly tariff adjustments during Jan-Aug had been limited to 65 paisa per unit, equivalent to an increase of only 1.9 per cent over the base electricity tariff. It attributed this outcome partly to tariff rationalisation measures and an additional electricity consumption package for industrial and agricultural consumers, which encouraged greater use of electricity from the national grid. According to the Power Division, the September FPA is expected to be Rs1.45 per unit higher than that of August’s Rs1.11 per unit FCA, with an estimated financial impact of Rs32.7bn on consumers’ electricity bills in November. The Power Division said it was continuing to monitor developments in international fuel markets and supply chains while taking measures to minimise the impact of external price shocks on electricity consumers. On the other hand, industrial consumers are contesting the purported positive impact of industrial support package on incremental consumption and claim that Rs22.96 per unit marginal cost rate was helping a select few while the actual marginal cost of Rs34 per unit was resulting in Rs11 per unit feeding into the average consumer tariff, becoming a burden for all consumers. The National Electric Power Regulatory Authority last week conducted a public hearing on the revision or suspension of incremental package but an outcome is awaited.

items.title: France : la préfecture de Paris interdit un parcours de manifestation avant le 17 octobre
items.description: La mobilisation du 17 octobre n'a pas encore commence que les autorites parisiennes en restreignent deja les itineraires. Le prefet de police, Patrice Faure, a interdit le parcours d'un cortege, alors que la colere contre la vie chere rejoint celle des lyceens. Le 15 octobre, la prefecture a rejete le parcours declare par Interfac IDF, de Republique a Concorde, invoquant des risques de troubles a l'ordre public et la proximite de bâtiments officiels. Elle propose de rejoindre Nation a la place, ce que refusent les organisateurs. Un second cortege, reunissant des Gilets jaunes et des syndicats, est envisage d'Opera a Bastille. La police veut, la encore, imposer un autre itineraire. Un rassemblement sur les Champs-elysees a egalement ete demande, sans decision annoncee a ce stade. L'Union etudiante appelle a se retrouver a Republique a 14 heures. Le retour du spectre des Gilets jaunes Plus de 1 000 initiatives sont repertoriees en ligne a travers le pays, sans garantie qu'elles auront toutes lieu. La multiplication des appels montre toutefois que la contestation depasse largement Paris. La flambee des prix, notamment des carburants, rappelle les revendications a l'origine des Gilets jaunes en novembre 2018. Pres de huit ans plus tard, le pouvoir d'achat reste au centre de la contestation et les syndicats tentent de federer les mecontentements. La secretaire generale de la CGT, Sophie Binet, a annonce le soutien de son syndicat : « La montee du 17 octobre montre l'ampleur de la colere et donc, partout ou les conditions seront reunies, la CGT en sera. » Une jeunesse mobilisee, un gouvernement sur la defensive Le rendez-vous du 17 octobre pourrait prolonger les manifestations lyceennes contre la penurie d'enseignants, l'etat des etablissements et Parcoursup. Malgre la promesse de 3 000 professeurs remplacants, la contestation se poursuit. La reponse policiere est aussi contestee : plus de 6 800 personnes ont ete placees en garde a vue et plusieurs blessures font l'objet d'enquetes. Le 15 octobre, le Premier ministre Sebastien Lecornu a qualifie l'evolution du mouvement de « mouvement de violences urbaines ». Face a la colere provoquee par la vie chere et les difficultes de l'ecole publique, le gouvernement insiste surtout sur les risques de violences. Cette priorite donnee au maintien de l'ordre expose l'executif a de nouvelles critiques, a quelques mois de l'election presidentielle de 2027.

items.title: Coopération sanitaire: les Pays-Bas réaffirment leur engagement aux côtés du Burkina Faso
items.description: Le ministre de la Santé, Dr Robert Lucien Jean-Claude Kargougou, a reçu en audience, le mercredi 14 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou, une délégation du ministère des Affaires étrangères des Pays-Bas, conduite par Peter Derrek Hof, directeur du développement social. Au cœur des échanges : les priorités sanitaires du Burkina Faso et les perspectives de consolidation de la coopération entre les deux pays. Cette rencontre a permis à la délégation néerlandaise de mieux appréhender les orientations du gouvernement burkinabè en matière de santé, ainsi que les efforts engagés pour améliorer l’accès des populations aux soins. Les discussions ont notamment porté sur le développement des infrastructures sanitaires, le renforcement des compétences du personnel de santé, la disponibilité des médicaments et l’acquisition d’équipements médicaux. Au-delà des priorités nationales, les échanges ont mis en lumière le rôle des partenaires techniques et financiers dans le renforcement du système de santé. Peter Derrek Hof a rappelé la contribution des Pays-Bas au financement de plusieurs mécanismes et organisations internationales, notamment le Fonds mondial, Gavi, le Mécanisme de financement mondial (GFF) et le Fonds des Nations unies pour la population (UNFPA), dont les interventions soutiennent différents programmes sanitaires au Burkina Faso. Qualifiant la rencontre de « très informative et très utile », le responsable néerlandais a réaffirmé la volonté de son pays de poursuivre le dialogue avec les autorités burkinabè. Il a également souligné l’importance de maintenir des échanges étroits autour des besoins en infrastructures sanitaires et des possibilités de contribution du secteur privé. Cette audience témoigne de la volonté des deux parties de maintenir un cadre de dialogue sur les enjeux sanitaires. L’objectif est de favoriser une meilleure articulation des appuis extérieurs avec les priorités nationales et de soutenir durablement les efforts engagés pour renforcer le système de santé et améliorer les conditions de prise en charge des populations. DCRP/MS L’article Coopération sanitaire: les Pays-Bas réaffirment leur engagement aux côtés du Burkina Faso est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Drivers threaten to remove traders from lorry stations over TrafficTech concerns
items.description: Commercial drivers in Accra have issued a one-week ultimatum to authorities to eject traders who have taken over lorry stations, threatening to take the law into their own hands if nothing is done. According to the drivers, the activities of traders at major lorry parks and bus stops are making it impossible for transport operations to run smoothly and for the new TrafficTech enforcement system to work. The drivers, comprising members of the Ghana Private Road Transport Union (GPRTU), Concerned Drivers Association and other transport operators, say traders have converted loading bays, pedestrian walkways and road shoulders into market stalls. Speaking to journalists, the drivers lamented that passengers now struggle to board vehicles while drivers are forced to load on the roadside, creating heavy traffic and confrontations with city authorities. “TrafficTech cannot be implemented when traders have taken over our stations. How do you expect us to comply when there is no space to park and load?” one driver lamented. “Sack all traders from the lorry stations. We are giving authorities one week to act swiftly. If they fail to order the traders to leave, we will sack them by ourselves,” they warned. They are calling on the Ministry of Local Government, the Accra Metropolitan Assembly (AMA), the Ghana Police Service and the Ministry of Transport to immediately clear traders from all designated lorry stations to avert clashes. They warned that failure to act within the seven-day window could lead to chaos and disruption of transport services nationwide.

items.title: Winners of the Wildlife Photographer of the Year 2026
items.description: © James Lewin / Wildlife Photographer of the Year The Meeting Place . Winner, Animals in Their Environment. James Lewin watched a young bull elephant spray a group of zebra as they congregated in the Kenyan Chyulu Hills. Although there was no shortage of subjects and action around this waterhole, James had to deal with the harsh, unforgiving light. He chose to soften the light using a camera converted to infrared, creating this dreamlike scene. © Anton Sorokin / Wildlife Photographer of the Year Protective Pose . Winner, Behavior: Amphibians and Reptiles. Anton Sorokin found a California newt laying its eggs as it clasped vegetation that already held another newt’s egg clutch. © Alex Visbal / Wildlife Photographer of the Year The Great Divide . Winner, Wetlands: The Bigger Picture. Alex Visbal documented how a single engineered line can reshape an entire wetland in Utah’s Great Salt Lake. The distinctive pink color on the left is caused by bright-pink microbes that thrive in extremely saline water, which happens when an area is cut off from a supply of fresh water. The lake’s ecology is in sharp decline because of industrial use, upstream diversions, and climate change. Since this image was taken, the State of Utah has brought the area under conservation management. © Loren Elliott / Wildlife Photographer of the Year On the Outskirts . Winner, Photojournalist Story Award. A coyote pads along a trail in Bernal Heights Park, overlooking the city and bay of San Francisco. This individual is part of a resident pack that Loren Elliott observed hunting rodents in the park, which is also popular with people and dogs. © Tony Wu / Wildlife Photographer of the Year Making Morays . Winner, Under Water. Tony Wu provides a first-time glimpse into the mating ritual of Abbott’s moray eels. Wu has been working with biologists to address a knowledge gap of the social behavior of this eel species. Guided only by a dim red-light source to minimize disturbance, and using a customized fisheye camera lens, he has studied this male since 2024 as it visits females that dwell in crevices on the reef. © Kutub Uddin / Wildlife Photographer of the Year Tiny Dancers . Winner, Portfolio Award. Kutub Uddin reveals a magical and often surreal world of slime molds that can barely be seen with the naked eye. Fine threads, known as capillitium , emerge on the round, yellow-green bodies, which will eventually help disperse reproductive spores. © Francisco Negroni / Wildlife Photographer of the Year Warning Sign . Winner, Photojournalism. Francisco Negroni recorded this scene of a dead puma amid the rugged, windswept beauty of Argentine Patagonia. Tied to the fence and presented as a hunting trophy, this display was one that Francisco had “never witnessed or photographed before.” In 2025, Santa Cruz banned the hunting of pumas, but illegal persecution continues. © Aaron Sanders / Wildlife Photographer of the Year A Watchful Eye . Winner, Animal Portraits. Aaron Sanders glimpsed a common octopus behind a curtain of kelp in the waters off southwest England. Sanders was diving off Porthkerris Beach when he noticed the footprints of octopus suckers through a thin blade of kelp, and a single eye slowly emerging. “We remained perfectly still, watching one another with a seemingly shared curiosity,” Sanders said. © Oscar Whitfield / Wildlife Photographer of the Year Labour of Love . Winner, 11-14 Years, Young Wildlife Photographer of the Year 2026. Oscar Whitfield noticed the arduous exertion of this dung beetle pushing its precious cargo. Using a fast shutter speed and high light sensitivity, Oscar laid flat on the ground to photograph the beetle at eye level, with the sunshine and heat creating dry dust all around him. © Alex Lindbloom / Wildlife Photographer of the Year Night-Time Catch . Winner, Oceans: The Bigger Picture. Alex Lindbloom found a whale shark investigating the catch of a “bagan,” or mobile net-fishing platform, in the inky waters off Papua. Alex started searching for sharks around dawn when the nets were still in the water. Initially lacking natural light for his drone’s camera, he found these sharks illuminated by the bagan’s bright lights. © Isak Pretorius / Wildlife Photographer of the Year Scenes from the Swamp . Winner, Behaviour: Birds. Isak Pretorius chanced across two elusive shoebill storks among wetland vegetation. Exploring the swamp in a narrow canoe with a guide, Isak felt exceptionally lucky to see not one but two shoebills. The birds pulled out vegetation, dropped it, and then repeated the process several times. It’s likely that this was a breeding pair gathering nesting material. © Federico Veronesi / Wildlife Photographer of the Year The Aftermath . Winner, Behavior: Mammals, and Overall Winner, Wildlife Photographer of the Year 2026. Federico Veronesi witnessed this powerful moment of an elephant carrying a dead calf, a rare glimpse into complex animal behaviors. Veronesi was tracking elephants when he came across an unusual pattern of drag marks in the sand of a dry riverbed. The source became clear when he caught up with a family group. A female emerged with the calf, its leg wedged between her tusk and trunk. Behaviors centering on death have been observed in both Asian and African elephants, including vocalizations, guarding the dead, inspecting and handling bones, and carrying the deceased. Some researchers suggest these behaviors could indicate an elephant’s journey to understanding death, while others interpret these actions as possible displays of grief. © Michał Michalski / Wildlife Photographer of the Year Escape Artistry . Winner, Natural Artistry. Michał Michalski used a slow shutter speed to create the illusion of trees still swathed in autumn foliage. Michalski was in a field of unharvested sunflowers that had attracted mixed flocks of birds, especially goldfinches and bramblings. As they took to the sky, startled by a sparrowhawk, Michalski blurred the movement against a backdrop of leafless birches. © Sitaram Raul / Wildlife Photographer of the Year Shifting Sand . Winner, Behavior: Invertebrates. Sitaram Raul encountered a scorpion burrowing into one of the shifting dunes of the Thar Desert in India. Exploring the dunes at night near the village of Sam, Raul saw many scorpions searching for prey. But as sunrise approached, they started burrowing to avoid the intense heat. Raul timed the exposure so that the excavated sand was suspended in midair. Wildlife Photographer of the Year is developed and produced by the Natural History Museum in London. Captions are provided by the photographers and WPY organizers, and are lightly edited for style.

items.title: Tres de cada diez viviendas vendidas en España generan pérdidas para el propietario
items.description: Tres de cada diez casas vendidas en España durante 2024 generaron pérdidas patrimoniales para su propietario. Es decir, se transmitieron por un precio inferior al que se pagó inicialmente por ellas. En ese año se registraron 379.301 operaciones de inmuebles que servían como vivienda habitual y que no estaban afectos a actividades económicas. De esas transacciones, 114.011 (el 30,1%) se cerraron por debajo del precio de compra original, mientras que las otras 265.290 (el 69,9%) dejaron un saldo positivo para el vendedor. Las operaciones que se cierran con pérdidas corresponden en buena medida a casas que se compraron en el pico de la burbuja, con un precio ya muy elevado, y se han vendido con una rebaja respecto a ese momento. items.title: AI could create 10 to 20 times more jobs despite current recruitment slowdown – Hubtel CEO
items.description: The Chief Executive Officer of Hubtel, Alex Bram, has projected that artificial intelligence (AI) could eventually create 10 to 20 times more jobs, despite growing concerns about the technology displacing workers and making it harder for young graduates to secure employment. He believes the current disruption to businesses and the labour market will be temporary, arguing that human creativity, changing consumer demands and companies’ desire to expand will create new employment opportunities as the technology becomes more widely adopted. “It’s temporary, I think. It’s very temporary. We’re going to end up creating 10 times, 20 times more jobs,” he predicted. Speaking in an interview ahead of the second episode of the Digital Economy Forum , Mr. Bram acknowledged that AI is already affecting recruitment and forcing businesses to reconsider how they operate. He warned that graduates entering the job market could face particular difficulties because AI systems can now perform some of the routine, knowledge-based tasks traditionally assigned to entry-level employees. “So, yes, some people are going to find it very difficult to find work, especially entry-level jobs in very formal environments,” he said. He explained that information acquired through formal education is increasingly accessible through AI systems, allowing employers to undertake certain tasks without necessarily recruiting additional workers. However, the Hubtel CEO maintained that the resulting disruption should not be mistaken for a permanent decline in employment opportunities. “I think in the end AI is going to create a lot more jobs. The reason I say that is three things. The first thing is that as humans, we are extremely creative,” he explained. The opportunities and potential disruptions associated with artificial intelligence will form part of discussions at the second episode of the Digital Economy Forum , under the theme “AI and the Ghana Economy: Opportunity or Disruption?” The forum, held in partnership with Hubtel , will feature the Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Sam George; Technical Advisor at the Finance Ministry, Dr Theo Acheampong; Founder of AI for Ghana, Adam Watkins; Head of Engineering at Hubtel, Augustine Adjei; and Vice President of IMANI Africa, Bright Simons. It will air live on JoyNews and Joy 99.7 FM on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, at 8 p.m. Hubtel feels the disruption Drawing on his company’s experience, Mr. Bram disclosed that Hubtel, which employs approximately 700 people, has not recruited new staff for nearly a year as it restructures its operations to take advantage of artificial intelligence. The company began experimenting with AI in 2022 and established an AI laboratory in 2023. Since then, the technology has significantly influenced its operations. “We haven’t recruited any new staff for about almost a year now. We’re restructuring quite a number of things because we can do certain things faster, better, when we are augmented with AI,” he revealed. Mr. Bram acknowledged that the changes could create uncertainty among employees as the company reviews existing processes and the responsibilities of its workforce. He explained that Hubtel is working to help employees adjust to the changing workplace, including changes within its engineering operations to focus more on productivity. “People need to change their roles, what they do on a day-to-day basis. We need to help people transition into this new era,” he said. While the company has experienced a slowdown in recruitment, Mr Bram did not disclose any layoffs resulting from AI adoption. He insisted that businesses would ultimately find new opportunities to expand their operations as the technology improves productivity. Why AI could create more jobs Explaining his optimism, Mr. Bram identified three factors he believes will sustain employment creation in an AI-driven economy. The first is human creativity, which he argues will continue to produce new ideas, products and services that technology alone cannot exhaust. The second is the continuous evolution of human needs and consumer preferences. “We have enormous and endless desires as humans, which is like we’re never satisfied,” he explained. He argued that these changing demands would encourage entrepreneurs and businesses to develop new products and services, creating further economic opportunities. His third argument is that successful businesses are primarily motivated by growth, profitability and market expansion rather than simply reducing their workforce. “Every company I know competes on how much profit you can make, how many more people you can serve, how much dominance you can exercise on the market. You want to win. Every company is strategising to win,” he said. Mr. Bram used Hubtel as an example, arguing that drastically reducing its workforce would not necessarily position the company to become a dominant digital services provider. He believes that although some organisations may initially reduce costs or restructure their operations, the long-term economic opportunities presented by AI could encourage businesses to expand into new areas. The CEO did not provide a specific timeline or supporting employment projections for his expectation that AI could create 10 to 20 times more jobs. The figure reflects his outlook on the technology rather than an independently established forecast. Workers must adapt Despite his optimism, Mr. Bram cautioned that workers and professionals would have to reconsider how they deliver value as artificial intelligence becomes more accessible. He identified doctors, lawyers and accountants among professionals whose traditional ways of working could be significantly affected. According to him, AI is making specialised information more widely available, meaning professionals can no longer rely exclusively on knowledge that clients previously found difficult to access. He argued that the emphasis must increasingly shift towards using that knowledge to deliver better outcomes for clients. For example, he suggested that lawyers could focus more on reviewing agreements, offering expert guidance and representing clients, even as AI tools make it easier for individuals to prepare basic legal documents. He believes businesses must also redesign their processes to allow employees to work effectively alongside AI rather than treating the technology solely as a replacement for human labour. Opportunities for Ghana Looking ahead, Mr. Bram expressed confidence that Ghana could benefit considerably from artificial intelligence if the country develops the necessary skills, infrastructure and policies. He envisages a future in which young Ghanaians use AI to improve manufacturing, agriculture, design and other productive sectors. “I want to see more Ghanaians be better designers, be better manufacturers, be better farmers, be better agro-processors,” he said. He believes the technology could help businesses and individuals find solutions to longstanding challenges, improve productivity and accelerate national development.
