items.title: Cybercrime: IGP warns Nigerians against seven online offences
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Disu, has warned Nigerians that unauthorised access to private accounts, online impersonation, cyberbullying, spreading false information, sharing intimate images without consent and facilitating financial fraud can attract criminal prosecution. Disu urged citizens to exercise caution in their online activities, verify information before sharing it and avoid lending their bank accounts or SIM cards to others for suspicious transactions. He gave the warning in Abuja at the 2026 Cybersecurity Awareness Campaign of the Nigeria Police Force National Cybercrime Centre, NPF-NCCC, themed, “Towards a Resilient Cyberspace: Think Before You Click.” The IGP said many people could become involved in cybercrime through seemingly casual online activities without appreciating their legal consequences. “Many Nigerians do not wake up to commit cybercrime. They stumble into it through small things done casually,” he said. Citing the Cybercrimes (Prohibition, Prevention, etc.) Act, 2015, as amended, Disu listed unauthorised access to another person’s phone, WhatsApp, email or social media account as a potential criminal offence. He also warned against creating fake accounts using another person’s name or photograph, sending threatening or harassing messages, and knowingly circulating false information capable of causing panic or endangering lives. The police chief said sharing another person’s nude or private photographs and videos without consent could also attract prosecution, adding that offences involving children were particularly serious. He cautioned Nigerians against allowing others to use their bank accounts or SIM cards to receive money without understanding the source and purpose of the transactions, warning that accounts used to facilitate fraud could expose their holders to investigation and possible prosecution. Disu further identified fake payment alerts and receipts, as well as dealings in other people’s Bank Verification Numbers, National Identification Numbers and card details, as activities that could amount to fraud, forgery or other cybercrime offences. He stressed that ignorance of the law would not excuse criminal conduct, adding that people who knowingly aided, encouraged or conspired with cybercriminals could also face legal consequences. “The penalties include imprisonment and heavy fines. Your thumb is powerful; one tap can build a life or ruin one. So before you post, pause. Before you forward, verify. Before you lend, think,” he said. Calls for proactive cybersecurity Beyond individual online conduct, Disu called for a proactive approach to cybersecurity, urging law enforcement agencies and other stakeholders to identify emerging threats and vulnerabilities before they cause harm. He said Nigeria’s digital environment had become central to national security, economic activities, public services and everyday life, while exposing citizens, businesses and institutions to fraud, identity theft, data breaches, extortion and cyber-enabled financial crimes. According to him, protecting the country must extend beyond physical spaces to the networks, platforms and systems on which society depends. He said effective cybersecurity required intelligence-led policing, threat analysis, open-source intelligence, digital forensics and timely information sharing. “We must move from incident response to threat anticipation, from reactive investigation to proactive disruption, from analysing yesterday’s attacks to preparing for tomorrow’s,” he said. The IGP, however, emphasised that such efforts must be guided by reliable intelligence, human oversight, the rule of law and respect for fundamental rights. He described personnel of the NPF-NCCC as guardians of Nigeria’s digital frontier, saying the centre must continue to strengthen its capacity to analyse threats, investigate offences, preserve digital evidence, support victims and disrupt criminal networks. Disu said technology alone could not guarantee cybersecurity without skilled personnel, sound procedures, accountability and public trust. Banks, fintechs urged to strengthen internal controls The police chief also called on banks, fintech companies, payment service providers and telecommunications operators to strengthen internal controls and address potential insider threats. He said cyber-enabled financial crimes could be facilitated by malicious conduct, collusion, compromised credentials, abuse of privileged access, negligence or weak oversight. According to him, organisations should strengthen access controls, employee screening, separation of duties, transaction monitoring, internal audits and independent oversight. “Privileged access must be tightly governed and suspicious patterns must trigger prompt review,” he said. Disu clarified that the warning was not a judgment on the integrity of employees in those sectors, but a reminder that trust must be supported by verification and accountability. He said the NPF-NCCC would continue to work with regulators and financial intelligence agencies to support the lawful detection and investigation of cyber-enabled financial crimes, including alleged insider collusion. Where evidence existed, he added, investigations would be conducted professionally and impartially. Youth urged to shun cybercrime The IGP urged parents and educators to make online safety an essential life skill, while calling on businesses to treat cybersecurity as a leadership responsibility rather than an information technology issue. He also encouraged technology and financial sector partners to incorporate security into their services and cooperate lawfully with relevant authorities. Addressing young Nigerians, Disu said their digital skills could contribute to national development if channelled into legitimate careers in cybersecurity, software development and technology entrepreneurship. “Do not let pressure for quick wealth mortgage your future. Cybercrime can cost your freedom, reputation and peace of mind. Choose creativity over criminality and integrity over shortcuts,” he said. He urged victims of fraud, cyberbullying, sextortion and recruitment attempts into cybercrime to seek assistance and report such incidents. Disu said building a resilient cyberspace required cooperation among government agencies, law enforcement, regulators, financial institutions, technology providers, educators, civil society, the media and citizens. He called for stronger mechanisms for sharing threat intelligence, reporting incidents promptly, coordinating responses and preserving digital evidence, stressing that cybersecurity was a shared responsibility. items.title: Financement associatif : L’intérieur appelle les walis et gouverneurs à durcir les contrôles
items.description: Les walis et gouverneurs ont été appelés à renforcer la surveillance des aides versées par les collectivités territoriales à la société civile. Les nouvelles directives prévoient un contrôle des conventions de partenariat avant et après leur mise en œuvre, ainsi qu’une vérification plus stricte de la situation juridique des associations et de l’utilisation des fonds publics. La distribution des subventions publiques aux associations fait l’objet d’un encadrement renforcé au Maroc. De nouvelles instructions des services centraux du ministère de l’intérieur ont été adressées aux walis et gouverneurs des préfectures et provinces du royaume, avec pour objectif de mieux contrôler les aides financières accordées aux organisations de la société civile sur les budgets des collectivités territoriales. Les autorités entendent mettre un terme aux pratiques jugées désordonnées dans la répartition de subventions et d’aides représentant des milliards de dirhams, en imposant un examen préalable et un contrôle a posteriori des conventions de partenariat et de financement. Selon des sources bien informées qui se sont confiées à Hespress , des gouverneurs des régions de Casablanca-Settat et de Rabat-Salé-Kénitra ont déjà commencé à appliquer ces directives. Des courriers ont été adressés aux présidents des collectivités territoriales relevant de leur ressort pour les inviter à revoir leurs modalités de gestion du soutien aux associations. Avant tout engagement financier, ils sont notamment appelés à vérifier la situation juridique des organismes concernés et à s’assurer que leurs activités sont conformes aux objectifs inscrits dans leurs statuts. Au-delà de la régularité administrative des dossiers, les nouvelles mesures visent à mieux encadrer les critères d’attribution des fonds. Les autorités insistent sur la nécessité de mettre en place des procédures transparentes de sélection et de subordonner les financements à la nature des activités et des programmes proposés. Il ne s’agit plus de se limiter à la signature de conventions de partenariat, mais de prévoir des indicateurs précis pour mesurer les résultats obtenus et des mécanismes permettant de suivre l’exécution des engagements pris par chaque partie. Des critères d’attribution plus stricts Les présidents des collectivités territoriales sont placés au premier plan de ce dispositif de contrôle. Ils devront s’assurer que les associations bénéficiaires exercent réellement leurs activités et disposent des capacités nécessaires pour mener à bien les projets financés. Les contributions accordées devront également rester compatibles avec les crédits inscrits dans les budgets des collectivités, afin d’éviter tout engagement financier supérieur aux ressources disponibles. Les directives rappellent, dans le même temps, que les conventions de soutien doivent respecter les compétences propres, partagées et transférées aux collectivités territoriales, telles qu’elles sont définies par la loi organique n° 113.14 relative aux communes. Les financements doivent ainsi concerner des domaines relevant des prérogatives des conseils élus, à l’exclusion des activités et des projets situés en dehors de leur champ légal d’intervention. Les autorités provinciales demandent également aux responsables locaux de respecter les procédures d’appels à projets pour sélectionner les associations bénéficiaires, conformément aux règles en vigueur. Cette démarche doit permettre aux organismes remplissant les conditions requises de disposer de possibilités d’accès plus équitables aux financements. L’examen des dossiers devra reposer sur des critères transparents, tenant compte de la nature des activités proposées, de leurs objectifs et des populations auxquelles elles s’adressent. Le contrôle s’étend aussi aux conventions de partenariat à vocation développementale ou d’investissement. Les commissions techniques compétentes sont appelées à jouer pleinement leur rôle dans leur examen, en évaluant leur pertinence et leur cohérence avec les priorités du développement local. Cette étape doit intervenir avant la présentation des conventions pour approbation et l’accomplissement des procédures de visa, afin de sécuriser les engagements financiers et juridiques qui en découlent. Justifier l’utilisation des fonds publics Le renforcement du dispositif ne s’arrête pas à l’attribution des subventions. Les nouvelles instructions imposent également aux présidents des collectivités de consolider les mécanismes de suivi et de contrôle après le versement des aides. Les associations financées devront remettre des rapports finaux détaillés, sur les plans moral et financier, rendant compte de l’exécution des programmes et des projets soutenus. Ces documents devront être accompagnés de pièces justificatives permettant de retracer l’utilisation des crédits et de vérifier que les sommes versées ont bien été affectées aux objectifs prévus par les conventions de partenariat. Cette exigence vise à renforcer la traçabilité des dépenses et à rapprocher l’octroi des subventions des résultats effectivement obtenus. Une attention particulière devra également être portée à la situation juridique des associations candidates. Les autorités demandent aux collectivités de vérifier la conformité de la composition des bureaux dirigeants avec les procès-verbaux des assemblées générales et les statuts des organisations, avant de transmettre les conventions aux services compétents pour validation. Enfin, les dossiers de convention devront comporter plusieurs pièces administratives : des copies des récépissés définitifs, les déclarations légales, les cartes nationales d’identité des membres des bureaux dirigeants, ainsi que les documents relatifs à la situation organisationnelle des associations. L’objectif est de permettre aux autorités de s’assurer de la légalité des organismes contractants et de l’exactitude des informations communiquées sur leurs représentants. À travers cet ensemble de mesures, le ministère de l’intérieur entend renforcer la surveillance de l’argent public versé aux associations, depuis la sélection des bénéficiaires jusqu’à la justification des dépenses. La mise en œuvre effective de ces directives devra permettre de mieux encadrer les financements des collectivités territoriales et de privilégier les projets dont les retombées pour les citoyens peuvent être vérifiées. The post Financement associatif : L’intérieur appelle les walis et gouverneurs à durcir les contrôles appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Bangkok : la voix de la Guinée porte ! au Caucus des gouverneurs africains, face à Ajay Banga et à Kristalina Georgieva
items.description: Les Assemblées annuelles FMI–Banque mondiale abordent leur vitesse de croisière. Entre rencontres techniques, échanges informels et séances plénières, le ballet est intense. Mercredi, 14 octobre 2026, la délégation guinéenne a pris une part active aux Caucus des gouverneurs africains, d’abord avec le Président du Groupe de la Banque mondiale, puis avec la Directrice Générale du FMI. Elle était conduite par Mme la Ministre de l’Économie, des Finances et du Budget, Mariama Ciré Sylla, Gouverneure pays auprès des deux institutions, et comprenait le Ministre du Plan, le Gouverneur de la BCRG et de hauts cadres. Avec le Président Ajay Banga : financer l’Afrique face aux crises Le Président du Groupe de la Banque mondiale et son équipe ont longuement échangé avec les ministres gouverneurs africains. Au cœur des débats : le financement des économies du continent face aux crises successives, l’impact des ressources de l’IDA (bilan de l’IDA-21 et gestion des chocs depuis la COVID-19) et la nécessité de réformer les modèles de croissance. Les orientations retenues : Changer de paradigme. Ajay Banga a plaidé pour une place prioritaire aux PME africaines, avec un meilleur accès aux capitaux, des facilités bancaires accrues et des mécanismes de crédit adaptés. C’est le levier essentiel d’une résilience durable, pour s’affranchir de la dépendance exclusive à l’aide extérieure. Investir dans les infrastructures et le capital humain Pour capitaliser sur la jeunesse du continent, il faut conjuguer réformes favorisant l’investissement privé et consolidation des services de base : éducation, santé, connectivité numérique. L’intervention remarquée de Mme la Ministre Au nom de la Guinée, Mme Mariama Ciré Sylla a plaidé pour la valorisation des corridors de croissance sur le continent. Elle a présenté l’approche guinéenne du programme Simandou : bâtir, autour des infrastructures ferroviaire et portuaire, un corridor d’investissements structurants pour diversifier l’économie et créer des emplois décents. Mme la Ministre Gouverneure a aussi insisté sur la transformation sur place des ressources minières en Afrique, sur le soutien au secteur privé et aux champions nationaux, et sur la valorisation du capital humain, que vise la Simandou Academy. Une contribution très appréciée par le Caucus À l’issue de la séance, le Président du Conseil des Gouverneurs africains a remis à Ajay Banga un mémorandum officiel du Caucus sur les engagements liés à l’IDA-21. Avec Mme Kristalina Georgieva : résilience et transformation structurelle. Seconde rencontre de grande envergure : un échange « puissant et constructif », selon la délégation, avec la Directrice Générale du FMI et son équipe. Thème : des partenariats renforcés pour consolider la résilience économique et promouvoir la transformation structurelle de l’Afrique, dans un environnement mondial de plus en plus exposé, aux chocs. Les discussions ont ciblé la gestion de la dette publique, le climat des affaires et l’intégration régionale. Les préoccupations et attentes africaines : Une voix plus forte Le Caucus a salué l’impact concret du troisième siège attribué à l’Afrique subsaharienne au conseil d’administration du FMI, et demande de poursuivre vers une représentativité encore accrue. Une dette plus soutenable. Le service de la dette absorbe jusqu’à la moitié des recettes fiscales dans certains pays. Les gouverneurs réclament une réforme de l’architecture financière mondiale : mécanismes de résolution plus rapides, financements à coûts plus abordables, pour protéger les budgets d’éducation et de santé, soutien pour faire face aux chocs liés au changement climatique, rendre les espaces budgétaires efficaces et durables. L’intégration régionale comme moteur. La pleine mise en œuvre de la ZLECAf est identifiée comme le levier pour bâtir des chaînes de valeur régionales et renforcer la compétitivité du continent. Un appui du FMI sur mesure. La Directrice Générale a réitéré l’engagement du Fonds à adapter ses outils de prêt aux réalités africaines, pour aider à reconstituer les marges budgétaires, protéger les populations vulnérables et encourager un climat d’investissement plus attractif. » je vous ai entendu pour vos plaidoyer…ce qui est bon pour l’Afrique, est bon pour le monde entier. L ‘Afrique…c’est l’avenir et c’est là que le monde devra trouver le futur moteur de sa croissance et son développement. » affirmera, la Patronne du FMI. Le plaidoyer : un message africain dans un monde incertain Dans un contexte mondial fragile et volatil, les gouverneurs africains ont porté un message commun : financer la transformation plutôt que seulement amortir les chocs. Cela suppose des ressources concessionnelles à la hauteur, une dette gérable, des PME mieux financées, une intégration régionale accélérée et une industrialisation qui retienne la valeur ajoutée sur le continent. La Guinée y apporte une contribution concrète : un corridor Simandou pensé comme moteur de diversification, de création d’emplois et de formation de talents. C’est ce qui a donné du poids à la voix de la Ministre Mariama Ciré Sylla à Bangkok. Service Communication, Relations Publiques MEFB

items.title: Will Supply Ministry’s wheat intervention really rein in cost of unsubsidized bread?
items.description: As the grain and bakery industries petition the government for permission to increase bread prices in order to protect their profits, the Supply Ministry has announced it is injecting wheat onto the national commodity exchange to bring prices down and cut production costs. The move came after calls for a government review of bread pricing guidelines in August and September . Producers said they needed to increase consumer prices to compensate for rising production costs, particularly of flour. Despite talks between ministry and industry representatives, the government has held the price caps and loaf weight specifications steady , announcing the supply release instead. However, sources from the grain, milling and bakery industries who spoke to Mada Masr expressed doubt that the mechanism would meaningfully reduce production costs, indicating that the last time the ministry undertook a similar supply allocation in 2023, the move only fuelled profiteering on a secondary market that emerged in parallel to the commodity exchange. The ministry has not said how much wheat it will offer via the commodity exchange, though ministry spokespeople explained that the extra supply would be enough to bring costs down across the supply chain. Speaking on condition of anonymity, two grain industry sources told Mada Masr that the imported wheat is expected to be available via the Egyptian Commodities Exchange either this week or next. Sales are to be capped at 500 tonnes per mill, and, as per the agreement with the ministry, two trading sessions would be held weekly, the sources said. The CEO of the commodity exchange told financial newspapers on Tuesday that trading had begun this week. The ministry aims to sell wheat at LE16,500-LE16,700 per tonne. The sources said supplies will be available to all licensed mills, allowing more flour for bakeries that produce commercial bread, such as fino and “tourist” loaves. However, the announced prices alone are not enough to convince mills to buy wheat through the exchange, said another grain industry chamber member. A tonne of wheat currently costs LE16,800-LE17,200 on the open market, depending on quality. But once the additional costs of participating in trading on the commodity exchange are factored in, the gap between the exchange price and the open market price narrows. The source said that mills remain skeptical about the value of going to the exchange under its current system, given the registration and trading fees involved — costs they do not necessarily incur when purchasing directly from traders. The source added that it would be difficult to assess whether the government’s price is competitive or not before learning more about the specifications and quality of the wheat being offered. When buying directly from private sector suppliers, mills can inspect a shipment before completing a purchase. A mill owner said that there are questions beyond the immediate cost of the wheat: can the government ensure a steady supply of wheat through the commodity exchange to control costs and justify the cost of switching to the exchange? Until the government’s mechanism proves capable of consistently meeting market demand, dealing with established suppliers is the more transparent option, he said. Global wheat prices have risen amid Russia’s escalating war on Ukraine, disrupting Black Sea shipping and ultimately pushing costs up in Egypt, the world’s largest wheat importer. While the government says it has bought more domestically grown wheat, Egypt is still heavily reliant on wheat imports from both Russia and Ukraine. The cost pressures have become increasingly evident in Egypt’s domestic flour market over recent months. The price of a tonne of imported wheat stood at around LE12,500 in June, with a ton of unsubsidized flour at around LE17,000. Now, a ton of unsubsidized flour stands at around LE21,000. Flour, in turn, accounts for between 60-70 percent of the production cost of commercial bread, according to an estimate from an anonymous General Bakeries Division source. This makes rising flour prices a direct strain on bakeries’ profit margins, particularly alongside increases in other operating costs. A bakeries division member told Mada Masr that resuming wheat sales through the exchange would not be an adequate solution to the gap between the production costs of unsubsidized bread and the prices set by the Supply Ministry. The government used the same mechanism around three years ago, the source said, without adequately increasing the supply of raw materials available to bakeries to ease cost pressures. Bakeries’ costs include various production inputs, all of which are impacted as the exchange value of the Egyptian pound continues to fall against the dollar, which is currently trading at LE53, up from less than LE49 at the end of August. The Supply Ministry last offered imported wheat via the exchange from October 2023 until January 21, 2024. Then-Supply Minister Ali Meselhy attributed the trading suspension to price speculation on domestic wheat prices. At the time, sources who spoke to Mada Masr pointed not only to the small quantities offered by the ministry, which limited their impact on market prices, but also said that several mills that weren’t actively processing grain at the time registered as buyers on the exchange only to bull and then resell the government-offered wheat at higher prices in the free market. The commodity exchange was established by prime ministerial decree in 2020 as an organized market for trading storable commodities through what the exchange itself describes as an “important” pricing mechanism. Meselhy described it at the time as a way to regulate prices, saying it would promote market transparency and reduce price disparities across markets. items.title: Okpara built wealth, not personal fortune — Arthur Eze
items.description: . Present leaders struggling to match Okpara’s legacies- Otti . Plans tech-driven farm settlements, targets food exports . As Okpara’s son seeks return to dad’s green revolution By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — The Chairman of the third Michael Okpara Memorial Lecture, Chief Arthur Eze, has challenged Nigerian leaders to emulate the late Premier of the defunct Eastern Region, Dr Michael Okpara, who prioritised wealth creation, industrialisation and public welfare over personal enrichment. Eze, represented by Prince Emeka Eze, said Okpara exemplified selfless leadership and unimpeachable integrity, noting that despite controlling enormous public resources as Premier between 1959 and 1966, he died without owning a decent home. Speaking at the Michael Okpara University of Agriculture, Umudike (MOUAU), during the lecture themed “Leveraging Technology in Agriculture: Building Digital Rails for Food Security, Agroenterprise and Financial Inclusion,” he recalled how Okpara transformed the Eastern Region through farm settlements, industries, free education and scholarships. He cited farm settlements in Ohaji, Igbariam, Ulonna and Ububra as examples of Okpara’s commitment to empowering young people, creating jobs and driving economic growth. Eze urged present-day leaders to embrace the late Premier’s philosophy that government should create wealth and improve citizens’ welfare rather than serve as a platform for personal enrichment. Otti unveils farm settlement plan Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, announced plans to establish technology-driven farm settlements to make the state self-sufficient in food production and a net exporter of agricultural produce. He said a working group comprising government officials, MOUAU representatives and agricultural experts would identify the state’s comparative advantages and develop an implementation plan, with himself leading the team. “I want us to start with a farm settlement. We want to take it to this level now, where we introduce technology, and we don’t only want to be self-sufficient in food production. We want to be a net exporter of food for Abia State,” Otti said. He directed the university’s Vice-Chancellor to nominate one or two experts for the team and pledged government funding for the initiative, which he hopes will yield results within six months to one year. Otti identified palm produce, cocoa, avocado and cashew as potential areas of investment, stressing the need to move from subsistence farming to commercial agriculture, processing and exports. Citing lessons from a recent visit to Ethiopia, he said the country’s agricultural exports demonstrated how investment, innovation and improved crop varieties could turn agriculture into a major revenue earner. “We are not a failure, but we’ve not done well. And we must accept that. This is a wake-up call for us to start doing well. We can do well,” he said. The governor also pledged continued support for MOUAU’s infrastructure and development. Technology key to food security, agricultural revolution – VC . Says Okpara’s legacy must inspire action In her address, the Vice-Chancellor, Prof . Ngozi Akanwa, called for increased investment in agricultural technology, research and innovation to tackle food insecurity, boost agribusiness and drive economic development. She said artificial intelligence, precision farming, biotechnology, smart irrigation and digital agricultural markets could improve productivity, reduce post-harvest losses and strengthen agricultural value chains. Prof . Akanwa said the university would move beyond commemorating its namesake to translating his legacy into practical results through relevant research, quality graduates, technology transfer and research commercialisation. She also pledged to strengthen partnerships with government, industry and farming communities to position MOUAU as a leading agricultural hub. The Vice-Chancellor commended Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, for supporting the university’s development, including improvements to its entrance gate and the provision of a new statue of its namesake. In his remarks, the Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of the Governing Council, Comrade Fidelis Ede, described Okpara as a great sage whose agricultural revolution remained outstanding and unparalleled, urging contemporary leaders to draw lessons from his vision and commitment to development. NRCRI DG canvasses value addition The Director-General of the National Root Crops Research Institute (NRCRI), Umudike, Prof. Chidozie Ngozi Egesi, called for technology-driven agriculture to increase farmers’ earnings, reduce losses and stimulate industrialisation. He said the institute was deploying conventional breeding and modern genomic techniques to develop higher-yielding, disease-resistant, climate-resilient and nutritious varieties of cassava, yam, sweet potato and other root and tuber crops. Egesi also highlighted efforts to improve farmers’ access to quality planting materials through decentralised seed multiplication systems. He stressed that Nigeria must move beyond exporting raw produce to processing crops into food products, livestock feed, starch and other industrial raw materials. “Technology is anything that enables a farmer to produce more, to lose less, to earn more and to manage his risk better,” he said. He called for stronger collaboration among universities, research institutes, businesses and governments to translate research into commercially viable innovations. Okpara’s son urges smarter farming The late Premier’s first son, Chief Uzodinma Okpara, urged the Igbo to deploy modern technology to achieve food security, boost productivity and create wealth. He said his father’s agricultural vision must be pursued through smarter production methods, value addition and improved market access. “It will not simply be about growing more. It will be about growing more in a smarter way, adding value, connecting to markets, and turning science into prosperity,” he said. Okpara commended MOUAU Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Ngozi Akanwa and her team for sustaining the institution’s agricultural mandate, noting that its farm experiments and departmental research reflected its commitment to practical agriculture. The lecture was delivered by Dr Seyi Ebenezer, founder and Chief Executive Officer of PAYAZA Africa Limited. The post Okpara built wealth, not personal fortune — Arthur Eze appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Sexual abuse in schools persists because perpetrators are not held accountable – Dr Nyarkoa
items.description: Educator and Gender Advocate, Dr Abena Nyarkoa, has warned that sexual abuse is becoming normalised in Ghanaian schools because perpetrators are not being held accountable. She has called for immediate action, including clear policies on how schools should handle allegations of sexual misconduct and stronger education to help prevent abuse. Speaking on JoyNews’ The Pulse on Thursday, October 15, Dr Nyarkoa said the failure to punish perpetrators undermined efforts to address the problem. “If I have to be frank, I think it has been normalised. I think sex in schools has been normalised. And it is very important that we are talking about it now; it needs to be addressed. The key question we have to ask is, why does it keep happening over and over again? It is because people are not held accountable,” she said. Her comments followed allegations of sexual abuse involving the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School and female students. READ ALSO : Obuasi SHTS: Number of students alleging sexual abuse rises to 16 Dr Nyarkoa stressed the need for authorities to establish clear procedures for responding to such cases and ensure that those found culpable face consequences. She also called for greater parental involvement, arguing that efforts to protect students must include parents alongside school authorities. According to her, education on sexual abuse must receive greater attention to discourage misconduct, while accountability must underpin measures to safeguard students. “There is this social parlance that ‘prevention is better than cure’, so we need to address it at the root. I am saying that education is very important; education on sexual consent and sexual boundaries is very important,” “We need to involve parents as well. Parents must have a conversation with their children,” she said. The Obuasi case is the subject of a JoyNews investigation by Manasseh Azure Awuni, titled Inside the Dreaded Headmaster’s Bungalow, which examines allegations against the school’s headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai. MyJoyOnline reported on October 15 that Manasseh initially received information concerning five students. The number increased to 14 during his visit to the school, with two additional students subsequently coming forward, bringing the total to 16. The investigation also reported that complaints had reached municipal authorities, education officials and other influential figures months before the headmaster’s suspension. On October 13, Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu directed the Ghana Education Service to suspend Mr Abdulai pending a full investigation. He also requested an investigation by the Criminal Investigation Department of the Ghana Police Service. The allegations against the headmaster remain subject to investigation.

items.title: La Bourse de Casablanca clôture en territoire positif
items.description: La Bourse de Casablanca a terminé sur une note positive jeudi, son indice principal, le MASI, gagnant 0,19% à 16.998,93 points (pts). Le MASI 20, qui regroupe les 20 valeurs les plus liquides, a pris 0,29% à 1.233,74 pts, et le MASI ESG, indice des entreprises ayant la meilleure notation ESG selon Moody’s ESG Solutions, a avancé de 0,15% à 1.255,17 pts. Le MASI Mid and Small Cap, reflétant la performance des petites et moyennes entreprises cotées, a augmenté de 0,05% à 1.616,65 pts. Sur le plan sectoriel, les indices « Participation et promotion immobilières » (+3,14%), « Banques » (+0,69%) et « Assurances » (+0,19%) ont signé les meilleures performances. À l'inverse, les secteurs « Sylviculture et papier » (-5,21%), « Chimie » (-2,80%) et « Matériels, logiciels et services informatiques » (-1,40%) ont enregistré les plus fortes baisses. Les échanges ont dépassé 183 millions de dirhams (MDH), réalisés principalement sur le marché central « Actions » et dominés par les transactions sur Attijariwafa bank (20,98 MDH), TGCC (17,91 MDH) et Managem (17,27 MDH). La capitalisation boursière s'est établie à près de 1.000 milliards de dirhams. Aux valeurs individuelles, les plus fortes baisses ont été accusées par Zellidja (-7,67% à 240,05 DH), IB Maroc.com (-6,36% à 50,1 DH), Rebab Company (-5,85% à 88,5 DH), Med Paper (-5,21% à 22,56 DH) et SNEP (-3,24% à 280,5 DH). À l'opposé, Alliances (+3,85% à 351 DH), Douja Prom Addoha (+3,50% à 34,3 DH), CFG Bank (+2,09% à 195 DH), Microdata (+1,33% à 760 DH) et AtlantaSanad (+1,30% à 121 DH) ont affiché les plus fortes progressions. items.title: Chief Justice has designated Achimota Court to handle petroleum diversion cases – NPA CEO
items.description: The Chief Executive Officer of the National Petroleum Authority (NPA), Godwin Edudzi Tamakloe, has disclosed that the Chief Justice has designated the Achimota Court to handle cases involving the diversion of petroleum products. Appearing before the Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee (PAC) hearing on Thursday, October 15, Mr Tamakloe said the NPA had engaged the Chief Justice to secure a specialised court to deal with offences involving petroleum service providers. He said the move followed audit findings and other concerns within the petroleum industry, which required stronger enforcement measures. “A person who diverts petroleum products commits an offence and is liable on summary conviction to a fine not less than 2,500 penalty units and not more than 5,000 penalty units, or to a term of imprisonment not less than two years or five years or both. So one of the things that we have done is to reach out to the Chief Justice for a specialised court to deal with such recalcitrant that is petroleum service providers. “Based on the audit findings and others too, I had to personally go with my team to go and meet the Chief Justice, ask the judiciary to basically give us a court that can deal with industry-specific,” he said. The NPA CEO said the Authority is committed to pursuing offenders and recovering revenues due it. Asked whether the Authority actively pursued such cases, he responded in the affirmative, stressing that “there was a sanctioning mechanism to ensure compliance.” “So I need that money, and I follow it religiously,” he said.

items.title: Philip Nai and friends gear up for bigger seventh Christmas outreach
items.description: Philip Nai and his friends are preparing for the seventh edition of the annual Christmas Eve outreach for underprivileged children, with organisers promising a bigger event this year. Philip Nai, a media practitioner and producer, started the initiative to put smiles on children’s faces. Each year, the event dubbed ‘Philip Nai and Friends’ brings together games, learning, healthcare and opportunities for the children to interact. This year, the children can look forward to health screenings, face painting, dancing competitions, a bouncy castle, health talks and talks by well-known personalities. The aim is to give them an enjoyable day and ensure they leave feeling healthier, more confident and encouraged. The outreach began in December 2020 and has taken place every Christmas Eve since, in different communities across Accra. The team has visited Martey Tsuru Park, Presby Park, East Airport and La, as well as Our God Reigns Ministry International near La Tawala Beach. The organisers have also spent Christmas Eve with children at the cancer unit of the Korle Bu Teaching Hospital. Most recently, they visited the Agblezaa community, where Nana Aba Anamoah and Cwesi Oteng joined them to encourage the children. Beyond the annual outreach, Philip Nai and Friends have also paid school fees, medical bills and other expenses for children in various communities, easing the financial burden on their families. Ahead of the event, Philip Nai said the initiative was driven by the belief that every child deserves love, attention and a chance to be happy. “Every year, we look forward to doing something special for these children. Seeing them smile and enjoy themselves reminds us why we started. This is the seventh edition, and it means a lot to us, so we want to make it even more impactful. We want the children to have fun, feel loved and know that there are people who genuinely care about them,” he said. Philip Nai, Lead Producer at Joy FM, has for years balanced his media work with giving back to society, particularly by supporting children in need. With preparations gathering pace, the organisers are calling on individuals, companies and other well-meaning partners to support the initiative through cash donations, food, products, services or any other contributions they can offer. The venue will be announced soon, with further details expected in the coming weeks. For Philip Nai and Friends, the goal remains unchanged: to put smiles on children’s faces and make a difference in their lives.

items.title: 2027: Obi’s performance in Anambra not enough to defeat APC in Lagos — Former lawmaker
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former Deputy Speaker of the Lagos State House of Assembly, Hon. Kolawole Taiwo, has argued that Peter Obi’s performance as governor of Anambra State cannot be compared with the achievements of successive administrations in Lagos, insisting that the opposition cannot rely on Obi’s record to challenge the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the state. Taiwo stated this while speaking on Vanguard’s Politics Hub, where he discussed the APC’s continued dominance in Lagos and the lessons the party learnt from the 2023 general elections, when its presidential candidate, Bola Tinubu, faced a strong challenge from Obi, who contested under the Labour Party. Reflecting on the APC’s experience in the 2023 elections, Taiwo said the outcome had shocked the party but also made its members more prepared. “We were shocked four years ago but when you are shocked, that makes you a stronger person,” he said. According to him, the factors that contributed to the party’s electoral setback in 2023 were no longer evident in the same way, adding that the APC had taken steps to ensure that its position and account of events were better heard by the public. “What happened four years ago is not happening now. There were some things that led to it (the loss), those things, we are not seeing it again,” Taiwo said. He rejected the suggestion that the Igbo community was responsible for the electoral outcome in Lagos, arguing instead that the result reflected a wider expression of public dissatisfaction, particularly among younger voters. “Some people said it was the Igbos but I said no, it was not the Igbos. The worst part of that tsunami, it was the Gen-Z and everybody that just decided that they think they can just be ruling us anyhow,” he said. Taiwo also said the APC had introduced measures to make its position heard, noting that his appearance on the programme was an opportunity to present the party’s perspective. “We (APC) have also introduced so many things. For instance, people like us coming to talk on this show is because we also want people to hear our own part of the story. The story was one sided,” he said. On Obi’s record in Anambra, the former lawmaker questioned whether it could serve as the basis for challenging the APC’s record in Lagos, insisting that the two states should not be compared without considering their different circumstances. “Obi cannot come here and say, I performed in Anambra. What type of performance is that when you put it beside Lagos? You now say you want to premise your election on your performance in Anambra, then, there is something wrong with us,” Taiwo said. He further argued that governors would have achievements to point to in their respective states, but maintained that Obi’s record in Anambra should not be used as the sole yardstick for judging the APC’s performance in Lagos. “You cannot put his performance in Anambra beside Lagos. Even a blind and deaf governor will have something he has done.” The post 2027: Obi’s performance in Anambra not enough to defeat APC in Lagos — Former lawmaker appeared first on Vanguard News .

GSA strengthens electricity meter testing to protect consumers and improve energy reliability
items.description: The Ghana Standards Authority (GSA) says it is strengthening electricity meter testing, transformer calibration and quality assurance services to improve energy reliability, protect consumers and support Ghana’s transition to clean energy. The Director-General of the GSA, Professor George Agyei, said accurate measurement and the testing of energy equipment were essential to achieving Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) Seven, which sought to ensure access to affordable, reliable, sustainable and modern energy for all. He was speaking at the 2026 World Standards Day Grand Durbar held at the Takoradi Technical University on the theme: “ Shared Vision for a Better World – Spotlight on SDG 7: Affordable and Clean Energy .” Prof. Agyei said some energy challenges attributed to inadequate supply could also result from failures in standards, including inaccurate electricity meters, faulty transformers and substandard solar panels. “Energy can only be affordable when it is measured accurately. It can only be reliable when equipment is tested. It can only be clean when the technology we import and manufacture meets verified performance requirements,” he said. He announced that Takoradi was one of three national electricity meter testing centres, alongside Accra and Kumasi, to ensure that consumers in the Western Region benefited from the programme. He said under the National Electricity Meter Testing Programme, every electricity meter installed in Ghana was required to be tested and certified by the GSA. The service is free to the public and financed by the Government, but compulsory under the Standards Authority Act, 2022 (Act 1078), he said. Prof. Agyei added that meters already in service were required to comply with the applicable requirements by December 31, 2028. He said the Authority was also advancing plans for a National Transformer Testing and Calibration Centre to ensure that transformers supplying electricity to homes and industries were tested against international standards before failures occurred. The facility would be developed in line with relevant International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) standards and ISO/IEC 17025 requirements for testing and calibration laboratories. On service delivery, Prof. Agyei said the GSA’s 24-Hour Services Directorate would provide testing, inspection, certification, calibration and verification services around the clock. He said the initiative would support the Government’s 24-Hour Economy agenda by enabling ports, factories and exporters to access quality assurance services without unnecessary delays. “Ghana’s 24-Hour Economy cannot run on eight-hour quality services,” he said. Prof. Agyei called for stronger collaboration among regulatory agencies, industry and other stakeholders, stressing that standards were essential for building public confidence in products and services. He urged industry players to view compliance as an investment rather than a cost, describing it as a requirement for accessing markets and improving competitiveness. He also encouraged students to pursue careers in engineering, metrology and standards development to support the future of clean energy and industrial growth. Touching on Ghana’s role in regional standardisation, Prof. Agyei announced that the country would host the 33rd General Assembly of the African Organisation for Standardisation (ARSO) in Accra in July 2027. The assembly would coincide with ARSO’s Golden Jubilee, marking 50 years since the organisation was established in Accra in 1977. He said Ghana was committed to contributing to Africa’s standards development, particularly under the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), to facilitate trade and improve upon the competitiveness of African products. As part of activities marking the celebration, participants were expected to witness the commissioning of the GSA’s new Concrete and Ceramic Tiles Laboratory. The laboratory is expected to strengthen quality assurance for building materials and provide additional protection for builders, homeowners and other users. Prof. Agyei said standards often went unnoticed when they worked effectively but could have serious consequences for consumers, businesses and the economy when they failed. He called on stakeholders to support the Authority’s efforts to uphold quality and safety, saying the GSA’s motto, “We Set the Standard,” required collective commitment to ensure that products and services met established requirements. Omanhene of Essikado Traditional Area, Nana Kobina Nketsia V, said World Standards Day should be a reflection of how far the country had entrenched standards that secured the future of the country-human and material resources in focus. Some participants, however, questioned the standards on energy drinks, foods in second-cycle institutions, and the need to ban the use of unapproved chemicals in food and other beverages to reduce the growing incidence of non-communicable diseases.

‘Dismissed or suspended? Ghanaians deserve clarity’ – NPP demands clarity on Ampofo Ankrah’s fate
items.description: The New Patriotic Party (NPP) has called on the Presidency to clarify the employment status of National Sports Authority (NSA) Director-General Yaw Ampofo Ankrah amid conflicting accounts of whether he has been dismissed or suspended over the alleged 2026 FIFA World Cup visa scandal. The party’s Director of Communications, Dennis Miracles Aboagye, said the government must make a clear public statement on the decision and disclose the terms of any action taken against the NSA chief. Speaking at a press conference on Thursday, October 15, Mr Aboagye questioned the delay in the government’s response to the allegations, arguing that the President acted only after pressure from the public and the Minority in Parliament. He said a petition had been submitted to the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) on September 8, but President John Dramani Mahama did not act on Mr Ampofo Ankrah until October 1, when calls for the NSA Director-General’s removal had intensified. Mr Aboagye said the timeline raised questions about the government’s commitment to accountability and transparency, particularly when allegations involving a senior public official were concerned. He also questioned the lack of consistency in official accounts of the decision against Mr Ampofo Ankrah, saying it remained unclear whether the NSA Director-General had been removed from office or temporarily suspended while investigations continued. “Some official account says that the National Sports Authority Director General, Mr Ampofo Ankrah, has been dismissed. Others say he was suspended pending investigation. Which is which? Ghanaians deserve a clear statement from the Presidency,” he said. Mr Aboagye further called on the Presidency to publish the letter communicating the decision to Mr Ampofo Ankrah to establish the precise nature of the action taken against him. He said the government should explain the conditions attached to the decision, including whether the NSA Director-General had been dismissed outright or asked to step aside pending the outcome of investigations. items.title: Tears, looting as Army evicts civilians from Effurun barracks
items.description: By Jimitota Onoyume, Assistant News Editor About one million civilian residents and traders at the Mammy area of the Nigerian Army barracks in Effurun, Uvwie Local Government Area, Delta State, have been evicted, their shops and buildings demolished. Read Also: Toluwanisings was rushed to 8 hospitals before death – PA Some of the victims. The distraught residents and traders, who spoke to Vanguard, alleged that they were ordered to vacate the premises within three days, leaving them with little time to secure alternative accommodation and business locations. Some even said they had just 24 hours notices from the barracks authorities. According to the residents they were initially assured that the eviction notice affected only hotel operators, and that those living and doing business in other parts of the barracks would not be affected. They said they were, therefore, shocked on Wednesday when soldiers in patrol vehicles began announcing that all civilians must leave the premises, declaring that there would be “no more Mammy Market anymore”. “Initially, they told us that only hotels had been asked to leave and that those of us living here were not the target. They brought a bulldozer on Monday, and we saw them demolish only one hotel in the barracks. “This gave us peace of mind. “But by Wednesday morning, we saw soldiers shouting, ‘No Mammy again, no Mammy again,’ and ordering all of us to move,” a resident, Mama Iyabo, said. An Igbo businessman, who operated a popular beer parlour with the name Chief Judge, said his business premises were demolished on Wednesday after he was given little time to remove his belongings. He said his father had allegedly acquired the land more than 20 years ago and operated the business until his death a few years back, after which he (Chief Judge) took over. “I continued after my father passed on. We have been here for as long as I can remember. I never imagined this kind of disaster would happen to me. “They came and ordered us to move our things before 5 p.m. They demolished my business premises,” he said. The businessman alleged that three air conditioners, plasma television sets and other valuables were stolen while he struggled to evacuate his belongings ahead of the demolition. “I lost over N10 million. I don’t know where to begin. I couldn’t carry all my things under such a condition,” he lamented. “ We pay N3,500 yearly for ID, N500 for pass – Miracle Another resident, Odige Miracle, said his brother operated a boutique and a canopy-rental business in the area but lost valuable items because they were not given adequate time to move out. According to him, occupants paid N3,500 annually for verification cards, in addition to N500 on the last Saturday of every month for access to the Mammy. “They just told us to move within 24 hours. We couldn’t take many of our belongings. My brother operated a boutique and did canopy business here. We have lost so much. “The government and the Army command should help us with funds to start afresh,” he pleaded. Traders operating along the Effurun-Sapele Road section of the Mammy Market were also ordered to leave. Many of them told Vanguard that they started dismantling their makeshift shops on Wednesday evening after receiving the order to vacate the area. “We still don’t know why the Army suddenly came for us too,” some of the traders said. They were seen struggling to salvage goods and other belongings as bulldozers pulled down their shops. Some traders collapsed Vanguard gathered that some traders reportedly collapsed after seeing the bulldozers approaching to carry out the demolition. “Some of us had already started stocking goods for Christmas because we usually buy things early ahead of the festive season. And some customers start shopping early for Christmas.You can see the extent of our losses,” a trader said. The traders alleged that they had paid to secure the spaces where they erected their shops and regularly paid various charges to the barracks leadership through intermediaries. “It was not as if we just moved into this place and started selling. We paid for the spaces we occupy and also pay service charges regularly to do business here,” they said. A restaurant operator, Madam Eno, said she had operated her restaurant built with blocks along the Warri-Sapele Road section of the market for more than 10 years before it was demolished. She said she could only salvage the roofing sheets and some of the wood from the building. Many of the affected residents and traders wept as they recounted their losses, saying they do not know how to start afresh amid the soaring cost of accommodation and commercial premises in Warri and Effurun. They appealed for assistance. Army mum At press time, the Army had yet to respond to the allegations, as efforts to reach its officials for comments were unsuccessful. The demolition continued on Thursday, with household items and other belongings scattered across the affected areas. Residents and traders were seen scrambling to secure vehicles to evacuate the few valuables they managed to salvage. Meanwhile, Brigadier-General Ibrahim Baba Buhari recently assumed duty as Commander of the 63 Brigade of the Nigerian Army in Asaba, Delta State. The brigade oversees operations at the 33 Battalion in Effurun. Vanguard News The post Tears, looting as Army evicts civilians from Effurun barracks appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Teach consent and sexual boundaries from pre-school to prevent abuse – Gender advocate
items.description: Educator and gender advocate, Dr Abena Nyarkoa, has called for education on sexual consent from the basic school level to help combat sexual abuse in schools. Speaking on JoyNews’ The Pulse on Thursday, October 15, she said educating children about consent should form part of efforts to protect them from abuse. According to her, “I am saying that education on sexual consent and sexual boundaries is very important right from pre-schools; we need to teach children about self-autonomy, about boundaries.” Her comments came during a discussion on allegations of sexual abuse involving the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School and female students. Dr Nyarkoa also urged parents to maintain close communication with their children and create opportunities for them to discuss sensitive issues. She stressed the importance of parental involvement in efforts to address sexual abuse, alongside education and accountability within schools. “We need to involve parents as well. Parents must have a conversation with their children. If a teacher is overly friendly, why? Parents need to talk to their children about this,” she said. The gender advocate further called for a designated female officer to serve as a coach and mentor for girls, offering guidance and someone they could approach with concerns. “There should also be a safeguarding officer and preferably a woman on site so that girls can talk to them,” she suggested. She said these measures should be supported by clear policies for handling allegations and action against those found responsible. Dr Nyarkoa had earlier warned that the failure to hold perpetrators accountable was contributing to the normalisation of sexual abuse in schools.

items.title: L'Arabie saoudite accuse l'Iran de continuer à armer les Houthis au Yémen
items.description: L'Arabie Saoudite, a accusé, jeudi, l'Iran de continuer à armer, former et soutenir les Houthis au Yémen. Pour Ryad, la récente « escalade avec les Houthis est encouragée par l'Iran ». Le vice-ministre saoudien chargé de la diplomatie, Rayed Krimly, a accusé jeudi Téhéran d'être derrière la récente intensification du conflit entre les Houthis pro-iraniens du Yémen et les troupes gouvernementales appuyées par Ryad. « Nous pensons que l'escalade engagée par les Houthis à ce stade le plus récent du conflit est encouragée par l'Iran », a-t-il déclaré au cours d'un point de presse en ligne, affirmant que Téhéran continuait « d'armer, entraîner et soutenir » le mouvement, « en violation des résolutions du Conseil de sécurité de l'ONU ». Le responsable a cependant assuré que Ryad restait en contact direct avec Téhéran, même si « d'une manière générale, il ne semble pas que les Iraniens soient en mesure de faire les concessions nécessaires à une solution ». Il a aussi accusé les Houthis d'avoir refusé une rencontre proposée à Oman ces dernières semaines, alors que les attaques se sont multipliées de part et d'autre pendant cette période. « Au début de cette escalade, nous leur avons proposé de les rencontrer à Mascate mais ils ont refusé. C'est la dernière communication que nous avons eue avec eux, il y a quelques semaines », a-t-il dit. L'Arabie saoudite, premier pays exportateur de pétrole au monde, subit depuis plusieurs jours des attaques répétées, avec notamment samedi une frappe meurtrière contre l'aéroport international de Ryad. L'ampleur de ces attaques est inédite depuis le début en 2014 de la guerre au Yémen opposant les Houthis aux forces gouvernementales, qui bénéficient du soutien militaire d'une coalition conduite par l'Arabie saoudite depuis 2015. Après quatre ans de trêve, le conflit a repris en juillet, ouvrant un nouveau front de la guerre au Moyen-Orient. En septembre, les Houthis ont pris le littoral yéménite sur la mer Rouge, renforçant leur emprise sur le détroit de Bab el-Mandeb, stratégique pour l'accès au canal de Suez. Ce conflit, dans l'un des pays les plus pauvres du monde, a provoqué selon l'ONU l'une des pires crises humanitaires, la plus grande partie de la population yéménite dépendant désormais de l'aide internationale. The post L'Arabie saoudite accuse l'Iran de continuer à armer les Houthis au Yémen appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Accord sur le diesel : Lavrov accuse Zelensky de défier ouvertement Trump
items.description: a l'issue du VIIe sommet de la Conference pour l'interaction et les mesures de confiance en Asie (CICA), le 15 octobre, le ministre russe des Affaires etrangeres Sergueï Lavrov a denonce la volonte de Kiev de poursuivre les frappes contre les raffineries russes. Pour le ministre, l'attitude du dirigeant ukrainien Volodymyr Zelensky face a l'accord sur le diesel conclu entre Moscou et Washington temoigne de son refus de toute demarche constructive. Kiev refuse de renoncer aux frappes Lavrov a affirme que Moscou avait accepte la proposition americaine, tandis que Zelensky reclamait des missiles pour les systemes Patriot : « L'accord a ete propose, nous l'avons accepte, mais Zelensky a declare a plusieurs reprises qu'on ne vienne pas l'importuner avec cet accord sur le diesel, mais qu'on lui donne plutot des missiles pour le systeme Patriot afin de continuer a frapper le secteur energetique russe, notamment les raffineries de petrole. » Le meme jour, Zelensky a annonce au Financial Times la reprise des frappes visant les raffineries russes, suspendues pendant quelques jours. Il a invoque les attaques contre le reseau energetique ukrainien. Le president americain Donald Trump avait demande a Kiev d'y renoncer, les considerant comme l'une des causes de la hausse des prix du diesel. Selon le chef de la diplomatie russe, cette attitude revient a defier ouvertement le president americain : « Il est desormais clair pour tout le monde qu'il s'agit d'un defi sans detour et grossier lance au president Trump, qui a activement soutenu cet accord et s'est exprime publiquement a son sujet a plusieurs reprises. » Un accord entre Moscou et Washington L'accord remonte a l'entretien telephonique du 9 octobre entre le president russe Vladimir Poutine et Donald Trump . Il prevoit des livraisons de diesel russe aux marches americain et mondial pour contenir les prix. Washington a accorde une derogation aux sanctions jusqu'au 7 avril 2027. Moscou prevoit de livrer 300 000 tonnes de diesel en octobre, 500 000 en novembre et jusqu'a un million en decembre. Selon le vice-Premier ministre russe Alexandre Novak, les exportations pourraient ensuite atteindre trois millions de tonnes par mois, sans affecter l'approvisionnement du marche interieur. L'accord a accentue les tensions avec Kiev. Selon le Financial Times , la delegation ukrainienne a ecourte ses discussions a Miami . Trump a de son cote critique Zelensky en demandant a l'Ukraine de se choisir un nouveau dirigeant . Lavrov estime que Kiev refuse tout compromis : « Zelensky considere que le monde entier lui est redevable, alors qu'il n'a aucune obligation envers personne. Et il n'est pret a entreprendre aucune demarche constructive qui serait veritablement honnete et equitable. » Le ministre a reaffirme que Moscou restait ouvert a des negociations honnetes et equilibrees, mais refusait qu'une simple pause des combats serve a rearmer les forces ukrainiennes.

items.title: Mali : les femmes rurales face aux difficultés d’accès au financement
items.description: Le Mali a celebre, ce jeudi 15 octobre, la journee internationale de la femme rurale, placee cette annee sous le theme : « Femme agricultrice : actrice incontournable dans un systeme resilient face aux defis du changement climatique ». Si cette journee met en lumiere la contribution des femmes a l'agriculture, l'acces au financement demeure un obstacle au developpement de leurs activites. a Sikasso et a Bankass, des femmes temoignent des difficultes rencontrees et des solutions mises en place pour y faire face. a Sikasso, les conditions d'octroi de credits bancaires compliquent les activites des femmes transformatrices de produits agricoles. Face a cette situation, certaines ont choisi de s'organiser en cooperatives pour financer leurs projets. Fanta Diamoutene, transformatrice de produits agricoles, explique que les prets accordes par les banques ne couvrent pas toujours les besoins exprimes. « Quand tu demandes un pret, tu n'obtiens pas l'integralite du montant », deplore-t-elle. Pour contourner cette difficulte, elle et d'autres femmes ont cree une cooperative dotee d'une caisse d'epargne et de credit. Le principe consiste a accorder des prets aux membres, qui remboursent ensuite les sommes empruntees avec des interets. « Par exemple, si une personne emprunte 5 000 F dans notre caisse d'epargne, elle doit rembourser au bout de trois mois en ajoutant 750 F », precise Fanta Diamoutene. Les interets ainsi collectes permettent de renforcer progressivement le fonds et de financer les besoins d'autres membres. Espoir d'une autonomie financiere a Bankass, Mariam Dougnon, commercante, a beneficie de l'appui financier d'une ONG. Ce soutien lui a permis d'acquerir du materiel et de renforcer les moyens de son entreprise. Grâce a ce financement, elle a notamment achete un mini-moulin et une decortiqueuse d'arachides. Elle a egalement consacre une partie de l'argent a son fonds de roulement. « Autrefois, c'etaient les femmes qui decortiquaient l'arachide a la main. Mais depuis que j'ai obtenu ce financement, j'ai achete une decortiqueuse et j'ai utilise le reste de l'argent comme fonds de roulement. J'en ai vraiment tire profit », temoigne-t-elle. Aujourd'hui, Mariam Dougnon nourrit l'ambition de developper davantage son activite et de diriger, a terme, une grande entreprise. Des credits adaptes aux besoins des femmes Malgre les initiatives individuelles et collectives, l'acces au financement reste un enjeu pour les femmes rurales qui souhaitent developper durablement leurs activites agricoles et commerciales. Les groupements feminins plaident ainsi pour la mise en place de lignes de credit adaptees a leurs besoins et a leurs capacites de remboursement. Selon des associations feminines, un meilleur acces aux financements pourrait leur permettre de renforcer leurs equipements, d'accroître leur production et de consolider leurs activites. Lire aussi : Mali : l'acces des femmes aux terres agricoles reste un defi L’article Mali : les femmes rurales face aux difficultés d’accès au financement est apparu en premier sur Studio Tamani - Informations, débats, magazines : toute l’actualité du Mali, en 5 langues .

items.description: Le Camarade Premier ministre, Chef du Gouvernement, Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, a reçu en audience, ce jeudi 15 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou, une délégation de la Société de cardiologie du Burkina (SO.CAR.B), conduite par son président, le Professeur Nobila Valentin Yaméogo. La délégation est venue lui présenter les objectifs du 9ᵉ Congrès scientifique de la SO.CAR.B, couplé au 4ᵉ Congrès de l’Association des Sociétés de cardiologie d’Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre (ASCAOC), qui se tiendront du 28 au 30 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou. ‎ ‎Placée sous le thème « Cœur et nutrition », cette rencontre mettra l’accent sur le rôle de l’alimentation dans la prévention des maladies cardiovasculaires. À sa sortie d’audience, le Professeur Yaméogo a expliqué que le choix de cette thématique répond à la progression de ces pathologies et à la nécessité de mieux informer les populations sur les habitudes alimentaires favorables à leur santé. ‎ ‎« Le thème “Cœur et nutrition” va nous permettre de faire de la prévention cardiovasculaire, de promouvoir une meilleure prise en charge des maladies cardiovasculaires et de transmettre des informations capitales à nos populations, afin que manger ne soit pas une source de maladie », a-t-il souligné. ‎ ‎Les échanges ont également porté sur la valorisation des produits locaux. Pour le président de la SO.CAR.B, une alimentation saine peut s’appuyer sur des denrées produites localement et accessibles aux populations, en cohérence avec les orientations nationales en matière de souveraineté alimentaire. ‎ ‎Le Chef du Gouvernement a, dans ce sens, souligné l’intérêt d’une alimentation simple et adaptée aux réalités locales. « Parfois, la bonne santé se trouve dans la simplicité. On peut manger simplement ce que nous produisons et être en bonne santé », a-t-il déclaré. Il a ainsi insisté sur l’importance d’associer la promotion des produits locaux à l’adoption de bonnes habitudes alimentaires. ‎ ‎Prévu à l’hôtel Azalaï de Ouagadougou, ce rendez-vous scientifique devrait réunir près de 500 participants. Des spécialistes du Burkina Faso, d’autres pays africains et d’autres régions du monde sont attendus pour partager leurs expériences et échanger sur les avancées scientifiques dans le domaine cardiovasculaire. ‎ ‎En amont du congrès, des activités de formation, d’information et de dépistage sont prévues au CHU de Bogodogo, au CHU de Tengandogo et au CHU Yalgado-Ouédraogo. ‎ ‎Le CHU de Bogodogo accueillera notamment un enseignement technique consacré à l’échographie, pour l’exploration de certaines anomalies des artères cérébrales. Des sessions de formation sur l’hypertension artérielle associée à la grossesse seront, quant à elles, organisées dans les trois CHU. ‎ ‎À travers ce programme, la SO.CAR.B entend renforcer les compétences des professionnels de santé et améliorer le dépistage ainsi que la prise en charge des maladies cardiovasculaires, tout en donnant aux populations les moyens de mieux les prévenir. ‎ ‎𝐃𝐂𝐑𝐏/𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞

items.title: Zonda Tec launches HOWO T3M truck to support agric and logistics
items.description: Zonda Tec Ghana Limited, the official partner of Sinotruk in Ghana, has launched the HOWO T3M light-duty truck, designed to combine the flexibility of light commercial vehicles with heavy-duty capabilities. The new truck range is expected to support businesses across agriculture, retail, logistics and distribution, with different payload capacities to meet varying transportation needs. Chief Executive Officer of Zonda Tec Ghana Limited, Yang Yang, says Ghana must move beyond trading and invest more in engineering and local manufacturing to create jobs and build a competitive industrial economy. She believes developing local engineering capacity will enable the country to manufacture products for export to neighbouring countries and international markets. “Me, Madam Yang, as the CEO of Zonda, I strongly advocate. We need to shift from trading to engineering,” she said. She explained that the company’s local vehicle assembly operations are already contributing to skills development through the training of Ghanaian engineers by technical experts from Sinotruk. She said the initiative goes beyond providing employment, as it is also intended to address the skills gap in Ghana’s automotive engineering industry. “I really want to advocate to our government to support the engineering, especially the auto engineering industry in Ghana, because we are full of not only mineral resources, we are also full of human resources,” she stated. She added that investing in young engineers could create opportunities for them to work in neighbouring countries where technical expertise is increasingly needed. Yang Yang also called on government institutions, agricultural organisations, logistics providers and private businesses to support local assembly and strengthen Ghana’s transportation network. Meanwhile, Chief Representative of Sinotruk in Ghana, Mr Lu, said the partnership with Zonda Tec has evolved significantly since the two companies began working together. He noted that the collaboration, which initially focused on vehicle distribution, has expanded into local assembly of commercial vehicles. According to him, Sinotruk began assembling heavy-duty trucks in Ghana in 2019 before expanding its production capacity in 2023 in response to growing market demand. The company has since further expanded its facilities to accommodate the assembly of light-duty trucks. Also speaking at the launch, a Sinotruk representative, Samuel Mo, said the HOWO T3M was developed to respond to the transportation demands and operating conditions of the Ghanaian market. He explained that the vehicle incorporates heavy-duty engineering experience to provide durability, comfort and reliability, particularly for businesses operating under challenging road and loading conditions. The launch adds to Zonda Tec Ghana’s growing range of commercial vehicles and reinforces the company’s ambition to contribute to local automotive manufacturing, technical skills development and job creation.
