items.title: Infantino not fit to lead FIFA unless… – English FA chief
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye FIFA President Gianni Infantino has apologised to the FIFA Council for his World Cup sell-off plan but has been told he is not fit to lead world football’s governing body unless he releases documents relating to a controversial World Cup commercial rights proposal and answers questions surrounding the deal. Debbie Hewitt, chair of the English Football Association and a FIFA vice-president, said Infantino apologised to the FIFA Council over the abandoned FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal but failed to provide answers to key questions during a meeting in Zurich on Thursday. The proposal, which Infantino scrapped within days of its emergence, would have transferred a portion of FIFA’s commercial rights to a private investment firm. According to the BBC, the FIFA Council meeting lasted three and a half hours, with members also questioning Infantino over the suspended red-card ban handed to United States striker Folarin Balogun, the FIFA Peace Prize awarded to US President Donald Trump and funding for national football associations. Hewitt said the meeting was unusually frank but left several important questions unresolved, including requests for documents relating to the FFE proposal. “One of the disappointing things is that we didn’t get answers to anything that we had specifically requested — for example, getting the papers from FFE,” she said. “I think the man has to answer those questions and if he doesn’t answer those questions now, he’s not fit to be FIFA president — and that was what was shared in the meeting.” Hewitt said Infantino’s apology amounted largely to regret over failing to present the proposal to the Council rather than a full explanation of what happened. “What he really apologised for was not bringing it to the Council. If you regret it that deeply, share it with us,” she added. She said the documents were necessary to determine whether those involved in the proposal could be trusted and whether further action, including possible criminal proceedings, was warranted. UEFA, European football’s governing body, has been among Infantino’s strongest critics. It has prepared criminal legal proceedings against him and filed claims in three United States courts seeking the release of documents relating to the FFE proposal. Asked whether her position on Infantino had changed following Thursday’s meeting, Hewitt said she had received no new information that would alter her view, apart from the president’s apology. “From my position, nothing has shifted. I’ve no new information that makes me feel any differently, other than we do have a president who is apologetic,” she said. Infantino faces criticism over Balogun ban, Peace Prize The suspended ban imposed on Balogun after his red card at the 2026 FIFA World Cup was another major issue raised at the meeting. The suspension followed a request by US President Donald Trump for the decision to be reviewed. The BBC reported that a proposal was presented to the Council to amend FIFA’s disciplinary code to prevent a repeat, with the proposed changes stating that the disciplinary committee could not suspend an automatic one-match ban for a red card. Hewitt said the decision, alongside the FFE proposal, had damaged football’s reputation. “What happened in July did not serve football… whether it’s the Balogun case, the FFE case… the reputation of football was put under serious threat,” she said. “Once behaviour starts to influence what happens on the pitch, then I think it’s a dark day for football and a number of people said that in the room.” The FIFA Peace Prize awarded to Trump also came under scrutiny, with the Council discussing how the award was conceived, who authorised it and whether it should be withdrawn or reformed. Hewitt said FIFA’s social committee would investigate the circumstances surrounding the award and present its recommendations to the Council in December. She also criticised Infantino’s engagement with political figures and other dignitaries, arguing that football’s governing body should prioritise its 211 member associations. “When he puts other dignitaries in front of his 211 associations, then he’s lost what football is about,” she said. Infantino to seek third term Infantino is expected to stand for a third term as FIFA president in March 2027, but opposition figures have yet to produce a credible challenger. Former Tottenham Hotspur and Switzerland defender Ramon Vega has declared his intention to contest the election, although his chances of securing the required support from member associations remain uncertain. Some senior figures in European football have also called for former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger to challenge Infantino, but it remains unclear whether Wenger would be willing to enter the race. Candidates must secure the backing of five FIFA member associations, with the deadline for nominations set for November 18. Hewitt said it was important for FIFA members to have a choice in the election, noting that Infantino was re-elected unopposed in 2019 and 2023. “I think it’s important to Gianni to have somebody who stands with a different manifesto, and good for FIFA to have that choice,” she said. She added that a prospective challenger should put football first, unite the global game and demonstrate the courage to introduce reforms. The FIFA Council is expected to consider the findings of the Peace Prize investigation in December, as pressure mounts on Infantino to provide greater transparency over the decisions that have drawn criticism from members of the governing body. The post Infantino not fit to lead FIFA unless… – English FA chief appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Joint sitting of Parliament endorses emergency, governor's rule in KP amid opposition outcry
items.description: ISLAMABAD: A joint sitting of Parliament on Thursday gave its approval to the Centre’s imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa amid a strong protest from the opposition. The joint session had been summoned to discuss separate resolutions on the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in KP, where the opposition’s PTI was in power. During the session, which was addressed by both members of the treasury and opposition benches, the government justified its decision while the PTI lambasted the Centre and the allegations levelled against the party. The Centre took the measures on Oct 11, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. The move followed weeks of political tensions between the Centre and the PTI — as well as negotiations to bridge their differences — after the latter announced a long march to Islamabad to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan. During Thursday’s joint sitting, opposition members turned up carrying placards inscribed with slogans, such as “emergency na manzoor (emergency is unacceptable)”. PM Shehbaz, who attended part of the session, shook hands with opposition leaders of both the Senate and the NA, pictures and footage showed. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry tabled the two proclamations and separate resolutions regarding the emergency and governor’s rule. After hours-long debate, NA Speaker Ayaz Sadiq put the two resolutions to a vote, while opposition members chanted “emergency unacceptable”. The resolutions approving emergency and governor’s rule were then passed. At the outset of the proceedings, Chaudhry also presented a motion under Rule 232 of the Parliament (Joint Sitting) Rules 1973 to suspend certain sub-rules so he could move the resolutions. As loud noes echoed and opposition members chanted “emergency na manzoor ”, the speaker again put the motion to a vote by asking the members to stand up, which was then adopted with 214-56 votes. Subsequently, Chaudhry moved two resolutions before the joint sitting — one for approving the Proclamation of Emergency under Article 232 and the second for the proclamation of governor’s rule under Article 234. Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar then opened the discussion on the two resolutions and said members of the treasury benches were ready to reply to any query raised by the opposition. Explaining the constitutional process to approve the resolution for emergency, he said the joint sitting could reject it by a total majority, ie 51 per cent. Similarly, the resolution for governor’s rule also required a total majority of votes for approval. The joint sitting also offered prayers for the lives lost, mostly of children, in a roof collapse in Peshawar. The joint session took place a day after both Houses of Parliament, in separate sittings, passed resolutions endorsing the imposition of emergency in KP. According to Article 232 , if the “president acts on his own, the Proclamation of Emergency shall be placed” before both Houses of the Parliament for approval by each House within 10 days. Meanwhile, a proclamation for governor’s rule issued under Article 234 “shall be laid before a joint sitting and shall cease to be in force at the expiration of two months”, unless a joint sitting approves its extension. However, such a measure shall not remain in force for more than six months. Naqvi notes ‘clear stance’ of PTI lawmakers Speaking during Thursday’s joint sitting, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi urged the opposition to stick to facts when recounting the dialogue held with the government, asserting that the Centre had “no option left” but to impose emergency and governor’s rule in KP. “By God, our hearts did not want to do this,” Naqvi remarked, adding that the treasury members were trying their best so that the measures were not taken in KP. “I will request only that you let facts remain facts. […] We had no option left, after which we did this and you will definitely oppose it, but we should consider the facts,” the minister said as he sought to provide a “clarification” on the allegations levelled by the opposition. “Please do not say that we misused terrorism.” He also refuted what he said was the opposition’s stance that the government delegation left the talks. “We did not get up and leave […] we did not even urge you to hurry up.” Naqvi, who was part of the government’s delegation during the Oct 3 talks , emphasised: “We tried until the last minute […] It was our effort until the last hour that this (emergency/governor’s rule) is not imposed.” The minister said the federal government offered its KP counterpart to declare emergency in “12 districts, on which you said fine, let’s do it”. He claimed that PTI’s Asad Qaiser, who was present during the talks, was willing to sign an agreement, but he advised the latter to consult the KP government first. Pointing towards the opposition benches, Naqvi affirmed that the government was not levelling allegations against them. “I vouch for those sitting here that you were not even a single step behind on [countering] terrorism,” he added. The minister referred to a video clip — later sharing it on his X account — in which KP Information Minister Shafi Jan was asked to declare that the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) was a terrorist group. “Those individuals in the TTP who are against the state are terrorists,” Jan responded. Addressing the opposition members, Naqvi further said: “I believe that you, and those we spoke to, particularly Asad Qaiser sahib, as he responded on [the issue] of terrorism that day, I guarantee that even we were not thinking of the things they were speaking on.” He went on to acknowledge that all those present in the meeting “had an absolutely clear stance [on terrorism] that we will do this for Pakistan”. The interior minister, holding a paper, said he suggested to even exclude a term about the PTI calling off its long march, but PPP Vice President Sherry Rehman insisted on keeping it. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi holds a paper during a joint sitting of Parliament on Thursday. — screengrab via DawnNewsTV Naqvi noted that Sohail Afridi, the KP chief minister whose role is now non-functional, had not gone to the site of “even a single operation with the army and only used to say ‘I cannot afford this politically’”. The minister recalled his efforts to sort out differences between the Centre and KP, such as meetings between Afridi and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on the issue of provincial funds. While saying he did not deem it appropriate to speak about Afridi in his absence, Naqvi claimed he and the PTI leader had discussed a plan to strengthen police forces in five KP districts. He said the federal government wanted a meeting of the provincial apex committee to be held. “A press release had to be issued, which would state that we will fight against terrorism together. You can ask for that press release, what was written in it and what happened; everything is before you.” He recalled that some personnel were martyred in an attack “the same day”, adding that it took place in February. “We requested the CM sahib and took him to the funerals with us. That was the last day when CM KP attended the funeral of any army officer or jawaan (soldier),” he added. The minister concluded his speech by reaffirming the Centre’s determination to fight the wave of terrorism. He said the fight could not be waged on “under two [different] policies” of the federation and the province. He urged the PTI to hold discussions with the KP government on what matters were wrong, adding: “No political party should be accused of terrorism. This is a major thing. But if something has happened, it should be fixed.” Gohar objects to allegations of ‘backing terrorists’ Speaking on the Parliament’s floor, PTI interim chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan said the country was going through a “very fragile situation”. He lamented that the KP government was accused of “backing terrorists”. “The prime minister has alleged that we are supporting terrorists. We are disappointed to hear that. You have to apologise to the entire population of KP and us,” he said. “Prime minister, you have given a message to the entire world that one of the federating units of the country was backing terrorists,“ Gohar added. He highlighted that the opposition stood with the government during a war with India. “But today we are called supporters of terrorists,” he regretted. Barrister Gohar rejected the proclamation of emergency and declared that the PTI will make the country stronger and eradicate terrorism when it comes into power again. He also rejected the government’s claims that PTI leaders did not attend funerals of martyrs, recalling that he himself had attended multiple funerals in KP. Gohar said the PTI was willing to engage in dialogue with the government provided that its demands were met. He lamented that speeches of opposition members were not shown in the media. Speaking to the media at Parliament after the session, Gohar again condemned the move to impose the emergency and governor’s rule in KP. He noted that the production orders for two detained opposition MNAs — Sanaullah Khan Masti Khel and Dawar Khan Kundi — were issued on Wednesday, yet they were not brought to Parliament during the joint session. Gohar said by removing the PTI from power in KP would not affect the party’s popularity as “its strength is the public”. But, he continued, “we condemn the illegal and unconstitutional dismissal of a provincial government. We will raise our voice against it at every forum”. He then condemned terrorism, responding the federal government’s allegations that the PTI supported terrorism. He warned that accusing a provincial government of supporting terrorism would have “serious implications for Pakistan” internationally. The PTI chairperson added that the prime minister had made a “mistake by making a political statement in a federal cabinet that a provincial government was supporting terrorism”. “Don’t politicise the issue of terrorism,” Barrister Gohar urged. “Do not put the nation and the federation at stake for the sake of your narrative. This (terrorism) is not just an issue for a province or the federation. Rather, it was a state-level issue. Time will prove that your decision was political,” he added. He also rejected the allegations that the PTI was the reason behind the breakdown of talks with the government ahead of the imposition of governor’s rule in KP. Dar defends ‘difficult decision’ During the joint session, speaking towards the end of the debate, Deputy PM and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar defended the federal government’s “difficult decision” to impose emergency and governor’s rule in KP. Dar said that the decision was “categorically” in accordance with the Constitution and appealed to the opposition “not to misinterpret or misquote facts” to save personal politics. “Let me remind you of the history,” he said, saying that the menace of terrorism emerged after the 2014 Army Public School attack in Peshawar. The PML-N leader recalled that a multi-party moot was held following the attack, with PTI in attendance and on board with the counterterrorism decisions, including the National Action Plan (NAP). The deputy premier recalled that Operation Zarb-i-Azb and Operation Raddul Fasaad were launched against terrorists, adding that data showed their activities had “ended after the operations”. “We all are Pakistanis […], but we all have the clarity in our minds regarding the facts,” Dar emphasised. Referring to the opposition, Dar said he could see the PTI was against terrorism, but asked who those “few” were who he alleged opened the borders and let the terrorists enter Pakistan. “There are a few individuals in the party (PTI) who are responsible for the terrorism reaching its peak,” he claimed. “For how long will we keep repeating the same mistakes due to our petty politics and some individuals?” he asked. On political reconciliation, Dar said that the menace of terrorism should be dealt with before any other matter. “If not now, then when?” He also criticised Afridi for holding mobilisation campaigns across Pakistan while his province reeled from the threat of terrorism. Dar contended that the province had “collapsed in terms of governance”. Referring to the federal cabinet’s Oct 11 meeting in which the decision was made to impose emergency and governor’s rule in KP, Dar said that PM Shehbaz left the meeting by saying “it’s now or never” to deal with the deteriorating security situation. Achakzai blames ‘faulty decisions’ Speaking in the Parliament, NA Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai blamed “faulty decisions” of the country’s rulers for the current situation. He enquired about the whereabouts of Afridi, who was reported to be in preventative custody . Achakzai, who leads the opposition alliance Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-i-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP), accused PML-N’s Sadiq of not running the house judiciously as the speaker. He said the opposition was ready for dialogue on issues such as empowerment of Parliament and eradicating terrorism of all kinds. “If you hold dialogue on these issues, we will give unconditional support,” he added. The opposition leader compared the KP imbroglio to the 1971 separation of East Pakistan, noting that Afridi was called a “terrorist”. “Were multiple attacks on the heads of different political parties in the past in KP committed by Sohail Afridi?” he asked. Achakzai said terrorism was introduced by those who had brought fighters for the Soviet-Afghan war. “When the Afghan war was over, these terrorists were left free in the tribal areas of the country and they started killing Pakistanis,” he added. The opposition leader then mentioned the reported deaths during the July unrest in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK). The TTAP chief sought meetings of incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan with his family, friends and party workers. He questioned who had “sent” ex-premier Nawaz Sharif to exile in Saudi Arabia and who “murdered” ex-PM Benazir Bhutto. The NA speaker took exception to Achakzai’s remarks on his chairing of the session. “You are saying to me that I am not running the House correctly. You have not read Rule 30. Someone takes their mobile phone; someone disrupts [the proceedings].” Sadiq further said recordings of members’ speeches that were “anti-state” would not be uploaded on the NA’s social media accounts. Meanwhile, Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas accused the government’s delegation of derailing the dialogue with the opposition, including the Oct 3 talks . The Majlis Wahdat-i-Muslimeen (MWM) chief said some more time should have been allowed to make the talks successful and called for resolving the public’s issues instead of blaming each other. The senator contended that people voted for the PTI in large numbers during the February 2024 general elections in reaction to Imran’s imprisonment. Noting that this was his first tenure as a parliament member, Abbas said he realised that the Constitution was a safeguard of the rights of people. He further claimed he did not receive a salary or any perks and privileges from the Senate. ‘We kept waiting’: PPP’s Rehman recounts Oct 3 talks In her remarks, PPP’s Rehman asked the PTI to define its agenda and reasons for its long march , which the party had announced to stage towards Islamabad but remained within KP. The senator added that President Asif Ali Zardari and PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari had insisted on resolving issues through dialogue because terrorism was a red line for them. She called on the opposition not to dictate to the government and to avoid giving lectures on patriotism. Rehman emphasised that everyone was trying to find common ground and “a path of action”. The PPP leader objected to the opposition’s claims that the government delegation left the Oct 3 talks. “We kept waiting for you. The speaker and I ordered food for you as leaving was not being considered. We could have sat till 5am or 6am,” she said. Rehman asserted, “We had said we would wait further […] This is not fair to say that we said ‘we are leaving’. Definitely not. Opposite.” Speaking on the topic, the NA speaker — who chaired the talks — also remarked, “What was the hurry in launching the long march?” Sadiq referred to a post on X made by Afridi about going ahead with the long march even as the negotiations were underway. “You said to ignore it, so we kept ignoring it till 3am, so I think, if you want to sit again [at the table] then do not go into further details. Those things took place in confidence; bury them here.” The PPP vice president remarked that the country faced several emergencies, including those regarding education and poverty, that needed to be seen holistically. “If you think PPP is going to support any sort of emergency which is against the Constitution, you are wrong,” she declared. “This Constitution has bound the country together through difficult times. We remember the lessons from the fall of Dhaka,” she said. “PPP has seen many phases of the path towards democracy. It (martial law) was a dark chapter in history; we do not want the country to go through such an experience again,” Rehman said, recalling “sacrifices” made by her party. JUI-F says no ‘evidence’ presented Senator Kamran Murtaza of the Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F), who had earlier submitted a resolution opposing the imposition of governor’s rule in KP, contended that no documentary evidence was presented before the Parliament for the decision. He argued that the proclamation under Article 234 required a report from the KP governor, but in this case, Governor Faisal Karim Kundi had not presented a report explaining why governor’s rule was necessary. The JUI-F senator said the security situation in Balochistan was also grave and pointed out that a provincial government now had its writ in the Katcha areas without an emergency being imposed there. Murtaza stressed that free and transparent elections under a fair election commission were the only solution to the existing problems.

items.title: Obuasi SHTS scandal: Eduwatch calls for sex offenders’ register and mandatory background checks for teachers
items.description: The Executive Director of Africa Education Watch (Eduwatch), Kofi Asare, has called on the Ghana Education Service (GES) to introduce standardised safeguarding procedures, a sex offenders’ register and mandatory criminal background checks for teachers to address what he describes as systemic gaps in handling misconduct allegations in schools. Speaking on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show on Thursday, October 15, Mr Asare said the absence of consistent standard operating procedures (SOPs) had contributed to uneven responses to safeguarding concerns within the education system. His comments come after the Minister of Education, Haruna Iddrisu, directed the Ghana Education Service to suspend the headmaster of the Obuasi Senior High Technical School over allegations of sexual misconduct. The directive from the minister follows a media report suggesting the headmaster misconducted himself sexually against a female student of Obuasi SHTS in the Ashanti Region. He cited the case of the former headmaster of Benkum Senior High School, who he said was interdicted following an unverified allegation by a student of inappropriate advances. According to Mr Asare, the headmaster was not found guilty but was asked to step aside and transferred to ease tensions within the school after some teachers were perceived to have supported the complainant. He argued that clearly defined procedures were necessary to ensure allegations were handled fairly, protecting students while safeguarding the rights of accused staff. Mr Asare also questioned the handling of concerns surrounding the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School following violence at the institution about two months earlier. He maintained that consistent procedures would have provided a clear framework for determining the appropriate administrative response, rather than leaving matters to emerge through investigative journalism. Describing the situation as a systemic challenge, he said the GES needed to prioritise safeguarding and establish consistent processes for addressing allegations of misconduct. READ ALSO: GES recommends reposting of Obuasi SHTS headmaster after August 2026 campus riot The Eduwatch director further advocated a sex offenders’ register, arguing that such a system could help education authorities identify individuals with relevant histories. He suggested that, had such a register existed, the Obuasi SHTS headmaster would have been recorded following an earlier case in Toase. He also called for mandatory criminal background checks for prospective teachers, noting that several jurisdictions had adopted the practice and that Nigeria had begun introducing similar measures. Mr Asare said Eduwatch had been calling for these reforms for years, stressing that stronger institutional safeguards were necessary to prevent misconduct and improve accountability in schools.

items.title: EAMAU : Fin du jubilé d’or et rentrée académique 2026-2027
items.description: Lomé, 15 oct. (ATOP) – Le ministre malien de l’Enseignement supérieur et de la Recherche scientifique, président du Conseil d’administration de l’École africaine des métiers de l’architecture et de l’urbanisme (EAMAU), Pr Bouréma Kansaye, a présidé, le mercredi 14 octobre à Lomé, la cérémonie de clôture des festivités marquant les 50 ans de l’institution. La rencontre a été marquée par la rentrée solennelle et académique 2026-2027 et l’intégration du Burundi, dont le drapeau a été hissé pour symboliser son entrée parmi les États membres de l’École. Trois jours d’activités commémoratives ont été consacrés aux réflexions sur l’avenir de l’Ecole, aux échanges entre partenaires et aux activités culturelles et sportives des étudiants. Les rencontres institutionnelles et l’exposition organisée sur le site ont également permis de revisiter l’histoire de l’établissement et de dégager des perspectives pour les prochaines années. Les principales recommandations issues des échanges seront examinées par des équipes, afin de traduire les propositions les plus pertinentes en actions concrètes, notamment pour améliorer les contenus pédagogiques, la recherche et la vie estudiantine. Le ministre malien, Pr Bouréma Kansaye, a rappelé que les villes africaines font face à de nombreux défis, notamment l’urbanisation rapide, le manque de logements décents, les besoins en infrastructures, la mobilité durable et les changements climatiques. Pour y répondre, il a insisté sur la nécessité de moderniser les formations et de développer une recherche ancrée dans les réalités du continent. « Si ce cinquantenaire nous invite à célébrer nos réussites, il nous appelle également à préparer l’avenir avec ambition et détermination », a-t-il déclaré. Le ministre de l’Education nationale, Mama Omorou a salué le parcours de l’EAMAU, qu’il considère comme une illustration concrète de l’intégration africaine par l’éducation. Il a rappelé que l’EAMAU a formé plus de 4000 architectes, urbanistes et gestionnaires urbains en cinquante ans. S’adressant aux étudiants, il les a invités à exercer leurs futurs métiers avec responsabilité, en privilégiant des solutions architecturales et urbaines adaptées aux réalités du continent, respectueuses de l’environnement et des besoins des populations. M. Omorou a réaffirmé l’engagement du gouvernement togolais, aux côtés des autres Etats membres, à soutenir la modernisation des infrastructures pédagogiques, la transition numérique et la recherche sur les villes durables et les changements climatiques. Le directeur général de l’EAMAU, Dr Malam Boukar Awa Krou, a souligné que ce cinquantenaire a été l’occasion de mesurer le chemin parcouru, mais aussi de réfléchir aux défis qui restent à relever. Il a encouragé les enseignants à faire preuve de rigueur et de détermination dans l’accomplissement de leurs missions au cours de cette nouvelle année académique. L’adhésion du Burundi porte à quinze le nombre de pays membres de l’EAMAU. Pour cette nouvelle année académique, l’institution accueille dix étudiants burundais. Cette arrivée illustre la volonté de l’École de renforcer les échanges entre les pays africains et de former des professionnels au service du développement du continent. Pour les années à venir, l’EAMAU entend poursuivre sa modernisation. L’acquisition de nouveaux équipements pédagogiques, la numérisation progressive de la bibliothèque et le développement de plateformes d’apprentissage hybride et à distance figurent parmi les actions prévues. L’École compte également renforcer son corps enseignant, redynamiser ses laboratoires de recherche et élargir son réseau de partenaires institutionnels et académiques. La célébration est placée sous le thème « 50 ans d’excellence au bénéfice des villes et territoires d’Afrique ». Elle a mis en lumière le rôle de l’EAMAU dans la formation des compétences nécessaires au développement urbain du continent. Créée à la suite d’une volonté commune des pays africains en 1975 et implantée à Lomé en 1976, l’EAMAU contribue depuis cinq décennies à la formation de professionnels capables de répondre aux besoins des villes africaines. ATOP/AO/HKM/KYA

items.description: ANKARA, Oct 15 (Reuters) - Turkey will probably hold its 2028 elections earlier than expected, a presidential adviser said on Thursday, a move which would allow President Tayyip Erdogan to sidestep constitutional limits and run again for office. The next presidential and parliamentary votes are currently scheduled to take place in May that year. "It is now almost clear that the 2028 elections would be held in March or April," Erdogan's adviser, Mehmet Ucum, told reporters in Ankara.

items.title: Projet « Savanes Kpaadu » : Une délégation constate l’évolution des travaux de construction d’apatam scolaire amélioré
items.description: Dapaong, 15 oct. (ATOP) – Une délégation de Plan International Togo, s’est rendue, le mardi 13 octobre à l’EPP de N’Gambi, dans la préfecture de l’Oti, pour constater l’évolution des travaux de construction d’apatam scolaire amélioré. Cette visite a été précédée des cérémonies de réception des infrastructures démarrées dans les établissements depuis le 6 octobre dernier. La délégation est composée du représentant résident, Ousseynou Samb, du directeur de la mise en œuvre des programmes, Soba Palakeyem et de la directrice régionale Savanes-Kara, Mme Abalo Naka. Ces infrastructures sont réalisées dans le cadre du projet « Action intégrée de réponse de crise dans la région des Savanes au Togo (Savanes Kpaadu) ». Au total, 10 Ecoles primaires publiques (EPP) des préfectures de Tône, de l’Oti, de Kpendjal-ouest et de Cinkassé sont ciblées pour bénéficier de 13 apatams destinés à améliorer les conditions d’apprentissage des élèves. Réception d’ouvrage à Koutonbong A ce jour, les réceptions des infrastructures et des équipements ont été effectuées dans 6 écoles. Les ouvrages sont accompagnés de tables-bancs pour les élèves ainsi que de tables et de chaises pour les enseignants. Ces réalisations visent à favoriser un accès équitable à l’éducation pour les enfants déplacés internes, les enfants réfugiés et ceux issus des communautés hôtes. Elles s’inscrivent dans les efforts de renforcement des capacités d’accueil des établissements scolaires dans les zones vulnérables de la région. Parallèlement aux réceptions, des missions de suivi sont en cours, pour s’assurer de l’avancement des travaux de construction et de la qualité des réalisations. Ces activités mobilisent notamment les Comités de gestion des écoles primaires (COGEP), les autorités locales et éducatives, les entreprises attributaires ainsi que les communautés bénéficiaires. Elles permettent également de relever d’éventuelles insuffisances et de formuler des recommandations en vue de garantir la durabilité des ouvrages et des équipements. Le projet « Savanes Kpaadu » est financé par l’Union européenne (UE), à travers le service des instruments de politique étrangère, « Foreign policy instruments » (FPI) et mis en œuvre par Plan International Togo avec ses partenaires Humanité et Inclusion (HI), Communication pour un développement durable (CDD) et la Centrale africaine pour un développement intégral et durable (CADID). ATOP/TT/JK/BA

items.title: Octobre rose : l’ANINF mise sur les témoignages et la solidarité face au cancer féminin
items.description: À l’occasion d’une journée de sensibilisation organisée le 15 octobre 2026 à Libreville, l’Agence nationale des infrastructures numériques et des fréquences (ANINF) a misé sur des témoignages pour briser les tabous autour des cancers féminins. Touché par les récits des participantes, son directeur général a instruit le versement de 10 millions de FCFA pour leur apporter un soutien. Le directeur général de l’ANINF, Alberto Wenceslas Mounguegui Moudoki s’adressant aux victimes, le 15 octobre 2026. © GabonReview Briser le silence autour des cancers féminins et rappeler que le dépistage précoce peut sauver des vies. C’est le double objectif de la journée de sensibilisation organisée, ce jeudi 15 octobre 2026, par l’Agence nationale des infrastructures numériques et des fréquences (ANINF), dans le cadre de la campagne Octobre Rose, sous le thème « Unis par l’unique ». Pour cette édition, l’Agence a privilégié une approche centrée sur l’humain, en donnant la parole à des femmes aux parcours différents face à la maladie. Trois témoignages pour évoquer la réalité de la maladie, le poids de la perte, mais aussi la résilience et l’espoir. Particulièrement touché par ces récits, le directeur général de l’ANINF, Alberto Wenceslas Mounguegui Moudoki, a instruit l’agent comptable et le contrôleur budgétaire de remettre une enveloppe de 10 millions de FCFA aux personnes concernées afin de les soutenir. Un geste de solidarité qui a marqué cette rencontre consacrée à la prévention et à l’accompagnement des femmes confrontées au cancer. Prenant la parole, le responsable de l’Agence a insisté sur la nécessité de ne plus reporter les consultations médicales. « En matière de santé, attendre peut parfois avoir de lourdes conséquences », a-t-il averti, appelant les agents à faire de la prévention un réflexe plutôt qu’une réaction à l’apparition de la maladie. Une assurance maladie complémentaire mise en place au bénéfice du personnel Quelques moments de la journée. © GabonReview Il a également rappelé l’existence de l’assurance maladie complémentaire mise en place au bénéfice du personnel, invitant les collaborateurs à s’approprier ce dispositif et à utiliser pleinement les garanties offertes pour les consultations et les examens de suivi. « La santé n’a pas un coût, c’est un investissement », a-t-il souligné. L’aspect médical de la rencontre a été développé par le Dr Line Silat Tamo épouse Nzoumba Moukagni, oncologue médicale à l’Institut de cancérologie d’Akanda. À l’aide de supports visuels, la spécialiste a présenté les différentes formes de cancers féminins et insisté sur l’importance du dépistage précoce, notamment par la palpation et le suivi médical. Pour Nadine Gaudong, agente de l’ANINF, les témoignages ont surtout permis de rappeler qu’« il y a de l’espoir », même lorsque la maladie survient. Elle a salué les dispositifs de dépistage et le courage des femmes venues partager leur expérience. À travers cette initiative, l’ANINF entend inscrire le bien-être de ses agents au cœur de sa démarche institutionnelle. Au-delà des discours, le message de cette journée reste clair : se faire dépister, consulter à temps et accompagner les personnes malades sont des leviers essentiels dans la lutte contre les cancers féminins. L’article Octobre rose : l’ANINF mise sur les témoignages et la solidarité face au cancer féminin est apparu en premier sur Gabonreview.com | Actualité du Gabon | .

items.title: L’Iran multiplie les attaques dans le détroit d’Ormuz
items.description: Les attaques visant des navires commerciaux dans et autour du détroit d’Ormuz ont considérablement accéléré depuis le début du mois. L’Office des opérations commerciales maritimes du Royaume-Uni (UKMTO), un organisme de liaison de la Royal Navy britannique, a signalé 23 attaques au cours des deux premières semaines d’octobre, soit plus que n’importe quel mois depuis le début de la guerre contre l’Iran, lancée le 28 février. Entre mardi 13 et mercredi 14, deux navires appartenant à des armateurs émiratis, vraisemblablement attaqués par l'Iran, ont coulé après avoir été frappés dans ou à proximité du détroit d’Ormuz. A cargo ship sank near the Strait of Hormuz after reportedly being struck by a projectile, leaving containers floating at sea. All 21 crew members escaped safely. A second ship was also confirmed sunk amid intensifying attacks on commercial vessels. pic.twitter.com/tUfDqOYjr4 — Breaking911 (@Breaking911) October 15, 2026 Le porte-conteneurs GFS Pride avait été frappé mardi par un « projectile inconnu », tandis que le vraquier Cape Dao avait été touché trois semaines auparavant, le 23 septembre Two Cargo Ships Sink Near Strait of Hormuz, as Iranian Attacks Increase », The Wall Street Journal , 14 octobre 2026.'> 1 . Il s’agit des premiers navires coulés dans le détroit d’Ormuz depuis le début du mois de mars, lorsque le Safeen Prestige, un porte-conteneurs battant pavillon de Malte, avait été frappé à proximité des côtes d’Oman. Alors que les dernières opérations militaires américaines en Iran remontent, selon l’Institute for the Study of War, au début du mois de septembre, l’Iran a multiplié les attaques ces dernières semaines, contraignant des super-pétroliers à faire demi-tour pour retourner dans le golfe Persique Iran Escalates Attacks on Ships, Threatening Oil Export Recovery », Bloomberg , 13 octobre 2026.'> 2 . Ces attaques pourraient conduire à un ralentissement des flux pétroliers en provenance du Moyen-Orient, qui ont connu une nette hausse fin septembre. Des responsables iraniens ont déclaré en début de semaine que le pays avait commencé, depuis le début du mois, à utiliser différentes tactiques offensives contre les navires qu’il considérait comme enfreignant ses restrictions Iran shifting tactics to step up attacks on shipping before US vote, officials say », Reuters , 14 octobre 2026.'> 3 . Ces mêmes responsables revendiquent vouloir contrecarrer les efforts déployés par l’administration Trump pour faire baisser les cours mondiaux du pétrole – et donc à la pompe aux États-Unis – en amont des élections de mi-mandat. Le choc énergétique provoqué par la guerre contre l’Iran continue d’avoir un impact sur les prix, et notamment sur ceux de l’essence, et ce malgré les tentatives de l’administration Trump visant à les faire baisser. Aux États-Unis, l’indice mesurant les prix de l’essence a bondi de 9,1 % en septembre, soit la plus forte hausse depuis mars (+21,2 %). Vendredi 9, le président américain a annoncé avoir conclu un accord avec le Kremlin pour mettre « immédiatement » 300 000 tonnes de diesel « sur le marché américain et mondial ». Aujourd'hui, jeudi 15, l’Agence internationale de l’énergie a fait savoir que ses membres s’étaient mis d’accord pour « mener à bien les dernières mises sur le marché d'environ 100 millions de barils », dont plus de 20 millions de barils de gazole IEA Governing Board statement on energy markets and security , Agence internationale de l'énergie, 15 octobre 2026.'> 4 . Plus tôt dans la journée, des représentants américains avaient exercé des pressions sur les autres membres de l’Agence pour libérer au moins 100 millions de barils supplémentaires de stocks d’urgence US Tells IEA Nations It’s Unhappy With Emergency Oil Release », Bloomberg , 15 octobre 2026.'> 5 . Depuis le début de la guerre, 330 millions de barils sur les 400 millions engagés en mars – soit la libération la plus importante de l’Agence depuis sa création, en 1974 – ont été mis sur les marchés. L’article L’Iran multiplie les attaques dans le détroit d’Ormuz est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: Biens mal acquis : Libreville révise sa position, un avocat se retire sous les menaces
items.description: Un mémoire allégé, des formulations retirées et un avocat qui se retire après avoir signalé des intimidations : le dossier des biens mal acquis connaît une nouvelle inflexion. Selon Africa Intelligence, Libreville a remanié ses observations devant la justice française pour apaiser Denis Sassou-Nguesso, après plusieurs semaines de tensions entre les deux présidences. Libreville a atténué ses observations dans l’affaire des biens mal acquis. La défense des intérêts financiers du Gabon à l’épreuve des relations entre Oligui Nguema et Sassou-Nguesso. Photomontage d’illustration. © GabonReview Instruite en France, l’affaire des biens mal acquis porte sur des patrimoines immobiliers soupçonnés d’avoir été constitués avec des fonds publics gabonais détournés. Le Gabon, partie civile depuis 2023, entend obtenir réparation. Mais son soutien au jugement des personnes mises en examen, parmi lesquelles des proches de Denis Sassou-Nguesso, a transformé cette démarche judiciaire en différend avec Brazzaville. Les formulations qui fâchent disparaissent Dans sa publication du 15 octobre, Africa Intelligence révèle que les avocats du Gabon ont transmis, début octobre, de nouvelles observations au juge Serge Tournaire. Le mémoire de 53 pages déposé le 8 septembre laisse place à un texte de moins de dix pages, « largement édulcoré ». Les références au financement occulte lié à l’ancienne compagnie pétrolière Elf ont disparu. Surtout, Africa Intelligence relève la « suppression des formules autour du souhait du Gabon de renvoyer devant le tribunal correctionnel de Paris les personnalités mises en examen dans cette affaire ». Selon le média, le premier texte citait nommément Antoinette Sassou-Nguesso, épouse du président congolais, et son petit-fils Omar-Denis Junior Bongo. Denis Sassou-Nguesso y avait vu une attaque directe d’Oligui Nguema. Les personnes concernées restent présumées innocentes. En septembre, Me Vivien Patrice Makaga-Péa expliquait pourtant à GabonReview qu’« une partie civile ne poursuit personne et ne renvoie personne ». Il confirmait néanmoins le soutien gabonais aux conclusions du parquet. La révision des observations marque donc une inflexion, sans établir un abandon des demandes patrimoniales. Africa Intelligence ne rapporte ni retrait du Gabon comme partie civile, ni renoncement à récupérer les avoirs. La décision sur les renvois appartient au juge français. Le PDG dans le jeu diplomatique Le différend a débordé le prétoire. Selon Africa Intelligence , Denis Sassou-Nguesso a rencontré nuitamment Ali Bongo à Paris. Les deux hommes auraient évoqué des possibilités de « perturber le jeu politique en instrumentalisant les divisions » du Parti démocratique gabonais. Fin septembre, Oligui Nguema a dépêché des émissaires à Brazzaville. Le président congolais « n’a pu contenir sa colère lors d’un long monologue », en présence d’Omar-Denis Junior Bongo, rapporte Africa Intelligence . La modification des observations intervient après cette démarche d’apaisement. Un avocat signale des filatures et se retire Autre révélation préoccupante : Me Makaga-Péa a signalé au barreau de Paris des menaces, des intimidations et des filatures. La plaque de son cabinet aurait été arrachée. Selon Africa Intelligence , il a déposé plainte contre X le 5 octobre et s’est mis en retrait du dossier, désormais suivi par Raphaël Gauvain. Les auteurs de ces actes ne sont pas identifiés dans l’article. Rien ne permet donc de les attribuer aux protagonistes du différend diplomatique. Libreville cherche à apaiser Brazzaville, mais aucune contrepartie congolaise n’est rapportée. Reste à savoir si l’allègement du mémoire suffira à refermer la crise, sans affaiblir les exigences de réparation que le Gabon avait placées au cœur de sa démarche. L’article Biens mal acquis : Libreville révise sa position, un avocat se retire sous les menaces est apparu en premier sur Gabonreview.com | Actualité du Gabon | .

items.title: Ordre des géomètres du Togo : Un nouveau bureau pour renforcer la gouvernance foncière
items.description: Lomé, 15 oct. (ATOP) – Le nouveau bureau du Conseil de l’Ordre des géomètres du Togo a été présenté le jeudi 15 octobre à Lomé. Ce bureau de cinq membres a été élu le 27 août dernier lors d’une assemblée générale élective pour un mandat de trois ans. Il entend renforcer l’organisation de la profession, rapprocher leurs services des populations et de contribuer à une meilleure gouvernance foncière au Togo. Reconduit à la présidence de l’Ordre, Atcholadi Nikada et son équipe se donnent pour mission de promouvoir l’excellence dans la profession, de défendre les intérêts des géomètres et de représenter la corporation auprès des institutions nationales et internationales. Pour atteindre ses objectifs, le nouveau bureau a défini une feuille de route axée sur quatre priorités. Il s’agit d’accompagner les projets et les réformes structurants du gouvernement, de favoriser une meilleure répartition des géomètres sur l’ensemble du territoire afin de rapprocher leurs services des citoyens, de renforcer les compétences des membres et de consolider les échanges au sein de la corporation. Le bureau entend également poursuivre les démarches engagées pour la mise en œuvre des directives de l’Union économique et monétaire ouest-africaine (UEMOA), notamment l’harmonisation des textes devant faciliter la libre circulation des géomètres dans l’espace communautaire. Le représentant du ministre de l’Urbanisme et de l’Habitat, M. Affo Bidjo, a salué le dynamisme du bureau sortant et les actions menées en collaboration avec son département. Il a toutefois insisté sur la nécessité de mieux encadrer l’exercice de la profession, notamment en limitant les interventions des géomètres dits « ambulants » et en réorganisant leurs activités pour plus d’efficacité. Il a invité les géomètres à s’approprier le plan parcellaire et le réseau de bornes géodésiques afin de contribuer efficacement à l’identification et à l’enregistrement des parcelles. M. Affo a, par ailleurs, évoqué les réformes engagées pour améliorer la gestion foncière au Togo, dont le projet de cadastrage de l’ensemble du territoire national. Cette initiative, a-t-il dit, vise à identifier les véritables propriétaires des parcelles et à faciliter la délivrance des certificats ou des titres fonciers, dans le but de renforcer la sécurité foncière. Le président Atcholadi a réaffirmé la disponibilité de l’Ordre à contribuer aux politiques de développement territorial et aux réformes institutionnelles. Il a assuré que son équipe travaillera en étroite collaboration avec le ministère de tutelle, les institutions partenaires et l’ensemble des membres pour atteindre les objectifs fixés. ATOP/BA/AO

items.title: Loi organique sur les finances publiques :le Conseil constitutionnel censure le vote de l’Assemblée nationale
items.description: Dans sa décision n° 10/C/2026 du 15 octobre 2026, le Conseil constitutionnel a déclaré contraire à la Constitution la loi organique n° 38/2026, adoptée par l’Assemblée nationale le 1er octobre. En cause, le non-respect de l’article 82, alinéa 4, de la Constitution, qui impose un vote unique lorsque le Gouvernement en fait formellement la demande. Pour la haute juridiction, cette irrégularité constitue une violation d’une formalité substantielle et affecte la validité de la loi. Le Conseil constitutionnel a censuré la procédure d’adoption de la loi organique n° 38/2026 modifiant la loi organique n° 2020-07 du 26 février 2020 relative aux lois de finances. Saisi par le président de la République, il a estimé que l’Assemblée nationale avait méconnu une règle constitutionnelle encadrant le vote des textes législatifs. Au cœur du différend : l’article 82, alinéa 4, de la Constitution, qui permet au Gouvernement de demander à l’Assemblée nationale de se prononcer par un vote unique sur tout ou partie du texte en discussion, en ne retenant que les amendements proposés ou acceptés par lui. Dans sa décision, le Conseil ne s’est pas limité à relever une irrégularité dans le déroulement des débats. Il a considéré que le non-respect de cette disposition constituait une violation d’une formalité substantielle, de nature à altérer la procédure d’adoption et à affecter la validité de la loi elle-même. Une demande formelle du Gouvernement Dans sa requête reçue le 8 octobre 2026, le président de la République contestait la régularité de la procédure suivie par les députés. Il soutenait que l’Assemblée nationale avait examiné séparément les amendements du Gouvernement, avant de les rejeter, puis adopté l’article unique de la proposition de loi organique sans les intégrer. Pour étayer son recours, le requérant a produit deux clés USB contenant l’enregistrement de la séance plénière ainsi qu’un procès-verbal de constat d’huissier établi le 8 octobre 2026. Ces pièces reproduisent notamment les déclarations du ministre de la Justice, Garde des Sceaux, chargé de représenter le Gouvernement lors de l’examen du texte. Le ministre avait expressément demandé l’application du mécanisme prévu par l’article 82, alinéa 4, de la Constitution et par l’article 87, alinéa 2, du règlement intérieur de l’Assemblée nationale. Il avait sollicité un vote unique sur le texte, en ne retenant que les amendements proposés ou acceptés par le Gouvernement. Selon les éléments retenus par le Conseil constitutionnel, les amendements gouvernementaux ont pourtant été soumis à des votes séparés, puis rejetés. L’article unique de la proposition de loi a ensuite été adopté sans que ces amendements soient pris en compte. C’est cette succession d’actes que la haute juridiction a jugée contraire à la Constitution. L’article 82, une règle qui s’impose au vote parlementaire Dans son raisonnement, le Conseil constitutionnel rappelle le contenu de l’article 82, alinéa 4 : lorsque le Gouvernement le demande, l’Assemblée nationale doit se prononcer par un seul vote sur tout ou partie du texte en discussion, en ne retenant que les amendements proposés ou acceptés par le Gouvernement. La disposition ne distingue pas entre les projets de loi et les propositions de loi. La juridiction précise ainsi que, dans les deux cas, la demande du Gouvernement entraîne une obligation pour l’Assemblée nationale. Deux issues sont alors possibles, selon les termes de la décision : les députés adoptent le texte intégrant les seuls amendements autorisés par le mécanisme constitutionnel, ou ils rejettent le texte dans son intégralité. Ils ne peuvent, dans cette configuration, procéder à des votes séparés sur les amendements gouvernementaux, puis adopter le reste du texte comme si la demande de vote unique n’avait pas été formulée. Cette interprétation donne à l’article 82 une portée procédurale précise. Dès lors que le Gouvernement active ce mécanisme, les modalités du vote sont encadrées par la Constitution. Le débat parlementaire et le pouvoir de décision de l’Assemblée nationale doivent s’exercer dans le respect de cette exigence. Le Conseil constitutionnel ne fonde donc pas sa décision sur une appréciation politique du texte ni sur le bien-fondé de la réforme des lois de finances. Il se prononce sur la régularité de son adoption au regard d’une règle constitutionnelle explicite. Une formalité substantielle qui affecte la validité de la loi Le point décisif de la décision réside dans la qualification juridique du manquement. Au considérant 11, le Conseil constitutionnel affirme que le non-respect de l’article 82, alinéa 4, constitue une « violation d’une formalité substantielle ». Cette qualification distingue l’irrégularité relevée d’un simple défaut formel sans conséquence sur la validité de l’acte. Pour la juridiction, le vice a altéré la procédure d’adoption de la loi et affecte, par conséquent, la loi elle-même. Le raisonnement suit une progression claire : le Gouvernement a demandé l’application du vote unique ; l’Assemblée nationale a procédé à des votes séparés sur les amendements, puis adopté l’article unique du texte ; cette méthode a méconnu la Constitution ; enfin, la violation d’une formalité substantielle a entaché la validité de la loi. Sur cette base, le Conseil constitutionnel conclut que la loi organique n° 38/2026 est contraire à la Constitution. L’article premier de sa décision consacre cette conclusion. L’article 2 prévoit la publication de la décision au Journal officiel de la République. Le respect de la procédure, condition de validité de la loi Cette décision rappelle que la conformité d’une loi à la Constitution ne dépend pas uniquement de son contenu. La manière dont elle est examinée et adoptée compte également, en particulier lorsque la Constitution prévoit une procédure spécifique et que les conditions de son application sont réunies. En l’espèce, le Conseil constitutionnel a retenu que la demande du Gouvernement avait été formulée expressément et que les éléments versés au dossier permettaient d’établir que la procédure suivie par l’Assemblée nationale ne respectait pas le vote unique prévu par la Constitution. La portée de la décision dépasse ainsi le seul texte examiné. Elle souligne que les règles constitutionnelles encadrant le travail parlementaire ne peuvent être écartées au cours de la procédure législative. Lorsqu’une formalité substantielle est méconnue, l’irrégularité peut entraîner l’invalidation de la loi. Le Conseil constitutionnel n’a donc pas tranché l’opportunité de la modification de la loi organique relative aux lois de finances. Il a jugé que son adoption ne respectait pas les exigences constitutionnelles. C’est sur ce fondement procédural, et non sur une appréciation du fond de la réforme, que la loi organique n° 38/2026 a été déclarée contraire à la Constitution.

items.title: GloMeF CEO urges intensified public education on new road traffic regulations
items.description: The Chief Executive Officer of the Global Media Foundation (GloMeF), Raphael Godlove, has called for intensified public education on the new Road Traffic Regulations 2026 (L.I. 2519). The enforcement of L.I. 2519 introduced updated safety rules, automated enforcement, and stricter penalties for drivers, passengers, and pedestrians. In an interview with the Ghana News Agency (GNA), Mr Ahenu noted that although laudable, a lack of public understanding of the new road traffic regulations would undermine its full implementation. He said relying heavily on digital platforms for mass education would not be beneficial to many drivers, motorists and other road users, particularly those in rural communities. Mr Ahenu called on the government, law enforcement agencies and relevant institutions to adopt a more inclusive and community-based approach in educating the public on the regulation to enhance compliance. “We need face-to-face education, and the relevant authorities must go beyond social media and organise community engagements, public fora and directly sensitise the masses”, he suggested and called for collaboration among key stakeholders towards enforcing the Regulations. He said strengthened collaboration between the Motor Traffic and Transport Department (MTTD), transport unions, driver associations and road agencies and traditional authorities was required for an effective public education campaign on the regulations. “Road traffic laws must not be understood only by people who have smartphones, internet access or the ability to follow discussions on social media”. “In fact, a farmer at Yawsae and a commercial driver at a lorry station and a pedestrian in a rural settlement all deserve to understand the law”, he added. The nation’s new road traffic framework comprises the Road Traffic (Amendment) Act, 2025 (Act 1153), and the Road Traffic Regulations, 2026 (L.I. 2519). President John Dramani Mahama assented to the amendment on December 24, 2025, with Parliament approving the Regulations on May 28, 2026. The framework introduces several changes to improve road safety, strengthen traffic enforcement, and promote discipline among road users. Among the major reforms are automated traffic enforcement systems, including speed and red-light cameras, and a demerit point system linked to drivers’ licenses. It also pushes stricter penalties for serious traffic offences and a reduction in the permissible blood alcohol concentration for drivers from 0.08 to 0.05. The regulations introduced new requirements for commercial transport operations, vehicle inspections, speed control, and the commercial use of motorcycles, tricycles, and quadricycles for passenger services.

items.title: ‘Any tax on ChatGPT is an attack on education and innovation’- Akim Swedru, MP
items.description: The Member of Parliament for Akim Swedru, Kennedy Osei Nyarko, has opposed calls to introduce a tax on ChatGPT, arguing that such a move could undermine education and innovation. In a post on Facebook, the legislator questioned the rationale behind abolishing the betting tax while considering a tax on ChatGPT, a widely used artificial intelligence tool for learning, research, and other productive activities. “We cannot abolish the betting tax; rather, we should introduce a tax on ChatGPT, which is for education and innovation. Any tax on ChatGPT is an attack on education and innovation,” he wrote. The MP’s comments come amid public debate over the Ghana Revenue Authority’s new digital VAT collection system, which takes effect on October 15, 2026. The GRA has clarified that the new system does not introduce a new tax or increase the existing VAT rate. Rather, it is intended to improve the collection and accounting of taxes already applicable to digital services supplied by non-resident companies to consumers in Ghana. The applicable effective tax rate remains 20%, comprising 15% VAT, a 2.5% National Health Insurance Levy (NHIL) and a 2.5% Ghana Education Trust Fund (GETFund) Levy. According to the GRA, approximately 92 non-resident digital service providers are currently registered and remitting VAT. Where the applicable taxes are already included in subscription prices, the introduction of the new collection system will not result in an additional charge on the same transaction. However, the Authority has identified approximately 100 additional non-resident digital service providers that are not currently charging and remitting the applicable taxes. These providers will be progressively brought into the tax net. However, the scope of the original digital tax measures should be distinguished from any specific proposal to impose a separate tax on ChatGPT. The applicable rules and rates may also have changed since 2022.

items.title: Obuasi SHTS sexual abuse scandal exposes systemic failure in child protection – Moving Masculinity
items.description: Creator of Moving Masculinity, Esther Amarh, has described the alleged sexual abuse of female students at Obuasi Senior High Technical School as evidence of a systemic failure in Ghana’s child protection system. She says the failure of authorities to act on complaints against the suspended headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai, until a media report by JoyNews raises serious questions about the effectiveness of systems meant to protect students from sexual harassment and abuse in schools. Speaking on Joy FM’s Middaynews on Thursday, October 15, Ms Amarh called for collective outrage over what she described as a persistent failure to protect children, insisting that accountability must extend beyond the alleged perpetrator to officials who failed to respond to complaints. “As a nation, we should be collectively outraged by this ongoing systemic failure to protect girls, children, and boys. This sexual abuse often happens to boys as well,” she said. Her comments follow a JoyNews investigation by Manasseh Azure Awuni, which found that municipal authorities, education officials and other influential figures had received reports about alleged sexual abuse involving female students months before Mr Abdulai’s suspension. Ms Amarh said the fact that action appeared to follow public exposure rather than the initial complaints was particularly troubling. “The only tool that these authorities paid attention to was national shame and exposure, not conscience, not morality, not the right of those girls to have an education, and not their own structures and systems,” she said. She questioned the effectiveness of existing procedures for handling allegations of sexual harassment, assault, defilement and rape involving students, arguing that institutions must be held accountable when they fail to respond appropriately. “There must be consequences, not just for what the teacher or the individual did. There must be consequences for inaction. There must be an audit done of exactly who did not do what,” she added. She also proposed sanctions that could affect the salaries and promotion prospects of officials found to have neglected their duties, arguing that disciplinary measures must be strong enough to deter similar failures. “I have worked on these issues for over seven, eight, nine years, and it is exactly the same scenario: a girl reports, inaction, silence, no action. It escalates, more girls, more lives ruined, more education interrupted,” she said. Ms Amarh further urged Ghana to treat sexual abuse in schools as a national public health crisis rather than isolated incidents affecting individual students.

items.title: Hubtel CEO calls for national data-sharing framework to boost AI development
items.description: The Chief Executive Officer of Hubtel, Alex Bram, has called for a national data-sharing framework that encourages companies to preserve and make data available under appropriate arrangements to support the development of artificial intelligence (AI) in Ghana. He believes the absence of an effective system for sharing data between institutions remains a major obstacle to developing AI technologies locally, warning that investment in computing infrastructure alone will not be sufficient to drive Ghana’s AI ambitions. Mr. Bram wants the government to introduce incentives that encourage businesses to retain useful data rather than discard it, while establishing clear arrangements for how institutions can share information. “At the least, we should have a data framework that will sort of call on companies to actually not delete data, but store them, and have a framework for incentivising companies to store data,” he said. He explained that Ghana’s planned national AI compute centre would require substantial amounts of data to support the development and training of AI systems. “Because at some point when we finish the AI data centres, we will need a lot of data. But it’s a step in the right direction,” he added. Speaking in an interview ahead of the second episode of the Digital Economy Forum , Mr. Bram drew on Hubtel’s experience developing its own artificial intelligence systems to explain why the country must prioritise data availability alongside investment in computing infrastructure. The opportunities and challenges associated with AI adoption will form part of discussions at the second episode of the Digital Economy Forum , under the theme “AI and the Ghana Economy: Opportunity or Disruption?” The forum, held in partnership with Hubtel , will feature the Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Sam George; Economist and Technical Advisor at the Finance Ministry, Dr Theo Acheampong; Founder of AI for Ghana, Adam Watkins; Head of Engineering at Hubtel, Augustine Adjei; and Vice President of IMANI Africa, Bright Simons. It will air live on JoyNews and Joy 99.7 FM on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, at 8 p.m. Hubtel’s struggle to access data Mr. Bram revealed that Hubtel established an AI laboratory in 2023 after beginning experiments with the technology in 2022. The company initially sought to develop its own AI models using machine learning and neural network technologies, working with other businesses to test some of the systems it had developed. However, the company encountered difficulties obtaining sufficient data to improve the performance of its models. According to Mr. Bram, Hubtel approached several large companies to explore opportunities for sharing data but discovered that there were no clear arrangements governing how such exchanges should take place. “At a point, we tried to connect with other large companies to see if they can give us, they can share data with us, we can share some of our data with them,” he explained. “We realised there’s still no framework in Ghana for sharing data. And so some of them were like, do we sign NDAs? Do we copy our data in Excel and give it to you? Do we have an agreement to share the data, and how do we even share it? There’s just no framework.” He said the uncertainty made companies reluctant to share information, limiting Hubtel’s ability to obtain the data required to improve its AI models. “We just found that in Ghana it wasn’t. So there weren’t that many companies willing to share data with us to improve. So it became another obstacle that didn’t really help our success,” he said. Mr. Bram contrasted Ghana’s situation with developments in the United States, China and parts of Europe, where he believes established data-sharing arrangements have contributed to the advancement of artificial intelligence. He argued that Ghana must learn from these experiences by creating conditions that allow local technology companies to access useful data through structured arrangements. Data critical to Ghana’s AI compute centre The Hubtel CEO welcomed the government’s plans to establish a national AI compute centre, but maintained that the investment would achieve limited results without sufficient data to support the development of AI applications. He described the proposed facility as an important step towards positioning Ghana in the global AI economy, while urging policymakers to accelerate the development of the supporting systems. “So that data framework is important. If that AI compute centre is to succeed, because when a computer centre is there, without the data, it’s nothing,” he stressed. Asked whether the data-sharing framework should be established even before the physical computing infrastructure is completed, Mr. Bram agreed. “Yes, yes. I think we need that. I think at the least, if not maybe enforcing it on private companies, I think at least we can enforce it with the government institution. Because AI is just data,” he explained. His position suggests that government institutions could take an early lead in establishing clearer arrangements for retaining and sharing data, while incentives encourage private companies to participate. Mr. Bram believes such a framework could have significantly improved Hubtel’s own AI development efforts. “We will need that. If we had that, I’m sure our AI lab would have been a success. But we didn’t have that,” he said. Protecting personal and commercially sensitive data While expanding data availability could accelerate AI development, it also raises questions about how personal information and commercially sensitive records would be protected. A national data-sharing framework would need to establish clear rules governing which information can be shared, who can access it, how it can be used and what safeguards are required to prevent misuse. Such arrangements would be particularly important where information contains customers’ personal details, financial transactions, confidential business records or other sensitive material. The retention of data would also need to be distinguished from permission to share or use it for AI training. Preserving information does not automatically authorise its disclosure to third parties.

items.title: 4e session ordinaire de la commune Agou 2 : Les travaux consacrés à l’adoption du budget primitif 2027
items.description: Agou-Gadzépé, 15 oct. (ATOP) – Le conseil municipal de la commune Agou 2 a ouvert, le mercredi 14 octobre à Amoussoukopé, sa quatrième session ordinaire de l’année. Durant trois jours, les élus locaux se pencheront sur la présentation de la situation financière de la commune, couvrant la période du 1 er janvier au 30 septembre 2026. Ils procéderont également au débat et à l’adoption des orientations budgétaires pour l’exercice 2027. À l’ordre du jour figurent aussi la présentation de l’ONG « Pioneers en action pour le développement intégral de l’environnement » (PADIE) et du projet de développement du service public d’eau potable à Amoussoukopé, ainsi que l’étude, l’amendement et l’adoption du budget primitif 2027. La programmation des investissements pour 2027, une visite de terrain et une séance de sensibilisation des populations de Nyitoé-Zukpé sont également prévues. Le rapport sur la situation financière de la commune, couvrant la période du 1 er janvier au 30 septembre 2026, fait ressortir des recettes de fonctionnement réalisées à hauteur de 38 862 058 F CFA, pour une prévision de 73 876 886 F CFA. L’écart entre les prévisions et les réalisations s’élève ainsi à 35 014 828 F CFA, soit un taux de réalisation de 52,6 %. Le rapport indique également que les dépenses de fonctionnement exécutées s’établissent à 39 270 662 F CFA. Pour le préfet d’Agou, Ali Mouzou, cette session permettra aux conseillers municipaux d’examiner les perspectives financières de la commune, de définir les priorités d’intervention et d’apprécier les ressources nécessaires à mobiliser pour répondre aux besoins des populations. Le préfet a invité les participants à faire preuve d’un esprit de participation et de concertation afin d’aboutir à l’adoption d’un budget prenant en compte l’ensemble des secteurs sociaux de la commune. Le maire de la commune Agou 2, Sakpa Koofi Séssimé, a indiqué que cette dernière session de l’année constituera un cadre privilégié pour la programmation des investissements à réaliser en 2027. « Ces différents sujets exigent de nous un esprit de dialogue, d’écoute mutuelle et de recherche permanente de l’intérêt général. Je demeure convaincu que, grâce à l’expérience et à l’engagement de chacun, nos échanges aboutiront à des décisions pertinentes et bénéfiques pour les populations de la commune », a-t-il ajouté. ATOP/BSM/MET/MD

items.title: Finnish court reduces Simon Ekpa’s sentence to four years
items.description: A Finnish court of appeal has reduced the prison sentence of Biafra separatist Simon Ekpa from six years to four years while upholding his convictions for terrorism-related offences. In its ruling on Thursday, the court upheld Ekpa’s convictions for participating in the activities of a terrorist group and publicly inciting people to commit crimes with terrorist intent. The 41-year-old has been in custody since November 2024, when he was arrested by Finnish law enforcement authorities. Ekpa had appealed the September 2025 judgment of the Päijät-Häme District Court, which sentenced him to six years in prison. Prosecutors also appealed, seeking a harsher sentence. However, the appeal court reduced his sentence, citing circumstances surrounding the offences that it said bore similarities to situations in which grounds for exemption from criminal liability, including civil war, self-defence and necessity, could arise. According to the appellate court, the district court had accepted the prosecution’s case that Ekpa operated from Finland as the supreme commander of several armed groups in south-eastern Nigeria. The groups allegedly sought to establish an independent Biafran state, with members carrying out attacks on police stations, government buildings and military roadblocks in pursuit of that objective. The appeal court said it reviewed the evidence presented by prosecutors and reached the same conclusions as the district court regarding Ekpa’s activities. During the appeal, however, Ekpa submitted additional evidence in support of his argument that an internal armed conflict was ongoing in south-eastern Nigeria. He argued that international humanitarian law, rather than Finland’s domestic terrorism laws, should apply because his activities were connected to the conflict and were not driven by terrorist intent. The court examined the nature of the conflict, the organisation of the armed groups and the intensity of the fighting. It also compared the evidence with legal assessments of the Balkan wars by the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia. It found that evidence of Nigerian government forces deploying heavy weapons, including armoured vehicles and combat helicopters, supported the argument that an internal armed conflict existed. The court, however, ruled that the fighting did not meet the legal threshold for a civil war. Although it rejected Ekpa’s argument that the conflict negated terrorist intent in his actions, the court considered the circumstances relevant to sentencing and reduced his prison term from six years to four years. items.title: World's top cocoa producer Ivory Coast aims for a climate-tough bean
items.description: Kofi Alexis Amani has watched the trees on his cocoa plantation wilt and sometimes wither as rains became unpredictable and less abundant in Ivory Coast over the past several decades. “You can lose everything,” he sighed. The west African country is the world’s top cocoa producer, responsible for nearly 40 per cent of global output. Its economy also depends on the crop, which accounts for 15pc of GDP, supporting roughly five million people in a country of more than 33m. An Ivorian researcher measures cocoa pods on trees in a cocoa seed field belonging to the National Centre for Agronomic Research (CNRA) near Divo, on Sept 15, 2026. — AFP So, scientists at the National Centre for Agronomic Research (CNRA) have been working to develop a bean tough enough to survive the unpredictable weather events that man-made climate change has unleashed around the globe. Specifically, the researchers are working on bean varieties that are less sensitive to the availability of water. “We take the flowers from the male parents, which we then use to pollinate the flowers of the female parents… it’s their offspring that we take”, then test in the greenhouse and expose to various levels of water stress, geneticist Caudou Trebissou told AFP . A general view of Sun-dried cofffe beans near Divo, on Sept 15, 2026. — AFP So far, the researchers have come up with 11 “satisfactory” varieties, which they plan to eventually release on the market. Drier, hotter While rainfall has fluctuated in the country since the 1950s, it has steadily dropped since the 1980s, with the trend continuing over the past few decades, according to a report by the ministry of ecology. “From 2003 to 2022, we saw that rainfall has declined. We’re only at 1,100 and something” millimetres of water on average per year in the region, instead of the 1,200 to 2,000mm that cocoa trees need, Maryse Assi, a CNRA agronomist, said. Maryse Assi, a National Center for Agronomic Research (CNRA) agronomist poses for a photograph in a cocoa seed field near Divo, on Sept 15, 2026. — AFP When the plants manage to survive, “we see a drop in flowering or a shift in the flowering period” and “few fruits”, she added. The lack of rain also leads to “declines in soil fertility; some mineral elements will no longer be accessible to the plant”, she said. Farmers see this up close on their land. “When it doesn’t rain, the branches are dry, the leaves curl up” and “the pods are small”, said Anselme Kouakou, who grows cocoa a few kilometres from Amani in the centre of the country. Future lies ‘in research’ While waiting for science to come up with a super-cocoa bean, Amani and others like him have tried to stem the effects of climate change by altering how they plant their cocoa trees. He used to have just cocoa trees on his land. Now he intersperses them with cashew, iroko timber and banana — trees whose leaves shade the precious cocoa pods and whose trunks help irrigate them thanks to their high-water content. Ivorian cocoa farmer Koffi Alexis Amani holds a cocoa pod at a plantation near Bouafle, on Sept 16, 2026. — AFP The research cannot come fast enough in Ivory Coast, predicted to be hit by extreme weather events like droughts or torrential rains in the coming decades. “The future of our orchards lies in research,” Yves Brahima Kone, who heads the cocoa industry’s regulatory body, said at the start of September. Temperatures, which have already risen by one degree Celsius between 1991 and 2020 according to a government report, could continue to climb by 1.7°C to 3.7°C by 2080, according to studies. If nothing is done, “by 2050, Ivory Coast’s export agriculture will suffer a decline in cocoa production of 20 per cent”, the government has warned. The country is not the only one likely to suffer — Europe, the world’s largest consumer of chocolate products, takes in 70pc of Ivorian cocoa exports. Header image: Geneticist Caudou Trebissou measures cocoa pods on trees in a cocoa seed field belonging to the National Centre for Agronomic Research (CNRA) near Divo, on Sept 15, 2026. — AFP
