items.title: Cour Suprême : pourquoi le procès d’Algassimou est suspend aussitôt ouvert ?
items.description: Le procès de l’ancien avocat général près la Cour suprême, Algassimou Diallo, a connu un nouveau contretemps ce jeudi 15 octobre 2026. À peine les débats ouverts, ses avocats ont introduit une requête en récusation visant trois magistrats de la juridiction : Ibrahima Sory I Tounkara, Yaya Boiro et Fatou Bangoura. La demande a été soumise aux chambres réunies de la Cour suprême, qui se sont retirées pour délibérer. Cette démarche suspend, au moins provisoirement, la poursuite des débats, dans l’attente de la décision de la juridiction sur la requête de la défense. Face à cette initiative, le procureur général, Sidy Souleymane N’Diaye, a invité la Cour à examiner la demande formulée par les conseils du prévenu. Un procès déjà marqué par un premier renvoi Cette nouvelle difficulté intervient après un premier renvoi prononcé le 8 septembre dernier. À l’époque, la Cour avait décidé d’ajourner l’affaire afin de permettre la comparution physique d’Algassimou Diallo et de donner à ses avocats un délai supplémentaire pour préparer sa défense. Le prévenu avait alors été signalé introuvable à la suite de son transfèrement de la prison civile de Coyah vers celle de Macenta. Des accusations que l’ancien magistrat devra affronter Algassimou Diallo, ancien avocat général près la Cour suprême, est poursuivi pour des faits présumés de « provocation à la discrimination, à la haine ou à la violence, de discrimination et d’association de malfaiteurs ». L’issue de l’examen de la requête en récusation devrait déterminer la suite de la procédure et les conditions dans lesquelles les débats pourront se poursuivre.

items.title: Visa For Music 2026 : Rabat dévoile la programmation de sa 13e édition
items.description: Du 18 au 21 novembre 2026, Rabat accueillera la 13e édition de Visa For Music, rendez-vous incontournable des musiques d’Afrique et du Moyen-Orient. Avec plus de 35 projets artistiques sélectionnés parmi plus de 900 candidatures issues de plus de 90 pays, le festival confirme son rayonnement international et son rôle dans le développement de l’industrie musicale. Rabat se prépare à vibrer au rythme des musiques du monde. Le festival et marché professionnel Visa For Music revient du 18 au 21 novembre 2026 pour une 13ᵉ édition placée sous le signe de la diversité musicale, de la découverte et des échanges internationaux. Considéré comme un rendez-vous majeur des industries musicales d’Afrique et du Moyen-Orient, l’événement réunit artistes, producteurs, programmateurs, tourneurs et directeurs de festivals autour d’un objectif commun : favoriser la circulation des œuvres, encourager les collaborations et ouvrir de nouvelles perspectives aux artistes. Pour cette édition, l’intérêt international se confirme avec plus de 900 candidatures reçues en provenance de plus de 90 pays. À l’issue du processus de sélection, plus de 35 projets artistiques ont été retenus pour composer la programmation officielle. La sélection 2026 met en avant des univers musicaux variés, mêlant sonorités traditionnelles, jazz, musiques électroniques, créations instrumentales et musiques urbaines. Elle témoigne de la richesse des scènes contemporaines et de leur capacité à faire dialoguer les cultures. Parmi les artistes et projets annoncés figurent notamment GnawaTronic, porté par Omary et Hind Ennaira, Meryem Aboulouafa, OumY, Yugen Blakrok, Delehei, Enzo Avitabile & I Bottari, ainsi que Moonshine. La programmation fait également la part belle aux talents marocains, avec la présence de Jbiina, R2D, Soufiane AZ, Onzy Jazzbar et Rita Kamale, entre autres. Des artistes venus du Brésil, du Bénin, du Sénégal, d’Afrique du Sud, de Chine, d’Italie, du Canada et de nombreux autres pays contribueront à cette édition, qui entend offrir un panorama ouvert sur les musiques actuelles et les nouvelles formes de création. Un marché professionnel au service de l’industrie musicale Au-delà des concerts, Visa For Music se distingue par sa dimension professionnelle. Le festival constitue une plateforme de rencontres et de coopération entre les différents acteurs de l’industrie musicale, en favorisant notamment les échanges Sud-Sud et Nord-Sud. Producteurs, programmateurs, agents artistiques, tourneurs et responsables de festivals y trouvent un espace pour nouer des partenariats, développer des projets et accompagner la diffusion internationale des artistes. Cette dimension fait de Visa For Music un outil de structuration de l’économie créative, dans un secteur où l’accès aux réseaux professionnels et aux marchés internationaux demeure un enjeu majeur pour de nombreux talents africains et moyen-orientaux. Rabat, carrefour culturel international À travers cette 13ᵉ édition, Rabat entend conforter sa place sur la scène culturelle internationale. Pendant quatre jours, la capitale marocaine accueillera artistes, professionnels, médias et mélomanes autour d’une programmation qui met en avant la diversité des expressions musicales et les échanges entre les cultures. En associant spectacles, rencontres professionnelles et opportunités de coopération, Visa For Music poursuit ainsi son ambition : contribuer au rayonnement des artistes et renforcer la visibilité des industries musicales d’Afrique et du Moyen-Orient. Le rendez-vous est fixé du 18 au 21 novembre 2026 à Rabat, pour une édition qui promet de faire de la capitale marocaine un point de convergence des musiques et des talents venus du monde entier. The post Visa For Music 2026 : Rabat dévoile la programmation de sa 13e édition appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Twelve Golden Rules of real estate development in Ghana, Africa
items.description: By Dr Prince-Joseph M. K. Ayiku Real estate development is one of Africa’s greatest opportunities for economic growth and wealth creation. With a young population, rapidly expanding cities, and rising demand for quality housing, commercial, industrial and mixed-use properties, the potential is enormous. However, success requires far more than buying land and constructing buildings. Many projects fail because developers start building before resolving fundamental issues. True success demands the right location, quality materials, careful research, secure title, sound financing, and disciplined execution. These twelve golden rules provide a practical blueprint from land acquisition to construction, sales and long-term estate management. Rule 1: Choose the Right Location The value of a property begins with where it stands. A beautiful building in the wrong location will struggle, while a well-planned property in the right location will enjoy strong demand and lasting value. Location determines accessibility, rental income, security, resale value and future growth. Developers must assess access to roads and transport, proximity to schools, hospitals and markets, availability of water, power and internet, security, environmental risks like flooding, population growth, and planning restrictions. A location must not be judged only by its present state, but by how it will develop in the next 10 to 20 years with new roads, hospitals and commercial centres. Rule 2: Build With Quality Materials and Workmanship Quality may cost more today, but poor construction will cost much more tomorrow. Quality is the foundation of a developer’s reputation. Developers must use durable, standards-approved materials and engage skilled, qualified professionals to supervise every stage. Cheap materials cause cracks, leakages, electrical faults and structural failure. Quality control must cover soil testing and foundations, concrete and steel, roofing and waterproofing, plumbing, electricals, doors and windows, finishes, roads and gutters and fire safety. Every stage should be inspected before the next begins. Never secretly reduce specifications to increase profit. Every completed property is a public advertisement. Rule 3: Conduct Proper Market Research Do not build what you want to sell. Build what the market wants to buy. Every project must satisfy a real, measurable need. Developers must not rely on personal excitement. Research must answer: Who is the buyer? What property type do they need? What price can they afford? What features and payment terms do they want? How fast are competing properties selling? Is demand from residents, investors, or diaspora? An excellent property that does not match the market will not sell. Research must guide location, design, size, price and payment terms before major funds are committed. Rule 4: Secure the Land Before Investing A building is only as secure as the title beneath it. Land is the foundation of every project, and land administration remains a major challenge in Africa, with multiple sales, unclear boundaries, family disputes and forged documents. Developers must conduct full legal and technical investigations before purchase, verifying the seller’s identity and authority, ownership history, boundaries, existing mortgages or court disputes, approved land use, rights of way, and family or traditional interests. Qualified lawyers and licensed surveyors must be involved from the start, with searches at the lands commission and traditional authorities. No large payments should be made before ownership is confirmed, and every agreement must be documented. Rule 5: Respect Planning Laws and the Environment Responsible development works with the environment, not against it. Developers must obtain all necessary approvals – planning permission, building permits, environmental and fire clearances – before construction. Wetlands, waterways, flood plains and protected areas must be respected. Building in unsuitable locations causes flooding, damage, and loss of life. Responsible development must preserve natural drainage, provide proper stormwater systems, and consider waste management, sanitation, landscaping and energy use. Compliance protects the investment, the environment and the occupants. Rule 6: Prepare a Complete Feasibility Study Before breaking ground, make certain that the figures can carry the project. Every proposal must be tested financially. A professional feasibility study must estimate land and legal costs, design fees, construction and infrastructure costs, financing and interest, taxes and permits, marketing and administrative costs, contingencies, expected sales income, completion period, and profit margin. Developers must test what happens if material costs rise, sales slow down, or interest rates increase. Expected sales are not guaranteed cash. Profitability and cash flow must be examined separately, as a profitable project can still collapse from cash shortages. Rule 7: Protect Cash Flow and Control Costs Profit is important, but cash keeps the project moving. Cash flow is the lifeblood of development. Developers must prepare detailed budgets and monthly cash flow forecasts, matching customer deposits, loans and sales proceeds against expenses. Project funds must be separated from personal spending. Customer deposits must be used responsibly for their intended projects. Strong controls must cover procurement, materials inventory, contractor payments, payroll, variations, receipts, loans and taxes. Management must compare actual spending against budget monthly and identify overruns early. Rule 8: Deliver Infrastructure, Not Only Buildings A house becomes a home when the surrounding community works. Successful communities need more than buildings. Buyers expect roads, drainage, water, electricity, security, waste services, street lighting and internet, plus schools, shops and recreation. Infrastructure costs must be included in the budget from the beginning, not as an afterthought. Where public infrastructure is limited, developers need partnerships with utility providers and local authorities. A developer who builds buildings completes a project; a developer who provides infrastructure creates a functioning community. Rule 9: Put the Customer at the Centre A property sale may happen once, but a customer’s experience lasts for years. The customer is the reason the project exists. Marketing must be truthful, with clear prices, specifications, payment terms and completion dates. Developers must avoid unfulfillable promises and communicate early and honestly when delays occur. A clear customer service process should cover enquiries, reservations, payments, progress reports, inspections, handover, defect reporting and after-sales support. Satisfied customers become ambassadors. Rule 10: Build a Competent and Accountable Team Strong buildings come from skilled hands, clear leadership and honest supervision. No developer can succeed alone. The team may include architects, engineers, surveyors, lawyers, accountants, marketers and contractors. Every person must have a clear role and measurable responsibility. Contractors should be selected not just on price, but on experience, financial strength, safety and reliability. Every appointment must have a written contract defining work, price, timeline and quality. Leaders must promote honesty and eliminate bribery, inflated invoices and material theft. Rule 11: Manage Risks and Prepare for Change The best developer does not ignore risk; the best developer prepares for it. Every project faces risks including land disputes, construction delays, rising material prices, currency and interest rate movements, weak demand, contractor failure, flooding, policy changes and safety incidents. Each project should have a risk register identifying each risk, its impact, responsible person and response plan. Suitable insurance must protect workers, buildings and third parties. Risk management does not remove all problems, but helps respond quickly and reduce losses. Rule 12: Develop for Profit, People, and Posterity The greatest developments do not only occupy land; they improve lives and create legacies. Profit is necessary for survival, but development carries wider responsibility. Every project affects traffic, drainage, employment, services and community life. Developers should create safe, attractive, inclusive places that consider children, older people and persons with disabilities, offer fair opportunities to local workers, engage communities respectfully, and plan for long-term maintenance of roads, drains, parks and common areas. The most respected developers are remembered not just for buildings completed, but for communities created. In conclusion, Africa does not simply need more buildings. It needs quality developments in the right locations that endure, create value and support human progress. Dr. Prince-Joseph M. K. Ayiku, the writer

items.title: Five new telephony cell sites in Ashanti Region to be activated in October 2026 – Sam George
items.description: The Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovation, Samuel Nartey George, has announced that five new telecommunications sites in the Ashanti Region are expected to be activated by the end of October 2026. He also disclosed plans to extend telecommunications services to three additional communities in the Sekyere Afram Plains District, directing the Ghana Investment Fund for Electronic Communications (GIFEC) and its contractors to accelerate work to improve connectivity in the area. Mr George announced this during an inspection of four Rural Telephony Project sites at Nyameama No. 1, Nyameama No. 2, Dawia and Abenua in the Sekyere Afram Plains District. The tour was intended to assess construction progress, identify implementation challenges and ensure the timely completion of outstanding works. The Minister said the Rural Telephony Project was designed to bridge the digital divide by extending network coverage to communities that mainstream telecommunications operators might consider commercially unviable. He noted that communities in the Sekyere Afram Plains District were among those prioritised for improved network coverage. He commended the area’s Member of Parliament for advocating better telecommunications services and reaffirmed the government’s commitment to addressing connectivity gaps across the country. Mr George also disclosed that the government was collaborating with MTN Ghana to deploy 800 additional telecommunications sites nationwide. He stressed the need to upgrade existing rural networks from 3G to 4G, warning that expanding digital services in urban centres without corresponding improvements in rural communities could widen the digital divide as Ghana moved towards broader 5G deployment. The Minister further announced plans to conduct a comprehensive audit of all Rural Telephony Project sites inherited by the current administration. The exercise will establish the actual completion status of the sites and verify whether facilities reported as operational are actively providing network services. He urged traditional authorities and residents to protect the installed equipment against vandalism to prevent service disruptions. The District Chief Executive for Sekyere Afram Plains, Abubakar Issaka, commended the Minister for prioritising the district’s connectivity needs and pledged the Assembly’s support in protecting and maintaining the facilities. The inspection formed part of the Minister’s ongoing efforts to monitor rural telecommunications projects, address implementation challenges and extend reliable digital connectivity to underserved communities. Mr George was accompanied by Mr Issaka, GIFEC Administrator Rashid Tanko and officials from the Ministry and GIFEC.

items.title: Trump says military execution of Fort Hood gunman will not be livestreamed
items.description: US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that the execution of the Fort Hood gunman would not be livestreamed, but that immediate families of the victims would be able to view it in person. Nidal Hasan’s execution — scheduled for Dec 3 at Fort Hood, Texas, where he gunned down 13 people in 2009 — is set to be the first by a US military firing squad since 1945. “I think streaming the execution for all to see might have been a strong deterrent for the World to witness how America deals with Terrorists and SCUM like Hasan but, many very good and well-meaning people would rather not watch him die through streaming or through any other visual device,” Trump wrote. “He will die, as scheduled, by firing squad, but this event will not be streamed. That said, the execution may be viewed in person by the immediate families of the victims, if they so choose. They deserve to witness JUSTICE!” Some of Trump’s fellow Republicans, including Vice President JD Vance, as well as religious leaders and international observers, had expressed doubts about the Pentagon’s plan to livestream the execution of Nidal Hasan. Recent polls have also shown a majority of Americans opposed livestreaming it. The United Nations said streaming the execution would amount to “torture,” while the president of the US Conference of Catholic Bishops said it was a “barbaric promotion of a culture of death,” and both Australia and Britain’s prime ministers described it as “abhorrent”. Hasan, a former US Army psychiatrist, was sentenced to death in August 2013, after a military jury found him guilty of 45 counts of premeditated murder and attempted premeditated murder. Twelve of the 13 people Hasan killed and 30 of those he wounded were soldiers. He was left partially paralysed and confined to a wheelchair from being shot by police during his arrest. The shooting came weeks before Hasan, now 56, was scheduled to be deployed to Afghanistan. Under US military law, a US president must approve an execution by firing squad. President Donald Trump did so on Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth’s recommendation, the Pentagon said last week. The last US military execution was carried out in 1961, when John Bennett was hanged for rape and attempted murder.

items.title: Wike warns politicians against manufacturing grievances to win power
items.description: ….Laments decline in presidential election turnout By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has warned politicians against manufacturing grievances to win power, saying the tactic can “become the weapon that divides the country tomorrow.” Wike gave the warning on Thursday in a keynote address titled “People, Politics and Power Play in Nigeria: The Agitation for Equity and Fairness,” delivered at the first Idoma Hall of Fame induction ceremony in Abuja. The event was held in collaboration with Ochetoha K’Idoma as part of the Idoma Centenary Plus celebration. “Leaders, in particular, must resist the temptation to manufacture or manipulate grievances for political advantage. The politics of identity can mobilise people quickly, but the instrument that mobilises supporters today can become the weapon that divides the country tomorrow. “Nigeria cannot build a durable future if every political entrepreneur discovers that the easiest route to power is to persuade one group that another group is its enemy or oppressor. “Our task, therefore, is not to eliminate political competition, but to civilise it; not to eliminate our differences, but to manage them justly. “Nigeria belongs to all of us,” he said. “No Nigerian should need permission to feel at home in Nigeria. That is the deeper meaning of equity”, he said. Wike also lamented the steady fall in voter turnout at presidential elections, citing figures from the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC. “The Independent National Electoral Commission has drawn attention to the continuing decline in voter participation: presidential-election turnout fell from 53.7 per cent in 2011 to 43.6 per cent in 2015, 34.7 per cent in 2019 and 26.7 per cent in 2023. These figures should concern every democrat,” the minister said. He said citizens were being treated as an afterthought between elections. “Democracy cannot flourish when citizens are treated merely as voters to be mobilised when elections approach. Citizens must participate because government belongs to them. Political parties must therefore see citizens as partners in governance, not merely as instruments for winning elections”, he said. He urged Nigerians to move from the politics of “whose turn?” to the politics of “what is right?”, describing this as “the enduring task.” On how power is shared, Wike raised questions about zoning and rotation without taking a position on them. “When does zoning promote stability, and when might it constrain open political competition? “When does federal character protect diversity, and when can its implementation create tensions with merit and competence?” he added, saying such questions “deserve neither simplistic answers nor partisan slogans.” The minister said appointments by identity did not remove the duty to perform. “Representation should open the door, not remove the obligation to perform once one enters. “A nation does not become just by appointing incompetent people merely because they come from an underrepresented group; neither does it become meritocratic by pretending that historical inequalities do not exist.” Wike said a citizen’s sense of inclusion could not rest on appointments alone. “A young Nigerian without employment does not necessarily experience political inclusion because someone from his ethnic group has become a minister.” He listed what he believed must be done to turn agitation into national renewal. “We must build political parties that practise genuine internal democracy; strengthen electoral institutions and protect the integrity of the ballot; make public appointments more transparent; enforce constitutional principles of inclusion; expand economic opportunity; improve the quality of education; and ensure that development reaches rural communities as well as metropolitan centres.” The minister also challenged communities to apply the same standard to themselves that they demand of others. Turning to the occasion, Wike described the Idoma Hall of Fame as “an institution for establishing standards,” saying it tells a community “what it considers worthy of remembrance, what it regards as worthy of emulation, and, ultimately, what it wants the next generation to become.” He said the Idoma story “must never be told merely as a story of grievance, exclusion or what was denied,” but also “as a story of contribution.” The post Wike warns politicians against manufacturing grievances to win power appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Reprise des activités juridictionnelles à la Cour suprême du Togo
items.description: Lomé, 15 oct. (ATOP) – Après les congés de juillet à septembre, les magistrats de la Cour suprême du Togo ont repris leurs activités juridictionnelles le 1 er octobre dernier. La rentrée solennelle du jeudi 15 octobre, coïncide avec le 3 e jeudi du mois, jour d’audience à la Cour suprême. La séance a été dirigée par le président de la Cour suprême Yaya Bawa Abdoulaye, en présence des membres de la cour, des membres du gouvernement, des avocats, des auxiliaires de justice et des plaignants. Elle a permis au président Abdoulaye de faire l’historique de ces trois mois de congés, qui d’après lui, est née de l’époque coloniale, où les expatriés ou colons magistrats devraient prendre du temps pour voyager et se reposer et retourner dans leur pays de travail, au cours de ces trois mois. C’est cette tradition qui est restée jusqu’à nos jours. Le président Abdoulaye a déploré la lenteur de traitement des affaires pendantes et a plaidé pour le renforcement de la Cour, en magistrats suffisants pour traiter les dossiers de pourvoi qui vont en nombre grandissant. Le secrétaire général de la Cour suprême du Togo, Kodjo Gabriel Woayi, a relevé que selon l’organisation judiciaire, la magistrature a 3 mois de congés à partir du mois de juillet, à septembre. Et au cours de cette période-là, chaque magistrat va choisir un mois pour avoir ses congés, ce qui réduit du coup, les activités juridictionnelles. Il poursuit qu’à partir du 1 er octobre, tous les magistrats, à quelque niveau qu’ils soient, doivent regagner leur service et reprendre leurs activités. « Donc pour la Cour suprême, c’est la première audience de la reprise des activités, qui coïncide avec date d’aujourd’hui », a-t-il renchéri. En clair, sur toute l’étendue du territoire, à partir du 1 er octobre, il n’y a plus de congé dans le corps de la magistrature, tous les magistrats sont à leur poste et les audiences reprennent normalement. A la Cour suprême, c’est la reprise des audiences. « Nous tenons les audiences chaque mois. Chaque troisième jeudi de chaque mois, il y a une audience à la chambre judiciaire. Donc c’est le démarrage des activités de la Cour suprême au niveau de la chambre judiciaire », a déclaré le secrétaire général. Les affaires pendantes à la Cour suprême, sont celles qui ont fait l’objet de pourvoi. « Quand on rend une décision au niveau du tribunal et que l’une des parties n’est pas satisfaite de la décision, elle interjette appel, la Cour d’appel rend son arrêt et là, si elle n’est toujours pas satisfaite, elle saisit la Cour suprême. C’est la Cour suprême maintenant, en tant que dernier recours, qui tranche. Et il y a deux possibilités : soit la cour rejette le pourvoi, ce qui veut dire que la cour d’appel a bien rendu son arrêt, ou elle casse l’arrêt de la cour d’appel et renvoie à la cour d’appel, ou bien elle casse sans renvoi et donne force au jugement qui a été rendu en première instance », a expliqué Me Waoyi. Au rôle de cette audience d’ouverture, plusieurs affaires dont des délibérés et des nouvelles. ATOP/KYA/HKM

items.title: 2027: Odii pledges ₦2trn investment for Ebonyi
items.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, governorship candidate in Ebonyi State, Ifeanyi Chukwuma Odii, has pledged to attract more than ₦2 trillion in private investment to the state within six months if elected governor in 2027. Odii made the pledge on Thursday during an interview on Arise Television’s The Morning Show, where he outlined plans to leverage his business network, improve the investment climate and unlock the state’s economic potential. The businessman expressed confidence that he could attract the investment, citing his relationships with entrepreneurs and investors as well as opportunities in solid minerals, real estate, manufacturing, hospitality and other sectors. He said his strategy would focus on policies and an enabling business environment capable of encouraging investors to establish businesses in Ebonyi and create economic opportunities for residents. “I have a very large network of people, friends. Some of them are businessmen, they’re entrepreneurs,” Odii said. He added that he had more than 2,000 business contacts who could be encouraged to invest in the state if the right conditions were created. Explaining his approach, the PDP candidate said investors were primarily interested in returns and that his proposed administration would introduce policies to make Ebonyi attractive to businesses. “I’ll come up with policies. I’ll create an enabling environment that will make these people to come in and put their money because they want to make profit,” he said. Odii described solid minerals as one of Ebonyi’s major investment opportunities, arguing that the state had significant economic potential that remained underutilised. He also identified real estate, manufacturing, industrial development, hospitality and other commercial activities as sectors that could benefit from increased private investment. The candidate said investors who had made profits in Lagos and other commercial centres could be encouraged to expand their operations into Ebonyi. During the interview, the presenter questioned how Odii intended to deliver on the ₦2 trillion pledge within six months and asked him to demonstrate a track record of attracting investments on that scale. In response, Odii cited his more than two decades of business experience and his involvement in companies operating in manufacturing, raw materials, chemical trading, construction and real estate. He identified himself as chairman and chief executive officer of Orient Global Group, which he said operates in manufacturing, processing and the trading of industrial and oil-and-gas chemicals. He also mentioned Optimus Holdings, which he said was involved in construction, real estate and related businesses. Odii said he started as a small trader before expanding his business activities and establishing relationships with multinational companies. He maintained that his private-sector experience would help him understand investors’ needs and formulate policies capable of attracting capital to Ebonyi. The ₦2 trillion investment target and six-month timeline are pledges made by the candidate ahead of the 2027 governorship election. items.title: UN and Switzerland plan Sudan peace talks as US lawmaker proposes resource partnership
items.description: The UN and Switzerland are preparing a sixth meeting to coordinate peace efforts in Sudan, while a US congressman has proposed an agricultural and mineral partnership tied to progress on civilian protection and political stability. The United Nations (UN) and Switzerland will co-host a sixth consultative meeting on coordinating peace initiatives in Sudan in Geneva, as international and regional actors continue efforts to end the war. UN spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric announced the meeting at Tuesday’s daily press briefing, saying further consultations between the five-party mechanism and Sudanese political stakeholders were expected in the coming weeks. The meeting will bring together countries sponsoring major peace initiatives, members of the Quartet and five-party mechanism, Sudan’s neighbouring states and permanent members of the UN Security Council. The five-party mechanism comprises the UN, the European Union (EU), the League of Arab States, the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) and the African Union (AU). Dujarric also referred to Monday’s meeting in Addis Ababa , which brought together anti-war civilian and political forces, including the Civil Democratic Alliance for Revolutionary Forces ( Somoud ). He said the consultations aim to prepare for an inclusive political dialogue led and owned by Sudanese people. The fifth consultative meeting took place in January. ‘Sudanese youth network calls for civilian oversight of peace talks’ The Youth Network for Civilian Oversight has proposed an independent mechanism to monitor Sudan peace talks, track ceasefire arrangements and humanitarian corridors, and improve public transparency. In a policy paper published yesterday, Towards a New Civil Architecture for Peace Processes, the network proposes a “Joint Civilian Engagement Window” to strengthen public participation and connect negotiations with communities affected by the war. ‘US lawmaker proposes Sudan resource partnership’ US Congressman Jim Baird, a Republican representing Indiana’s Fourth Congressional District, has introduced the proposed Sudan IMPACT Act, which would establish an agricultural and mineral partnership with Sudan conditional on progress in protecting civilians and achieving political stability. According to the Sudan Investing in Minerals, Partnership, Agriculture, Commerce and Trade (IMPACT) Act, introduced as H.R. 10795 , the proposed legislation provides US agricultural and mining equipment, technology and expertise in exchange for Sudanese natural resources. The partnership would depend on the US secretary of state determining that Sudan had made significant progress in civilian protection, political stability and responsible resource management. Baird said economic cooperation could help Sudanese people build a more peaceful and prosperous country but stressed that civilian protection must remain the priority. He added that Sudan’s mineral resources could supply materials used in technologies such as mobile phones and cars, while creating economic opportunities for Sudanese people. The proposed partnership could cover agricultural machinery, irrigation technology, food processing, geological surveys, mining safety and environmental remediation. The bill remains a proposal, with any partnership dependent on the conditions set out in the legislation being met. items.title: A Pékin, Faure Gnassingbé honore la mémoire des héros du peuple chinois
items.description: Lomé, 15 oct. (ATOP)- Le Président du Conseil, Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé, a rendu hommage aux héros du peuple chinois, ce mardi 13 octobre 2026, à Pékin, une étape symbolique de sa visite officielle en Chine. Sur la place Tian’anmen, haut lieu de l’histoire nationale chinoise, le Président Faure Gnassingbé a procédé à un dépôt de gerbe au Monument des Héros du Peuple, avant de se recueillir en mémoire de ceux qui se sont sacrifiés pour l’indépendance, la souveraineté et le développement de la Chine. Cette cérémonie s’inscrit dans la tradition diplomatique, où les gestes symboliques accompagnent le dialogue politique et les initiatives de rapprochement entre les nations. Elle rappelle ainsi la qualité du partenariat entre le Togo et la Chine depuis l’établissement de leurs relations diplomatiques en 1972. Au fil des années, les deux pays ont renforcé leurs échanges et diversifié les domaines de coopération. Ces liens ont franchi une nouvelle étape le même jour, à l’occasion de la rencontre entre le Président du Conseil, Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé et le Président chinois, Xi Jinping, au Grand Palais du Peuple. Les deux dirigeants ont annoncé l’élévation des relations bilatérales au niveau d’une « Communauté d’avenir partagé Chine-Togo à l’ère nouvelle », ouvrant ainsi une nouvelle étape de partenariat. presidenceduconseil.gouv.tg

items.title: 2027: No vacancy in senate presidency, senators declare
items.description: By Henry Umoru, Abuja Ahead of January 16, 2027, National Assembly elections and nine months to the inauguration of presiding officers for the incoming 11th Senate, the Senate has declared that there is no vacancy in the office of the Senate President. With this development, strong indications have emerged that the doors may have been closed for those who intend to contest for the presiding offices of the President of the Senate and that of the Deputy President of the Senate, as serving senators vowed to return Godswill Akpabio and Barau Jibrin as President and Deputy President of the Senate unopposed. The senators, also through voice vote affirmation, have resolved to return any of the current principal officials who win the January 16 National Assembly election back into their various seats. They include the Senate Leadership position currently being occupied by Senator Opeyemi Banidele, APC, Ekiti Central; the Senate Whip position, currently occupied by Senator Tahir Monguno, APC, Borno North; and the position of Deputy Whip currently occupied by Peter Nwaebonyi (Ebonyi North). Others resolved to be returned unopposed if they emerged victorious in the January 16, 2027 National Assembly Election, are the Minority Leader, Senator Abba Moro, PDP, Benue South; Deputy Minority Leader, Senator Oyewumi Olalere, Accord, Osun West; and Minority Whip, Senator Tony Nwoye, NDC, Anambra North. The senators unanimously took the decision on Thursday following comments during plenary by the President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio, who cautioned the public against misinterpreting his comments on the bill seeking to decriminalise attempted suicide. In his remarks, Akpabio explained that his remarks on the bill, which scaled second reading on Tuesday, were being twisted, underscoring that terrorists have no religion and that those destabilising the country are not Nigerians. He added that suicide is forbidden as a Christian and that discussions around decriminalisation are in line with modern legislative practice. It was during discussions on the lead debate on the general principles of a bill to establish a framework for suicide prevention, decriminalise attempted suicide and provide for the establishment of persons who attempt suicide that the bill to this effect has scaled second reading in the Senate. The bill scaled second despite the position of the President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio, who insisted that the act should remain punishable by imprisonment, saying, ‘If you attempt suicide, make sure you die, and anyone who attempts and fails will go to jail.’ However, Akpabio maintained that attempted suicide should remain a criminal offence, arguing that removing the penalties could encourage the act, arguing thus, “If you attempt suicide, make sure you die. Anyone who attempts and fails will go to jail.” Akpabio had added that the issue involves both the Criminal Code and the Penal Code, requiring input from State Houses of Assembly during a public hearing to avoid legal conflicts. The proposed bill seeks to remove the conflict between existing criminal laws that punish attempted suicide and the National Mental Health Act, which recognises the need for medical intervention in mental health emergencies, just as it seeks to address what he described as a contradiction in Nigeria’s laws. It is titled A Bill to Establish a Framework for Suicide Prevention, Decriminalise Attempted Suicide and Provide for the Establishment of Persons Who Attempt Suicide, and for Related Matters 2006 (SB.730). It was sponsored by Senator Ekpenyong Asuquo, APC, Cross River South. No vacancy stance of senators in the 10th Senate on leadership positions in the 11th Senate was a sequel to a motion moved to that effect by the Whip of the Senate, Senator Tahir Monguno, and seconded by Senator Cyril Fasuyi, Ekiti North, just as this affirmed that the seat of the Senate President is not vacant and will remain occupied by Senator Godswill Akpabio. Monguno said, “Insha Allah, by the grace of God, the majority of us are going to make it back to the senate, and this seat is hereby declared: there is no vacancy. Sir, including the seat of DSP, there is no vacancy, including principal officers.” On his part, Fasuyi said, “Mr President, distinguished colleagues, I hereby support the motion ably moved by Senator Monguno. My name is Senator Cyril Fasuyi from Ekiti, North, a serving senator and an incoming senator in the 11th Assembly. I hereby support the motion, ably moved by Senator Monguno, that the seat of the Senate President in the 11th assembly is not open to any contest. It is already occupied by Senator Godwill Obot Akpabio. I so support. Thank you.” On his part, Senator Babangida Hussaini, APC, Jigawa North West, reaffirmed Akpabio’s contributions to his state, endorsing his return, and raised concerns over hard drugs and substance abuse, which he said must be addressed to defuel criminality, bandits and terrorism in the country. Senator Hussaini, who referred to Surah An-Nisa, chapter 4, verse 29, of the Quran, said, “The Quran specifically and unambiguously prohibits taking one’s own life and killing another person. There is no question of anybody taking their own life or another person’s life under any pretext. Allah has completely forbidden that. “Secondly, regarding your character and personality, the people of Kazaure will forever remain grateful to you because, at the Federal Polytechnic, Kazaure, you constructed a hostel accommodating more than 300 female students in 2010, during your time as governor. “Your personality and contribution to national development are established, and that cannot be changed. “When people want to argue, they hardly take the time to consult the Quran to understand Islam’s position on these social issues. Most of what we see concerning suicide bombings and people killing themselves involves disturbed individuals, a phenomenon found everywhere. It does not belong to any particular religion. “Unfortunately, distinguished colleagues, one area we have failed to address seriously is the influence of hard drugs and other substances on our youths. “Many young suicide bombers and people involved in criminal enterprises are influenced by hard drugs and other substances. “Until we are able to identify, track and block the sources of these harmful substances entering our society, we will continue to have this problem.” Thereafter, Akpabio then asked, “Is this the general view of the senate? Those in support say aye. The ayes from the senate were resoundingly loud. Akpabio continued thus, “And those against say nay. They are not here. I think that settles it.” Monguno moved the motion on the strength of submission made by Akpabio that, based on realities on the ground, the positions of the President and Vice President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria are beyond the reach of any new contender, making them eyeing the Senate Presidency position through negative media reports against him. According to the president of the senate, because of 2027, political detractors twisted what he said in the Senate during plenary on Tuesday this week to pitch him against the Muslim community in Nigeria during debate on the motion to decriminalise suicide attempts. Akpabio, who warned that no one who kills others in the name of suicide should expect heaven or paradise and urged television commentators to be wary of misrepresenting Senate proceedings, further noted that his ADC of 19 years is a Muslim, insisting he would never speak disparagingly about any religion. The President of the Senate jocularly stated that ‘The position of president and vice president is gone; the only one left is the position of the senate president, so anyone can talk down on me.’ Akpabio said, “I just want to drop a word of caution: when we discuss here, we discuss for and against, and in the cause of our discussions, whatever we say should not anger anybody outside this chamber, because at the end, what matters is our final decision. “I’m saying this because when my brother, Distinguished Senator Asuquo, brought a bill to discuss suicide, whether we should criminalise or decriminalise suicide, there were many comments that came out, and one of the comments that came out from the chair, a senator, came here and said, ‘What about terrorists who believe that if they kill, they will go to heaven and seven virgins will be waiting for them, but I want you to know that terrorists are not Muslims.’ “Terrorists are not Christians. Terrorists are human beings who believe in taking their lives and the lives of others. Many states of this federation are not interested in suicide bombing, but there are some people that, out of drugs or out of pecuniary reasons, undertake suicide bombings; those ones do not belong to any religion. The Muslim religion that I know forbids suicide; it forbids killing. “The Muslim religion that I know does not even allow somebody to take his own life, and if you look at the Quran, the Quran not only prohibits suicide; it also says that if you commit suicide, you will not enter into paradise, so if we are saying that if you kill, you have 14 or 7 or 70 virgins waiting for you in paradise, you cannot even enter paradise if you commit suicide. “So, people who are misinterpreting what we discuss here, I just want them to know that. Most of these people, more than 70 per cent, are not Nigerians; those who are are destabilising the security of this country. You need to know that, and so when we come here, there is no way we can sit as fathers and mothers and then encourage our children to go and commit suicide. # “I’m a Catholic in the Catholic religion, and in Christianity, suicide is also forbidden in the penal code of this country; suicide is also forbidden; it’s even a criminal act. The same thing with the criminal code. You have to distinguish between suicide committed by people who are mentally disturbed and suicide intentionally committed by people who are physically sound, so anybody that thinks he is committing suicide by killing others because he wants to go to heaven and see virgins, there will be no virgin for you, because the religion already says that if you commit suicide, you cannot go to that heaven; you cannot go to that paradise. “So when people sit down in panels to dissect and discuss, I know this is a politically charged period. I don’t like the idea of people sitting down on television and trying to misinterpret what we discuss here in the senate. We want to make the best laws, so we are bound to oppose each other, and we are also bound to support each other. “No matter the discussion, please take the final decision of the senate into consideration. Don’t go and sit down in panels and try to do politically motivated discussions. The Senate President believes strongly in the Christian religion and believes strongly in the Muslim religion. “Even as a governor, I sponsored 5,800 Muslims to the Holy Land, and I know I sponsored more than 10,000 Christians to also go to Rome and also go to Jerusalem. Go and look at the people working for me: my ADC for 19 years is a Muslim. I don’t recognise him as a Muslim. I recognise him as a brother; he’s from Azare in Bauchi State, the same thing with my CSO. Come and see the number of people working for me, and you’ll see that more than 65 per cent of They are Muslims. There’s no way I will talk down on Muslim religion, so people who go out there to talk should study the personalities involved. In this politically charged period, people should go and face the truth and discuss issues, not try to damage people’s reputations. “I know the position of president is gone. The position of vice president is gone. The only one that is left now is the position of senate president, so everybody will want to contest that. And then will want to mobilise.” However, when asked to react to the Senate’s spontaneous action after the plenary, Senator Ali Ndume (Borno South) said he was not in the chamber when the resolution was taken. “I was not in the chamber when the said resolution was taken,” he said. Recall that prelude to yesterday’s development, the lawmakers had in May carried out an amendment to the Senate Standing Orders restricting eligibility for the office of Senate President and other principal positions to ranking lawmakers of the 10th Senate who secure re-election into the 11th Senate in 2027. According to him, the action is not only self-serving but also undemocratic and unconstitutional, saying that with this development, what the Senate has done is to show a lack of confidence in electing leaders and may be forcing a determined leadership in the Senate. After a marathon executive session on May 5th, 2026, the Senate carried out an amendment that introduced stricter eligibility criteria for the emergence of presiding officers in the 11th Senate, effectively limiting the contest for Senate president and other top leadership offices to returning ranking lawmakers of the current Assembly. With this development, the revised rules and preferences for Senate leadership positions will now follow a hierarchy beginning with former Senate Presidents, former Deputy Senate Presidents, former Principal Officers, senators who have completed at least one full term, lawmakers transitioning from the House of Representatives, and finally first-time senators where no higher-ranking candidates emerge. The amendment also stipulates that only senators returning from the current 10th Assembly after re-election can contest the Senate presidency and other key leadership offices. But on May 8, 2026, the Senate made a dramatic U-turn on its controversial amendment barring first-time senators from contesting for presiding offices, reopening the race for Senate President and Deputy Senate President in the 11th National Assembly. The reversal effectively threw open the 2027 Senate leadership contest to all elected senators, regardless of tenure, ending attempts to restrict the race to ranking lawmakers returning from the current Assembly. items.title: Trump scraps plan to livestream firing squad execution
items.description: The firing squad execution of a convicted military base shooter will not be livestreamed, US President Donald Trump announced Thursday, canceling a contentious plan by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. The move to livestream Nidal Hasan’s execution was widely opposed at home and abroad, prompting outrage from both US Democratic and Republican politicians, the Catholic Church, rights groups and the United Nations. The cancellation is a blow to Hegseth, who is already under fire over the stalemated Iran war and its fallout, which are weighing on the Republican Party’s chances in upcoming midterm elections. Hasan “will die, as scheduled, by firing squad, but this event will not be streamed,” Trump said in a post on his Truth Social platform. The US president indicated that he did not personally oppose the streaming plan, saying that it “might have been a strong deterrent for the World to witness how America deals with Terrorists and SCUM like Hasan.” But “many very good and well meaning people would rather not watch him die,” Trump said, adding that the execution could still be viewed in person by immediate family of the victims if they wanted to do so. Hasan’s execution — scheduled for December 3 at Fort Hood, Texas, where he gunned down 13 people in 2009 — is set to be the first by a US military firing squad since 1945. Hegseth said last week that “we’ll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it’s public,” later confirming that the plan was to livestream the execution. items.title: Mahama cuts sod for Afienya Industrial Park, targets 120 enterprises
items.description: President John Mahama has cut the sod for the construction of the Afienya Industrial Park, a major industrial development expected to accommodate more than 120 enterprises and create jobs as part of the government’s efforts to position Ghana as a manufacturing and logistics hub for West Africa. The 1,238-acre industrial park is expected to provide businesses with serviced plots, ready-to-use factory shells and essential infrastructure, including electricity, water, roads, drainage, waste treatment facilities and security. Speaking at the sod-cutting ceremony, President Mahama said the project responds to growing investor interest in Ghana and the need to provide space and infrastructure for businesses to establish factories and expand production. “When the Ghana Free Zones Authority informed me that the Tema Export Processing Zone had no space left to allocate to interested industries, it was an encouraging sign of investor interest in Ghana’s economic progress,” he said. He added that the government has a responsibility to ensure that the growing interest translates into factories, jobs and increased exports. “Today, we take an important step towards fulfilling our commitment to make Ghana a manufacturing and logistics hub for the West African sub-region,” President Mahama stated. The President said the Afienya Industrial Park will address some of the challenges investors face in acquiring land and setting up businesses, particularly disputes over land ownership and the cost of providing essential services. He assured investors that the new industrial enclave would offer litigation-free land and the necessary infrastructure to facilitate the establishment of factories. “You come, the land is litigation-free, the services will be available, and we will bring the power, the water, the waste treatment plants, security, roads, everything here,” he said. “All you need is to come, build your factory, bring your machines, and start to produce.” President Mahama said the project would receive infrastructure financing support under the government’s proposed $10 billion New Economy Programme, which is expected to invest $2 billion annually over four years in productive sectors of the economy. He said half of the planned investment would go into agriculture and agro-processing, with the remainder supporting industry and infrastructure linking producers to markets. “The New Economy Programme will assist the Free Zones Authority to provide these facilities for the Afienya enclave,” he said, adding that the full framework would be presented to Parliament in the 2027 Budget. The President said the industrial park’s location along the Eastern Corridor Road, its proximity to the Port of Tema and the Tema-Mpakadan standard-gauge railway line would give businesses a strategic advantage in transporting raw materials and finished products to domestic, regional and international markets. Priority investment areas include cocoa, cashew and oil palm processing, textiles and garments, pharmaceuticals, medical consumables, automotive components and assembly, and light engineering. The park is also expected to create opportunities in logistics, data services, business process outsourcing, renewable energy and green manufacturing. President Mahama stressed that the benefits of the project must extend beyond businesses operating within the industrial park to surrounding communities, including Afienya. He called for local farmers, transport operators, suppliers and small businesses to be integrated into the supply chains of companies that establish operations there. “I believe that if enterprises are located here, there should be a programme that trains the local people so that they can get some of the jobs created in this industrial park,” he said. President Mahama said the Afienya Industrial Park should build on the experience of the Tema Export Processing Zone by strengthening local industrial production, creating sustainable employment and expanding Ghana’s export capacity. “Establish your businesses here, develop your products here, and use Ghana as the launching pad to reach customers across Africa and beyond,” he urged investors. He expressed confidence that the private sector would respond to the opportunities created by the project, adding that the ultimate measure of success would be operational businesses, employment for Ghanaians and products reaching wider African markets.

items.description: Lomé, 15 oct. (ATOP)- Le Président du Conseil, Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé, s’est entretenu, le 13 octobre 2026 à Pékin, avec Zhao Leji, Président du Comité permanent de l’Assemblée populaire nationale (APN) de Chine. A cette occasion, Zhao Leji a réaffirmé sa volonté d’œuvrer à la consolidation des relations d’amitié et de coopération sino-togolaises, élevées au rang de « Communauté d’avenir partagé Chine-Togo à l’ère nouvelle » par le Président chinois Xi Jinping et le Président Faure Gnassingbé. Dans cette perspective, le Président du Comité permanent de l’Assemblée populaire nationale (APN) a mis en évidence la nécessité d’approfondir la confiance politique mutuelle et de renforcer les échanges entre les peuples chinois et togolais, conformément aux orientations définies par les plus hauts dirigeants des deux pays. Sur le plan parlementaire, Zhao Leji a exprimé la volonté de l’Assemblée populaire nationale de Chine de renforcer les échanges avec les deux chambres du Parlement togolais. Il a également mis l’accent sur l’importance d’une coordination accrue au sein des instances multilatérales, notamment l’Union interparlementaire, afin de favoriser le dialogue et la coopération entre les institutions législatives. Pour sa part, Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé a réaffirmé l’intérêt du Togo d’approfondir sa coopération pragmatique avec la Chine, notamment à travers le renforcement du dialogue et des échanges entre les organes législatifs des deux pays, ainsi que la consolidation de leur concertation au sein des instances multilatérales. Cette rencontre témoigne de la volonté de Lomé et de Pékin de poursuivre le renforcement de leur partenariat stratégique, en privilégiant le dialogue politique, la coopération institutionnelle et l’exploration de nouvelles perspectives de collaboration mutuellement bénéfiques. presidenceduconseil.gouv.tg

items.title: Nigeria Airways pension payments stalled by FEC in 2006 — Fani-Kayode
items.description: By Dickson Omobola Former Minister of Aviation, Femi Fani-Kayode, has said members of the Federal Executive Council, FEC, rejected a proposal to pay pensioners of the defunct Nigeria Airways in 2006, prolonging their wait for their entitlements. Fani-Kayode, now Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, said he submitted the memo after a committee chaired by the then Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, Yayale Ahmed, recommended the release of funds to settle the pensioners. He said the proposal was opposed by some cabinet members who blamed former boards and management teams of the national carrier for its collapse. Fani-Kayode spoke in response to a statement by the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, who said President Bola Tinubu was clearing the backlog left by previous administrations over the non-payment of pensions and gratuities to former Nigeria Airways workers. In a post on X, Fani-Kayode said the problems that led to the airline’s collapse predated former President Olusegun Obasanjo’s return to office in 1999. According to him, Nigeria Airways had 32 functional aircraft when Obasanjo left office as military head of state in 1979, alongside experienced pilots and crew members, a competent management team and an accountable board. However, he said that by the time Obasanjo returned to power in 1999, the airline had only one aircraft left, which was not operational, while most of its assets had disappeared and the company was heavily indebted. Fani-Kayode attributed the airline’s decline between 1979 and 1999 to alleged corruption, mismanagement, mounting debts and operational failures. He said the company’s liquidation in 2004 followed years of decline and unsuccessful attempts to rescue it, including privatisation advice from the International Finance Corporation, which later withdrew. According to him, the Obasanjo administration had little choice but to liquidate the airline rather than continue providing public funds to sustain it. He said the liquidation left the payment of workers’ pensions as the outstanding issue. “After a committee that was chaired by Alhaji Yayale Ahmed, the then Head of Service, recommended that money should be released and paid to the pensioners, as Minister of Aviation in 2006, I presented a memo to the Federal Executive Council for that purpose and argued strongly that this was the right thing to do,” he said. Fani-Kayode said the memo was rejected because some members of the cabinet believed former workers of the airline did not deserve pensions because of their alleged roles in its collapse. He said he and those who supported the proposal were outnumbered during the deliberations, resulting in the matter being deferred. According to him, the issue was revisited by the administration of former President Umaru Musa Yar’Adua, which came to power in 2007 and paid most of the pensioners. He added that the administration of former President Muhammadu Buhari continued the payments, while the remaining entitlements had now been settled under Tinubu. Fani-Kayode commended the payment of the outstanding pensions, saying the former workers had suffered for years while waiting for their entitlements. “It is gratifying that under your leadership the remainder of the pensions have been paid. I only wish we had done that when we were in office. The pensioners suffered immensely over the years. I have always maintained that paying them was the right thing to do,” he said. items.title: Chine-Togo : l’innovation technologique au service de la transformation économique
items.description: Lomé, 15 oct. (ATOP)- Le Président du Conseil, Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé, entend faire du partenariat sino-togolais, notamment dans le domaine de l’innovation technologique, un levier d’accélération de la transformation structurelle de l’économie nationale. En visite officielle en Chine, il a su placer la diplomatie au cœur de cette ambition à travers une immersion effectuée ce 14 octobre 2026 dans les écosystèmes d’innovation. Au Monde des robots, le Président du Conseil a pu apprécier les avancées de la robotique et le potentiel de l’automatisation dans des secteurs clés tels que l’industrie, la logistique, l’agriculture et les services. Cette démarche ouvre des perspectives de coopération entre le Togo et la Chine, notamment en matière de transfert de savoir-faire, de développement des compétences technologiques et de promotion de l’innovation. Le Président du Conseil s’est également rendu à l’exposition consacrée à la technologie 6G où il a su explorer la prochaine génération des télécommunications. Avec les avancées attendues en matière de connectivité et d’intégration de l’intelligence artificielle, cette visite dessine de nouveaux horizons pour la transformation numérique. Déjà engagé dans le développement des services numériques, le Togo poursuit ses efforts pour améliorer la connectivité, renforcer la formation et développer les compétences nationales. Cette dynamique s’étend également au secteur éducatif, engagé dans une transformation portée par plusieurs réformes structurelles, dont la création de l’Ecole Nationale Polytechnique (ENP) et l’opérationnalisation des Classes-Métiers dès l’année scolaire 2026-2027. Elles ambitionnent également de promouvoir l’adoption des technologies émergentes et d’accélérer la transformation numérique des entreprises et des services publics, contribuant ainsi au renforcement des compétences nationales et à la modernisation de l’économie togolaise. Cette orientation vise à favoriser l’intégration du numérique dans les pratiques pédagogiques, à rapprocher les apprentissages des réalités du monde professionnel et à mieux préparer les jeunes aux exigences du marché du travail. D’ores et déjà, les deux structures visitées ont marqué leur adhésion à la politique de valorisation technologique et d’innovation portée par le Président du Conseil. Elles se sont engagées à offrir des formations gratuites aux meilleurs étudiants togolais dans les domaines des technologies de pointe. Cet engagement constitue une avancée concrète dans le renforcement de la coopération technologique sino-togolaise. Il permettra de préparer une nouvelle génération de talents togolais aux métiers d’avenir. presidenceduconseil.gouv.tg

items.title: Drone attack kills two in North Darfur as Red Crescent volunteer killed in Blue Nile
items.description: Drone attack in Furawiya area of North Darfur kills two and injures eight, while a Red Crescent volunteer dies in a bombing in Blue Nile and South Darfur authorities impose sweeping emergency measures. Two people were killed and eight others injured in a drone attack in the Furawiya area on Wednesday evening, according to the Karnoi Emergency Room, as violence and security measures continued to affect several parts of Sudan. In a report, the emergency room said preliminary information indicated that the attack burned two vehicles and targeted three others south of the market. The emergency room said telecommunications outages and the lack of access to Starlink satellite internet had made it difficult to contact volunteers across the area. The Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Joint Force control the localities of Karnoi and El Tina on the Sudan–Chad border in North Darfur, while areas bordering West Darfur continue to witness fighting with the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF). ‘Red Crescent volunteer killed in Blue Nile bombing’ The Sudanese Red Crescent Society announced the death of Badr El Din Omar Musa, a volunteer with its Blue Nile branch, who was killed while carrying out humanitarian work in the Umm Darfa area on Wednesday. Musa had been working with emergency teams providing primary healthcare at a health centre when the area came under bombardment, the society said. His death brings to 25 the number of Red Crescent volunteers killed since the war began in April 2023. The society called on all parties to respect and protect humanitarian workers and civilians and refrain from targeting medical facilities. ‘Three residents reportedly arrested in Blue Nile’ Separately, the Civil Society Initiative in the Blue Nile region reported that a security unit had arrested three residents of El Roseires locality and taken them to an undisclosed location without explanation. A source from the initiative told Radio Dabanga that the men were Elrah Younis Babiker, Elbagir Elamin Saad and Jabara Abdallah. The source said the men had been blindfolded when they were taken away and cited information indicating that they had been tortured. ‘South Darfur imposes three-month emergency measures’ In South Darfur, the head of the civil administration, Salah Ahmed Ismail, known as ‘El Mouj’, has issued an emergency order introducing sweeping security restrictions , including a ban on carrying weapons at markets and public gatherings. The order, which took effect immediately for three months and may be renewed, also prohibits speech, publications and activities deemed to incite hatred or racism. It bans firearms at markets and public gatherings, except those carried by authorised security personnel. It also prohibits celebratory gunfire at public and private events and the display of weapons inside vehicles. The order tasks the Joint Forces, the RSF and the federal police with securing markets and public gatherings, placing guards under police supervision. It cites the Emergency and Protection of Public Safety Act of 1997 and recommendations from the state security committee as its legal and administrative basis. ‘Restrictions on ethnic gatherings and publications’ The order prohibits ethnic gatherings, correspondence and banners that incite hatred or racism . It also bars the publication or circulation of news deemed likely to undermine public security or provoke racist discord. It prohibits tribal interference in civil, criminal and legal cases, while allowing mediation and reconciliation efforts. The measures also provide for judicial proceedings and military trials for military personnel who side with their tribes in conflicts described in the order as racist in nature. ‘Ban on military uniforms and illicit trade’ The order prohibits civilians from wearing military uniforms and bans trafficking in narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances, smuggling resources, obscuring vehicle identification and handling stolen goods. It also provides immunity for members of the regular forces while carrying out their duties, in accordance with the order’s provisions. The authorities have been instructed to implement the measures immediately, with the stated aims of improving security, curbing instability and promoting peaceful coexistence in South Darfur. Those who violate the order face up to one year in prison, a fine of up to SDG10 million, or both. Authorities may also confiscate materials and equipment used in offences, while repeat violations carry doubled penalties.
