items.title: Teacher, 30 students killed in Peshawar school roof collapse
items.description: PESHAWAR: At least 31 people, including 30 students and a female teacher, were killed when a school roof collapsed in the provincial capital’s Afridi Abad area on Thursday. Lady Reading Hospital (LRH) spokesperson Muhammad Asim initially told Dawn that the death toll had risen to 33, including a female teachers and students aged between seven and 14 and a female teacher. Later, he said that 30 students students and a female teacher had been killed. According to the official list of casualties shared by LRH, a total of 61 people were brought to the facility, of which 30 were discharged after being treated. Residents gather during a search operation after a roof collapsed at a school in Peshawar on October 15. —AFP A spokesman for Rewscue 1122 said schoolchildren were crushed and trapped after the roof gave way. “When the Rescue 1122 emergency response teams arrived at the scene, they found that one roof had collapsed onto another, causing the classroom below to be crushed and trapping children inside,” spokesman Bilal Ahmad Faizi said. Speaking to Geo News , Peshawar Deputy Commissioner Afaq Wazir confirmed that the rescue operation launched after the collapse had concluded. “Rescue teams have cleared all the debris, and no more injured children are at the scene,” he said. Following the incident, an emergency was declared at the hospital, said the LRH spokesperson in an earlier statement. Peshawar DC earlier told Dawn that the roof of Al-Khair School had collapsed, trapping students beneath the debris. According to a statement issued by his office, students were present in their classrooms when the incident occurred. A rescue official told AFP that the ceiling came down on the students after the roof of a higher floor collapsed, crumpling the two storeys. Peshawar Capital City Police Officer (CCPO) Dr Mian Saeed Ahmed said the building’s structure was weak. “Its roof was overweight with construction on a weak structure that caused the collapse,” AFP quoted him as saying. A girl who was injured after a school roof collapse receives first aid at a hospital in Peshawar October 15, 2026. —AFP Speaking to Dawn , Samiullah, a parent who rushed to the site after hearing about the incident, said he had rescued three girls, all under the age of eight. “I received a call from home at around 8:50am and reached the site about 10 minutes later, at around 9am. We have six children studying at the school,” he said. “When I saw the building, I thought my son, who was in a ground-floor classroom beneath the collapsed first floor, had also died. However, he had left the classroom to drink water,” he added. Resident Sohail told AFP “everyone began screaming in panic” after his niece managed to find her way home after escaping the building to inform them of the collapse. “When I arrived at the scene, I saw around 10 to 15 children trapped beneath the rubble, with debris piled up to their necks. We quickly pulled them out,” he said. Volunteers and relatives shift the body of a victim, killed after a roof collapsed at a school, into an ambulance outside a hospital in Peshawar on October 15, 2026. —AFP KP governor orders audit Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi expressed grief over the deaths in the school roof collapse and sought a detailed report on the incident. He also directed the authorities to determine the cause of the collapse. “The loss of precious lives of innocent children is an extremely painful tragedy,” he said, according to a statement, extending his heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families. He prayed for the speedy recovery of the injured children and directed the authorities concerned to provide them with the best possible medical facilities. In another statement on his X account, the KP governor added that he had also directed a structural safety audit of educational institutions across the province to “identify potential risks and ensure that immediate corrective measures are taken wherever necessary”. “We cannot allow the safety of our children to be compromised,” Kundi wrote. Later, Kundi also attended the funeral prayers of the dead. Speaking to the media, he said that a team had been constituted to probe the incident and the inquiry was underway. “The first step will be to determine who issued the no-objection certificate to the school,” he said. Kundi also announced that the bereaved families would be given Rs1m as compensation while the injured would be given Rs200,000. “A transparent investigation into the incident will be conducted and those responsible will be identified,” he said. Meanwhile, the Elementary and Secondary Education Department constituted a fact-finding committee to probe the incident and tasked it with submitting a report on Thursday. The committee included: Javid Iqbal, the chairman of the Private Schools Regularity Authority; Muhammad Farooq, the deputy secretary of the Elementary and Secondary Education Department; and a member to be co-opted by a committee. The committee was tasked with probing the incident and ascertaining the facts that led to the roof collapse, unearthing the factors that led to it, suggesting measures to prevent such incidents in the future and making appropriate recommendations. Separately, KP Inspector General (IG) Zulfiqar Hameed ordered Peshawar CCPO to oversee the rescue operation and directed the traffic police to establish a “green corridor” to ensure uninterrupted movement of ambulances. Rescue and police teams were directed to utilise all available resources, a statement said. “In this hour of grief, KP police stands with the affected families,” the IGP was quoted as saying. Residents and rescue workers gather near an ambulance after a school roof collapse in Peshawar Pakistan on October 15.—Reuters PM Shehbaz takes ‘serious notice’ Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has taken “serious notice” of the incident, as he offered his condolences to the bereaved families in a post on X. “Our children are our most precious asset, and every such loss is a tragedy for the entire country,” DPM Dar said. He added that “ensuring the safety and protection of our children must remain paramount”. “All necessary measures must be taken to provide immediate assistance to those affected, ensure the best possible medical care for the injured, and strengthen safety standards in our schools to prevent such tragedies from recurring.” PM Shehbaz also phone the KP governor according to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO). The prime minister offered condolences to the families of the deceased and directed authorities to provide the best possible medical facilities to the injured and all possible assistance to the affected families, the statement said. The prime minister also sought a comprehensive report on the incident. The governor briefed the prime minister on the incident and informed him that the school owner had been arrested and an investigation into the incident had been launched. The prime minister directed that all aspects of the incident be examined and action be taken against those responsible in accordance with the law, the statement added. Condolences President Asif Ali Zardari also expressed “profound shock and grief” over the tragic school incident in a statement on X. “This heart-wrenching tragedy has plunged the entire nation into shock,” he said, extending his condolences to the families of the children killed. He directed relevant authorities to provide top-notch medical facilities to the injured and extend assistance to the affected families. “In this hour of sorrow, the entire nation shares equally in the grief of the affected families,” he said. President Zardari emphasised the need for a comprehensive investigation to determine the cause of the incident and to ensure that all educational institutions’ buildings were following safety standards. PM Shehbaz expressed “deep grief and sorrow” over the incident, in a statement shared by his office. He extended his condolences to the bereaved families and prayed for the speedy recovery of the injured, directing that “all possible medical assistance” be provided. PM Shehbaz has also issued instructions to expedite relief operations, the statement said. In a post on X, he said: “My heart is with the families grieving the loss of their children and a teacher in the tragic roof collapse at a school in Peshawar. No parent should have to endure such pain. I extend my deepest condolences and pray for strength for every family affected.” He said that he had directed that the injured receive the best possible care. “We will ensure a thorough investigation into this tragedy and take every necessary step to protect the safety of children in schools across the country,” he said. PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari also expressed grief over the incident. In a post on X, he said he was “deeply saddened” by the tragedy, adding that the thought of parents sending their children to school in the morning only to receive news of their deaths was heartbreaking. He expressed solidarity with the bereaved families and prayed for the speedy recovery of the injured. Bilawal’s sister, MNA Aseefa Bhutto-Zardari, also extended condolences to the bereaved families and prayed for the swift recovery of the injured. She said schools must be places of learning and protection, adding that those responsible for ensuring children’s safety must be held accountable. Unicef also expressed its deep sadness over the incident. Unicef representative in Pakistan, Pernille Ironside, said in a statement: “Unicef extends its deepest condolences to the bereaved families and communities affected by this devastating incident.” “Our thoughts are also with the injured children; we wish them a swift and full recovery. Unicef stands ready to support the government’s response by providing psycho-social support to affected children, families and communities,” she said. Unicef called for urgent action to ensure that all schools, public and private, meet building safety standards and undergo regular safety inspections. “These standards must be strictly enforced to prevent such tragedies in future,” Ironside said. “Every child has the right to learn in a safe environment, where children can learn, grow and thrive, protected from harm. Going to school should never put a child’s life at risk,” she said. People stand near rubble after a school roof collapse in Peshawar, October 15, 2026. —Reuters The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) said it was “appalled” by the deaths. “It is important to stress that this was not an accident but a preventable failure, given that police have reportedly attributed the collapse to a weak structure carrying excessive construction,” it said, noting that a similar incident this year had killed 14 children at a tuition centre in Lahore. The commission called for an “independent, time-bound” inquiry with the findings to be made public. It also stressed the need for accountability of the school owner and the regulators “who allowed unsafe buildings to operate”, compensation for the families affected, and mandatory structural audits of all public and private schools. Roof collapse incidents Building and roof collapses are common in Pakistan, often attributed to poor safety standards and the use of substandard construction materials. In July, three girls, aged 3 to 13, were killed after a portion of the outer wall of a government primary school near Umerkot collapsed and the rubble fell on them. The same month, a child died, and at least five other people were injured after the roof of an under-construction private school building collapsed in Lahore’s Baghbanpura neighbourhood . On June 30, 14 children lost their lives when the roof of a private tuition centre collapsed in Lahore’s Kahna area. The incident had come less than two months after four children were killed and 20 people injured after the roof of a classroom at a private school in Dera Ghazi Khan collapsed. A probe into the DG Khan incident revealed that construction for an extension of the tuition centre’s building was under way when the roof of the classroom collapsed. Last week, two men died in Pakpattan after the roof of their house collapsed during heavy rain and a windstorm. In June, a labourer was killed, and three others were injured when the roof of an under-construction building collapsed in Khawaspur locality of Lalamusa , Gujrat. The same month, two people were injured after the roof of a house collapsed in Lahore’s Nishtar area. In August, a couple was killed, and their daughters were injured after the roof of their house in Shahzad Town , Islamabad, collapsed following three days of heavy rainfall. Additional input from AFP

items.title: Rush for fuel from accident tankers is stealing, punishable by law – NPA boss, Edudzi Tamakloe
items.description: National Petroleum Authority (NPA) Chief Executive Officer Edudzi Tamakloe has described the practice of rushing to collect fuel from accident tankers as stealing, warning that those involved are committing an offence. Appearing before the Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee (PAC) on Thursday, October 15, he said the practice should not be treated as an innocent rush to take advantage of an accident, but as the theft of petroleum products. “What you describe as a rush for fuel is stealing, for want of a better word, and you know in this country stealing is an offence,” he said. “A person who diverts petroleum products commits an offence and is liable on summary conviction to a fine not less than 2,500 penalty units and not more than 5,000 penalty units, or to a term of imprisonment not less than two years or five years or both,” he added. Mr Tamakloe said the NPA had launched a public education campaign dubbed “Stay Back, Stay Safe” to discourage people from approaching tankers involved in accidents to siphon fuel. He warned that the consequences of such actions could be devastating, particularly when people gather around tankers carrying highly flammable petroleum products. His comments followed concerns about the need for systems to alert emergency services when fuel tankers are involved in accidents, allowing the Police, Fire Service and ambulance teams to respond promptly and prevent people from gathering at accident scenes to collect fuel. Mr Tamakloe, however, explained that the sensors fitted to the vehicles are activated when the tanker begins moving and stop when it comes to a halt. He said the system enables the Authority to measure the freight payable, explaining how the sensors operate in tracking the movement of the vehicles.

items.title: Reps advance bill to establish renewable energy authority
items.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has passed the Electricity Act (Amendment) Bill, 2025, for second reading, setting the stage for further legislative consideration of a proposed National Authority for Renewable Energy (NARE). The bill, sponsored by Afam Victor Ogene, member representing Ogbaru Federal Constituency, Anambra State, and Chairman of the House Committee on Renewable Energy, seeks to consolidate renewable energy regulatory functions currently spread across different government agencies under a dedicated authority. Leading the debate, Ogene said the proposed legislation would address structural gaps in the power sector by transferring relevant renewable energy functions from the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC), the Rural Electrification Agency (REA) and the Rural Electrification Fund (REF) to the proposed authority. “This specialisation will improve coordination, reduce institutional overlaps and provide focused direction for the effective development of the renewable energy sector,” he said. The lawmaker argued that Nigeria needed to look beyond expanding the national electricity grid to tackle persistent electricity access challenges, particularly in rural and underserved communities. “We must embrace innovative, decentralised and renewable energy solutions that can reach communities and businesses more efficiently,” Ogene said. Under the proposed legislation, NARE would regulate and supervise renewable energy development, promote mini-grid and off-grid electricity systems, and expand access to electricity in rural, unserved and underserved communities, including island communities. The bill also seeks to encourage investment in the renewable energy sector through financial, fiscal and regulatory incentives designed to promote local manufacturing, research, innovation and capacity building. It provides for the development of renewable energy sources, including solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, biomass and hydrogen, as part of efforts to diversify Nigeria’s energy mix. Other proposed responsibilities of the authority include issuing licences, establishing standards, ensuring fair tariffs and resolving disputes in the renewable energy market to strengthen consumer protection and transparency. The proposed authority would also collaborate with NERC and the Federal Ministry of Finance to facilitate effective grid integration and harmonise renewable energy policies. A key provision proposes allocating 40 per cent of the annual funds of the Rural Electrification Fund to NARE to finance renewable energy development. The proposed funding arrangement is intended to support the authority’s operations and expand the deployment of renewable energy solutions across the country. Following deliberations, the House unanimously adopted the bill for second reading and referred it to the relevant committee for further legislative scrutiny. The committee is expected to examine the bill’s provisions, including the proposed transfer of personnel, assets and ongoing projects from existing agencies to the new authority. items.title: Afrique de l’Ouest : Des prisons sous forte pression
items.description: © Internet Au-delà du cas malien, la pression sur les établissements pénitentiaires traverse plusieurs pays de la sous-région. Du Sénégal au Niger en passant par le Burkina Faso et la Guinée, surpopulation et poids des personnes en attente de jugement sont au cœur des difficultés carcérales. Au Sénégal, la population carcérale atteignait 15 267 détenus au 18 août 2025, selon le ministère de la Justice. Parmi eux, 547 personnes étaient en détention provisoire depuis au moins trois ans. Face à la pression, l’administration pénitentiaire a également renforcé ses capacités d’accueil : 1 390 places supplémentaires ont été créées entre 2024 et 2025, tandis qu’un programme de modernisation prévoit la construction de plusieurs établissements. La pression apparaît moins forte au Burkina Faso, mais reste réelle. Les dernières statistiques nationales disponibles, arrêtées au 31 décembre 2024, font état de 8 799 détenus pour 5 403 places, soit un taux d’occupation de 162,9%. Les personnes en détention avant jugement représentaient 29% de la population carcérale, soit 2 552 détenus. Entre surpopulation et pistes de désengorgement Au Niger, des données plus récentes montrent une situation particulièrement tendue dans certains établissements. À la maison d’arrêt de Niamey, 1 895 personnes étaient détenues au 8 mars 2026, dont 1 496 prévenus et 399 condamnés. L’établissement affichait alors un taux d’occupation de 416%. À Dosso, la prison civile accueillait au 15 avril 2026 329 détenus pour 250 places, dont 149 prévenus. La question du désengorgement figure d’ailleurs parmi les préoccupations affichées par les autorités nigériennes. En avril 2026, le ministère de la Justice mettait notamment en avant la mise en œuvre des alternatives à l’incarcération comme l’un des moyens de lutter contre la surpopulation carcérale. Le recours au travail d’intérêt général et à la comparution sur reconnaissance préalable de culpabilité est également encouragé pour accélérer le traitement de certains dossiers. En Guinée, les dernières données nationales disponibles remontent à mars 2024. Elles faisaient état de 5 549 détenus, dont 55,5% en détention préventive. Le niveau d’occupation du système pénitentiaire était alors estimé à 171,4%. D’un pays à l’autre, les niveaux de surpopulation et le poids de la détention préventive varient, mais aucun des systèmes observés n’échappe totalement à la pression carcérale. Une réalité qui fait de la gestion des prisons un défi partagé à l’échelle ouest-africaine, avec des réponses encore très inégales selon les États. Mohamed Kenouvi

items.title: Minawi urges restraint as fallout from deadly Sudan-Egypt border strikes widens
items.description: Darfur’s governor says most reported victims of the North Wadi bombing came from Darfur, as rights groups demand accountability, cross border trade stalls and concerns grow over people fleeing the strikes. Darfur governor Minni Minnawi has urged Sudanese and Egyptian authorities to establish the facts surrounding deadly strikes on artisanal gold miners near the Egyptian border, warning against collective blame as tensions rise between the two countries. Dozens of Sudanese miners were reportedly killed in airstrikes in North Wadi on Saturday. Minawi said most of the reported victims came from Darfur and called for an end to the demonisation of the joint forces, stressing that individual incidents must not fuel accusations against entire communities. In a statement following a meeting with Egypt’s ambassador and consul in Port Sudan on Wednesday, Minawi said the Egyptian diplomats had expressed regret over the casualties and pledged that an ongoing investigation, conducted in cooperation with the Sudanese government, would establish the facts. He urged both governments to coordinate their investigations, publish their findings transparently and hold those responsible to account. He also called on citizens and the media in both countries to avoid unverified reports and inflammatory rhetoric. Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) Commander and Transitional Sovereignty Council President Lt Gen Abdelfattah El Burhan has ordered a fact-finding committee to investigate the miners’ deaths, while the National Human Rights Commission has announced plans to establish its own inquiry. This follows a similar probe by El Burhan conducted in the wake of a similar reported attack by Egyptian forces earlier this year on June 17 and 18. The Sudanese Observatory for Human Rights has meanwhile called for urgent verification of reports that people fleeing the strikes were detained after reaching Port Sudan, while others were taken into Egyptian territory. The organisation demanded disclosure of their whereabouts and guarantees for their safety and legal rights. ‘Border trade disrupted as calls for accountability grow’ The fallout has spread to cross border transport. The Egyptian Truck Drivers’ Union announced a suspension of truck movements into and out of Sudan until further notice, citing the killing of two Egyptian drivers in Khartoum and concerns over the safety of its members. Meanwhile, the Ashkeet and Argeen border crossings in Northern State remained closed for a third day amid protests against restrictions on personal imports and the import of fruit and vegetables. Residents of Wadi Halfa warned that the restrictions were driving up the cost of basic goods, squeezing traders and worsening an already difficult economic situation. One resident told Radio Dabanga that protesters could escalate their action if the authorities failed to respond. Condemnations of the miners’ deaths have continued across Sudan, with political groups, Resistance Committees, the Sudanese Journalists’ Syndicate and other organisations calling for an investigation and accountability. Activists have also launched a social media campaign under the hashtag #Haq_Al_Dahaba (right of the gold miners), demanding justice for the victims. The Justice and Equality Movement condemned the deaths of Sudanese miners while also expressing regret over the killing of two Egyptian nationals in Khartoum and the injury of a third. It urged the public to reject disinformation, inflammatory campaigns and unverified casualty figures. items.title: Cambodian Supreme Court Maximizes Sentence for Opposition Activist
items.description: Click to expand Image Cambodia’s Supreme Court, Phnom Penh, June 25, 2026. © 2026 Sopheng Cheang/AP Photo Cambodia’s Supreme Court on October 14 denied opposition activist Voeung Samnang’s request to serve his two sentences concurrently, meaning he will spend 11 years in prison. Samnang had been convicted on charges of “plotting an attack on the state” and received sentences of five and six years. The case illustrates the Cambodian government’s increased use of vague plotting charges to prosecute opposition activists and social media users and sentence them to long prison terms. Samnang had been a local commune official for the Cambodia National Rescue Party (CNRP), the opposition party dissolved by the government-controlled Supreme Court in 2017. He fled to Thailand in 2020 after charges were filed against him. In 2021, Thai police arrested him and forcibly returned him to Cambodia, alongside opposition activist Veourn Veasna, despite both being recognized as refugees by the United Nations refugee agency. Samnang was charged with plotting, convicted and sentenced to five years in prison in 2022 as part of a mass trial of 36 former CNRP leaders and supporters. While incarcerated, he was tried and convicted again in 2023 on additional plotting charges and sentenced to six years in prison. The ostensible evidence against him in both cases was Facebook posts related to the CNRP and his criticism of the government. Samnang’s wife, Teang Chenda, joined the “Friday Women,” a group of Cambodian women who held regular protests in the capital, Phnom Penh, to call for the release of their imprisoned husbands and sons. The Friday Women have faced harassment from Cambodian authorities during their public protests. Samnang’s case highlights the government’s unrelenting persecution of the political opposition ahead of next year’s local elections. Veasna, the man arrested alongside Samnang, was charged and convicted in a separate case. He later apologized to then-Prime Minister Hun Sen, joined the ruling Cambodian People’s Party, and was released from prison – part of the government’s systematic use of coerced confessions to discredit political opposition members and activists. Veasna later fled Cambodia and disavowed his defection to the ruling party.

items.title: Dr Ahmadou Touré : « Aucun développement durable n’est possible sans souveraineté effective »
items.description: © Internet Dans son nouvel ouvrage, « Souveraineté et refondation étatique au Mali (2020-2026) : vers l’Alliance des États du Sahel », l’enseignant-chercheur Dr Ahmadou Touré analyse la trajectoire ouverte en 2020. Maître-assistant et Directeur du Centre de recherche en gouvernance, médiation et sécurité au Sahel, il précise les critères d’une souveraineté effective et les conditions nécessaires à la consolidation de l’AES. Quelle idée centrale relie les années 2020 à 2026 ? Il s’agit de la reconquête d’une souveraineté effective et durable, comprise comme la capacité retrouvée de l’État à décider de son destin politique, sécuritaire, économique et diplomatique. La Charte de la Transition, les Assises nationales de la Refondation, la Constitution de 2023, le Cadre stratégique de refondation de l’État et la Vision Mali Kura 2063 ont donné à cette orientation un ancrage institutionnel. La montée en puissance des FAMa, la reprise de Kidal et l’émergence de l’AES l’ont prolongée sur les plans territorial et régional. Cette refondation ne sera durable qu’avec une présence civile effective de l’État et des résultats perceptibles pour les populations. Comment reconnaître une souveraineté effective ? Elle suppose un contrôle territorial durable, la maîtrise des décisions d’emploi de la force et la capacité de choisir ses partenariats ou de mettre fin aux dispositifs jugés inefficaces. Elle passe aussi par un meilleur contrôle des ressources stratégiques, la transformation locale et la mobilisation fiscale. Elle se vérifie surtout dans le retour des écoles, des services de santé, de l’état-civil et de l’eau. Aucun développement durable n’est possible sans souveraineté effective. Celle-ci se vérifie lorsque l’État assume pleinement sa responsabilité et produit des résultats concrets. Quelle fragilité menace le plus la reconstruction de l’État ? Le principal risque réside dans le décalage entre la reconquête militaire et l’ancrage civil. Sans services publics ni confiance des populations, le contrôle territorial est fragile. Il faut déployer et former des personnels locaux, investir dans les services essentiels, organiser le dialogue intercommunautaire, renforcer la justice transitionnelle et associer renseignement, présence civile et développement local. Que doit encore accomplir la Confédération AES ? Elle doit consolider ses institutions communes et leur donner leurs propres moyens. La Force unifiée doit s’appuyer sur un renseignement partagé, des protocoles harmonisés et une doctrine commune. Des corridors routiers et énergétiques, des réseaux électriques interconnectés, des initiatives agricoles et une banque finançant les projets productifs doivent rendre l’intégration visible dans le quotidien. La souveraineté collective sera crédible lorsqu’elle produira des bénéfices concrets et partagés en matière de sécurité, d’énergie, d’alimentation, d’échanges et d’emplois.

items.title: GhIG pushes for legislation to regulate geoscientists’ activities
items.description: The Ghana Institute of Geoscientists (GhIG) is pushing for a legal framework to regulate the practice of geoscience in Ghana, saying the move is critical to enforcing professional standards, ethical conduct and accountability. The Institute says it has prepared a draft bill for consideration and eventual passage by Parliament to provide a clear regulatory framework for geoscientists and complement existing legislation governing the sector. President of GhIG, Crisler Akwei Ankrah, says the proposed legislation is long overdue and will ensure professionals operate within acceptable standards and ethical boundaries. “Geoscientists in the country need to be regulated so that we can also carry out our profession with the best practice and within the ethical frame of the law. We think it’s long overdue,” he said. He explained that the Institute intends to build on the momentum surrounding the implementation of the Geological Survey Authority’s legislative instrument to advance the proposed legislation. Mr Ankrah also called for the establishment of dedicated geoscience desks at Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies to ensure geoscientific assessments form part of the building permit approval process. He argued that geoscientists should be required to assess the suitability of land before construction permits are granted, particularly in areas vulnerable to flooding and other environmental risks. “For flooding, nobody will get a building permit without a geoscientist signing off at the district assembly where they get a permit,” he stated. According to him, such assessments would help determine whether land earmarked for infrastructure development is suitable for construction, taking into account its terrain, drainage systems and other geological conditions. He believes integrating geoscientific expertise into local planning processes could help minimise or better manage some of the country’s recurring development challenges. Meanwhile, Deputy Director-General of the Ghana Geological Survey Authority (GGSA), Maria Yusuf, disclosed that the Authority has begun engagements with the Ministry of Works and Housing and various assemblies to strengthen its advisory role. “We are in touch with the Ministry of Works and Housing. I think we’ve been there on a number of occasions talking about these collaborations and how to go about it,” she said. She added that the Authority had also engaged several assemblies, although responses to the proposed collaboration has been mixed. The engagements form part of broader efforts to strengthen the application of geoscientific expertise in land-use planning, infrastructure development and national safety.

items.title: Terminaux portuaires : le géant danois Maersk arrive en Algérie
items.description: En attendant le français CMA CGM, le géant danois AP Moller Maersk arrive en Algérie par le biais de l’acquisition de 100 % d’une entreprise basée à Singapour, Portek International, déjà présente dans le secteur portuaire algérien. L'acquisition s’est faite auprès du Japonais Mitsui & Co. Portek est un opérateur de terminaux feeders (accueillant des porte-conteneurs de petit tonnage) possédant des participations dans sept terminaux portuaires en Algérie ( Bejaia ), au Gabon, en Indonésie, en Lettonie, à Malte et au Vietnam, ainsi que des activités d'ingénierie portuaire, a rapporté le site Globe Newswire. Le Danois AP Moller rachète un gestionnaire de terminaux présent en Algérie Employant environ 1 400 personnes, les terminaux portuaires multi-activités de Portek traitent chaque année environ sept millions de tonnes de marchandises en vrac, 700 000 conteneurs et environ 90 000 véhicules, a ajouté la même source. La réalisation de la transaction est soumise à la satisfaction des conditions de clôture habituelles, notamment l'obtention des approbations réglementaires et autres approbations de tiers, indique-t-on. Cette acquisition s'inscrit dans la stratégie d'AP Moller Capital axée sur les infrastructures de transport et de logistique et renforce son expertise dans le secteur portuaire. Selon Globe Newswire, AP Moller Capital entend, une fois l'acquisition finalisée, collaborer étroitement avec les équipes opérationnelles locales de Portek, y compris donc en Algérie, afin de consolider les compétences existantes de l'entreprise et d'accompagner sa prochaine phase de développement. L’opérateur compte mettre l'accent sur la performance opérationnelle, la gouvernance, la sécurité, la rigueur dans la gestion des capitaux et la performance environnementale, notamment la planification de la réduction des émissions. AP Moller entend apporter son expertise aux équipes locales “Portek correspond parfaitement à notre stratégie d'investissement et à notre philosophie d'actionnaire actif. C'est une entreprise établie, dotée d'un portefeuille diversifié d'opérations portuaires desservant d'importants flux commerciaux sur trois continents, et soutenue par des équipes opérationnelles locales expérimentées”, s'est félicité Semih Gökmen, associé chez AP Moller Maersk. Le groupe danois va ainsi apporter son expertise pour développer les compétences existantes de Portek et accompagner sa prochaine phase de développement, a-t-il ajouté. L’article Terminaux portuaires : le géant danois Maersk arrive en Algérie est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Kidal : Après l’armée, réinstaller l’État
items.description: © Internet Les FAMa ont repris Kidal le 6 octobre, près de six mois après leur retrait. La sécurisation de la ville ouvre un autre chantier : rétablir l’administration, ramener les services publics et renouer avec des populations dispersées, alors que les groupes armés restent actifs. L’armée malienne a consolidé sa présence après des opérations aériennes et terrestres menées dans le cadre de l’opération Dougoukoloko. Le Front de libération de l’Azawad (FLA), qui tenait Kidal avec le JNIM depuis les attaques du 25 avril, affirme avoir effectué un « repli stratégique et maîtrisé » afin de préserver ses hommes et ses moyens. Le gouvernement annonce « le retour progressif de l’administration et des services sociaux de base ». L’État-major entend aussi sécuriser les populations, les frontières et la circulation des personnes et des biens. La ville a toutefois changé de contrôle sans bataille terrestre décisive. Le FLA présente son retrait comme temporaire et les groupes armés conservent une capacité d’action dans la région. Le retour des FAMa constitue donc un succès, sans marquer la fin des menaces. L’expérience récente incite à la prudence. Après la reprise de novembre 2023, le gouvernorat, la police, la gendarmerie, le Trésor, l’hôpital et l’Académie d’enseignement avaient repris leurs activités. Les axes restaient cependant dangereux. Les attaques d’avril 2026 ont ensuite provoqué le départ de l’armée, de l’administration et d’une partie des habitants. Sécurité Tenir Kidal suppose de protéger la ville et ses accès. La route de Gao, les liaisons avec Anéfis, Tessalit et Aguelhoc ainsi que les circuits d’approvisionnement sont essentiels aux services publics et au retour des familles. Une présence limitée au chef-lieu laisserait les agents, les commerçants et les transporteurs exposés dès leur sortie de la localité. Réfugié à Gao depuis juillet, l’enseignant Almoustapha Maïga souhaite rentrer, mais évoque l’insécurité et le mauvais état de la route. « Beaucoup de mes collègues veulent aussi retourner, mais nous ne savons pas comment, avec le manque de ressources », a-t-il confié à la Deutsche Welle. Il demande un appui au transport pour ceux qui ont tout laissé derrière eux. Le renseignement de proximité et le traitement des alertes comptent autant que les patrouilles. Une population qui craint des représailles ou ne dispose d’aucun interlocuteur fiable transmet difficilement les informations nécessaires pour empêcher la reconstitution des réseaux armés. Services Le retour des services part d’une situation dégradée. Après le 25 avril, l’alimentation scolaire avait été suspendue dans 16 écoles de la région, touchant 2 913 élèves, dont au moins la moitié de filles. Fin juin, l’UNICEF signalait encore des établissements endommagés ou occupés et un accès très réduit aux cours. La Direction régionale de la Santé avait aussi été prise pour cible. Trois cliniques mobiles assuraient une partie des soins. En août, le CICR a transféré six blessés du Centre de santé de référence de Kidal vers l’hôpital de Gao. Le réseau urbain d’eau, qui desservait environ 1 004 ménages, avait également été affecté. Le retour des déplacés réclame une organisation concrète. Certaines familles ont perdu leur logement, leurs revenus ou leurs moyens de transport. Sidi Mohamed Ag Almoctar, Président du Conseil régional de Kidal, espère que « cette fois-ci, c’est la bonne ». Cet espoir reste lié à la possibilité de rentrer sans s’exposer à un nouvel abandon. Confiance La gouvernance locale forme le troisième volet. Élus, autorités traditionnelles, organisations de femmes et de jeunes, éleveurs, commerçants et déplacés doivent être associés aux décisions sur la reconstruction et les services. Dans un climat où la parole publique demeure prudente, des consultations régulières peuvent faire remonter les besoins sans confondre critique, désaccord politique et soutien aux groupes armés. L’universitaire Pierre Claver Bakoroba Traoré plaide pour une décentralisation plus poussée et pour le dialogue. « Il ne faut surtout pas fermer la porte », estime également un habitant interrogé par Studio Tamani. La concertation n’exclut ni l’autorité de l’État ni la lutte contre les violences. Elle peut réduire les frustrations dont les groupes armés tirent parti. Une administration présente, des routes praticables, des services ouverts et des habitants revenus durablement donneront un contenu concret à la reprise de Kidal. Sans ces relais civils, la ville risque de rester une position militaire disputée et de connaître encore les changements de contrôle qui ont rythmé son histoire récente. Massiré Diop

items.title: Martinez’s comments reflect ‘circus’ at Man Utd — Roy Keane
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former Manchester United captain Roy Keane says Lisandro Martinez’s public criticism of the club’s hierarchy reflects the “chaos” surrounding the Premier League side. According to the BBC, Keane described United as being “like a bit of a circus” following Martinez’s comments about the club’s failure to strengthen its squad during the summer transfer window. Martinez spoke out after United’s 2-0 defeat by Atletico Madrid in the Champions League on Tuesday, criticising the club’s recruitment and demanding more from its leadership. The Argentine defender said he expected more from director of football Jason Wilcox and the club’s hierarchy following United’s qualification for the Champions League. Speaking on The Overlap’s Stick to Football podcast, Keane questioned the timing of Martinez’s remarks, particularly given the defender’s own performances and United’s difficult run. “There will be some fans saying it’s great and some saying you’re letting the team down, especially from a player who hasn’t been at his best, when the team is struggling,” Keane said. He added that the club appeared divided and criticised the atmosphere surrounding United. “They’re obviously not together. It is chaotic there from the top to the bottom. We go there on match days and I don’t like the feeling around the club,” Keane said. He continued: “I think as a reflection of the club, it’s obviously chaos there, like a bit of a circus.” Keane also questioned players who publicly criticise their clubs during difficult periods, arguing that they should first examine their own performances. “When you’re going through a difficult spell like United are, the issue I have with certain players saying things is you always have to start with the man in the mirror before you start coming out with all these comments,” he said. Martinez later said on social media on Wednesday that he had spoken out of “anger and frustration”. The 28-year-old’s contract expires at the end of the season, although United have the option to extend it by another year. Keane also cast doubt on Martinez’s standing within the squad, saying he did not regard the defender as a senior figure at Manchester United. “I don’t think it will be a big falling-out – because I think we have question marks over this dressing room anyway,” he said. “I don’t think there’s enough characters – enough men in there – but I don’t see him as a senior player at Manchester United. I see him as a centre-half who’s making lots of mistakes.” Former United defender Gary Neville also criticised Martinez’s remarks, arguing that they could be interpreted as an attack on his teammates. Neville said senior players, including Harry Maguire and Bruno Fernandes, would have reason to be angry because Martinez’s comments suggested the squad needed more players. United will travel to Leeds United in the Premier League on Sunday. The post Martinez’s comments reflect ‘circus’ at Man Utd — Roy Keane appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Mfantsipim @150: Ace Anan Ankomah leads project to preserve school’s musical heritage
items.description: A text message about a school song competition has grown into a 14-track musical anthology documenting the history, traditions and musical heritage of Mfantsipim School as the institution marks its 150th anniversary. The Mfantsipim Old Boys Association (MOBA) has launched the Mfantsipim Sesquicentennial Anthology, a collection of historic school anthems, hymns, highlife songs and other compositions that have shaped the identity of the Cape Coast-based school across generations. The project was recorded and produced by lawyer Ace Anan Ankomah, an old boy from the 1984 year group, in collaboration with sound engineer Herbert Ebenezer Crassie. What began as an entry in a competition to compose a jama song for the anniversary eventually developed into a wider effort to recover, record and preserve songs associated with the school’s history. Ankomah said the project took shape after Alfred Prince Gyan, an old boy from the 2013 year group, contacted him about the competition. The two developed a composition into a medley and brought together fellow old boys from Joyful Way Inc. to record a demonstration. Their entry won the competition, but the idea soon grew beyond the original assignment. The anniversary planning committee later submitted a winning choral composition by Flora Adokoh, which became the foundation for the official Sesquicentennial Anthem. Ankomah subsequently engaged Crassie to orchestrate the piece. The project took another turn after Dr Ernest Addison, an old boy from the 1979 year group, suggested recreating the Mfantsipim Ode, which had been adopted as the school’s Centenary Anthem in 1976. That suggestion prompted the team to look beyond the anniversary’s new compositions and recover older songs that had become difficult to find or reproduce. One of these was the Mfantsipim Mfeha Ndwom. Kakra Essamuah, popularly known as Brazos, had preserved handwritten historical texts, while fellow old boy Timothy Andoh helped reconstruct the song from memory. The anthology also features Dwin Hwɛ Kan, the Sesquicentennial Anthem, Jama, and two historic highlife songs released in 1976 by Kwadwo Donkor, an old boy from the 1955 year group. Another contribution came from Emmanuel Dadson, known as Aezor, who sent Ankomah the lyrics to Ahotsewfo , the Fante version of the hymn For All the Saints. To capture the music as it is performed within the school, the recording team made two visits to the campus to record live performances by the choir and regimental band. Old boy Jonas Anterkyi handled the videography, while Professor Alfred Patrick Addaquay of the University of Ghana contributed an organ rendition of For All the Saints. Beyond celebrating the anniversary, the anthology documents the origins and evolution of songs that have become part of Mfantsipim’s institutional identity. The hymn For All the Saints became the school’s official hymn in 1910 in honour of Reverend Alfred Thomas Robert Bartrop, whose contribution helped save the institution from collapse in the early twentieth century. Dwin Hwɛ Kan , composed around 1910 by Reverend Gaddiel Robert Acquaah and Charles Emmanuel Graves, was adopted as the school’s official anthem in 1963. The Mfantsipim Centenary Highlife and Kwabotwe Highlife, composed by the late Kwadwo Donkor, were adopted for the school’s centenary celebrations in 1976. Bringing these works together gives old boys, current students and future generations an opportunity to engage with the music that has accompanied the school through different periods of its history. The project also relied on contributions from several other alumni, including Anselm Ransford Sowah, Poku Donkoh and Dr Nana Dadzie Ghansah. Albert Ocran produced the accompanying booklet without charge, while George Pabi designed the booklet and vinyl sleeves. Ankomah served as executive producer, with production and arrangement shared with Crassie. The anthology is dedicated to the MOBA 1984 year group and to the memory of the MOBA 1957 year group, which included Ankomah’s late father. As part of the preservation effort, Ankomah presented 1,000 pen drives containing the music, alongside booklets documenting the lyrics and history of the songs. A further 100 limited-edition red vinyl records have been produced for sale to old boys, with the proceeds intended to support the school. Several accompanying music videos have also been released on MOBA’s YouTube channels, extending access to the collection beyond the physical recordings. The combination of audio recordings, historical notes, video and vinyl reflects an effort to preserve not only the songs themselves but also the stories and traditions behind them. From a single competition entry to a 14-track anthology, the Mfantsipim Sesquicentennial project has become a collaborative effort to safeguard the school’s musical heritage. As Mfantsipim marks 150 years, the collection offers a lasting record of the songs that have helped define its identity and connect generations of old boys to their shared history.

items.title: Four feared dead, many injured as fuel tanker explodes in Edo
items.description: By Ozioruva Aliu, Beni City Tragedy struck in Oluku, Ovia Noth East local government area around the Benin-Lagos Highway on Thursday as a tanker laden with petrol exploded in the afternoon, consuming four people, including military personnel, while several persons suffered various degrees of injuries and burns. Several vehicles were burnt in the fire incident, while a market in the area belonging to a popular businessman, Chief Osamede Adun, popularly called Bob Izua, also got burnt. The tanker was said to have fallen on the road, and people were scooping fuel. Witnesses said the tanker fell at about 7:30am, and residents rushed to scoop fuel into their houses. The witness, who owns a shop opposite the scene of the incident, said efforts by security agencies to stop residents from scooping fuel failed. “It was as they were scooping fuel that the fire started. It spread to the Bob Izua market along the road. “Many cars were affected in the incident because the fire spread quickly. We have counted four persons that died. One soldier is among the dead.” Ten burnt persons were reportedly rushed to the University of Benin Teaching Hospital after suffering severe burns. A victim who did not want his name mentioned said, “I was also among those who were scooping the fuel. I escaped with whiskers. It was a soldier who called me and drew my attention to the fact that it was sunny and way the people rushed to scoop the fuel might ignite fire. “As I looked back after he spoke to me, the tanker busted into flames as people around the area ran for dear lives. I thank the soldier; if not, I would have been burnt by now. “Two men from the northern part who were directly under the tanker were burnt, while stores that were built on the drainage were burnt. The store was also burnt down, as we are yet to know the number of people that died. However, 10 people were rushed to the emergency unit of the UBTH. The UBTH, the management swiftly mobilised emergency services, treating those that were brought to the hospital. The Chief Medical Director of UBTH, Prof. Idia Ize-Iyamu, took charge of the emergency effort, leading the response team across the accident, emergency, and burns units to stabilise severe casualties and minimise fatalities. The post Four feared dead, many injured as fuel tanker explodes in Edo appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Gov’t launches rCOMSDEP in Ahanta West, Mpohor Fiase to promote responsible community mining
items.description: The government has launched the Responsible Cooperative Mining and Skills Development Programme (rCOMSDEP) in the Ahanta West and Mpohor Fiase areas of the Western Region, as part of efforts to formalise small-scale mining, protect the environment and ensure that mining communities benefit directly from the country’s mineral resources. Addressing stakeholders at the launch, the Deputy Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Hon. Yusif Sulemana, emphasised that responsible mining must go beyond mineral extraction to create jobs, support local assemblies and traditional authorities, and improve the livelihoods of residents. The Deputy Minister explained that the programme was designed to provide small-scale miners with a legitimate and organised pathway to operate responsibly. He noted that the government was working with relevant institutions, including the Minerals Commission and the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), to register and certify mining groups and cooperatives. Hon. Sulemana asserted that the formalisation process would provide miners with the necessary regulatory backing to operate within the law while ensuring that the initiative remains sustainable beyond changes in government. He urged mining cooperatives to employ people from their host communities, respect traditional authorities and landowners, and ensure that the benefits of mining are shared with residents. Deputy Minister also stressed the importance of adopting modern mineral-processing technologies to reduce reliance on harmful chemicals such as mercury and cyanide. “Such technologies could improve gold recovery while limiting environmental damage, particularly to rivers, farmlands and other natural resources”. He assured stakeholders that the relevant agencies would continue to monitor mining activities and support cooperatives in meeting the programme’s requirements. The Acting National Coordinator of rCOMSDEP, Mr Sheihu Sidiqq, in his address, acknowledged the devastating impact of illegal and irresponsible mining on Ghana’s water bodies, forests and farmlands, while recognising that small-scale mining remained an important source of livelihood for many families. The National Coordinator called on participating cooperatives to meet the requirements for accessing concessions, comply with all regulatory obligations and uphold the highest standards of safety, transparency and environmental stewardship. The Ahanta West and Mpohor Fiase launch marks another step in the government’s drive to formalise small-scale mining and promote environmentally responsible operations, with Nzema East in the Western Region expected to be the next area to benefit from the programme.

items.title: ¿Sobran kilos o falta testosterona? Uno de cada cuatro soldados estadounidenses puede tener niveles bajos de esta hormona
items.description: Las palabras son importantes. A veces describen una realidad. Otras, pretenden modificarla. Cuando Pete Hegseth se convirtió en secretario del Departamento de Defensa de Estados Unidos, empezó a llamarlo Departamento de Guerra. El pasado verano, le añadió una coletilla nueva: Departamento de Guerra de alta testosterona. Lo hizo al anunciar una nueva política que exige que todos los miembros de las fuerzas armadas mayores de 30 años analicen sus niveles de esta hormona. El objetivo, dijo, era preparar mejor a los miembros del servicio para un campo de batalla moderno “brutal e implacable”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: AI is forcing professionals to rethink how they deliver value – Hubtel CEO
items.description: The Chief Executive Officer of Hubtel, Alex Bram, has urged lawyers, doctors and accountants to rethink how they deliver their services as artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly makes specialised knowledge accessible to the public. He believes the growing adoption of AI will challenge professionals whose services have traditionally depended on their possession of specialised information, forcing them to focus more on the value and outcomes they deliver to clients. Mr. Bram argues that with AI systems now capable of providing information, preparing documents and performing tasks previously undertaken by trained professionals, simply possessing knowledge may no longer be enough to remain competitive. “Everything that you went to school to cram, chew, pour, pass, whatever you kept in your head, it’s what you are hoping to monetise over your lifetime, right? Well, guess what? Now that knowledge is in a computer,” he said. Speaking in an interview ahead of the second episode of the Digital Economy Forum, Mr. Bram explained that professionals must begin to see artificial intelligence as a reason to rethink their business models rather than simply a threat to their livelihoods. He believes the technology will push professionals to become more innovative in how they use their expertise to solve problems. The changing nature of work and the implications of AI for Ghana’s economy will form part of discussions at the second episode of the Digital Economy Forum , under the theme “AI and the Ghana Economy: Opportunity or Disruption?” The forum, held in partnership with Hubtel , will feature the Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Sam George; Economist and Technical Advisor at the Finance Ministry, Dr. Theo Acheampong; Founder of AI for Ghana, Adam Watkins; Head of Engineering at Hubtel, Augustine Adjei; and Vice President of IMANI Africa, Bright Simons. It will air live on JoyNews and Joy 99.7 FM on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, at 8 p.m. Lawyers must rethink how they deliver value Using the legal profession as an example, Mr. Bram explained that clients can increasingly use AI tools to prepare basic agreements and access legal information without necessarily relying on a lawyer for every stage of the process. He argued that this development does not automatically eliminate the need for lawyers, but changes the services clients may expect them to provide. “So a lot of people are going to find these answers. If you are an accountant, a lawyer, people can draft their own agreements. So you have to change your strategy,” he said. He suggested that lawyers could increasingly focus on reviewing documents prepared by clients, ensuring agreements meet the required standards and providing professional representation where necessary. “Let me review it for you, make sure that it fits,” he said, illustrating how lawyers could reposition their services. “We have to change our approach.” According to Hubtel CEO, the same principle applies to accountants and other professionals whose work involves processing information and applying specialised knowledge. He believes such professionals will need to demonstrate the additional value their expertise brings when clients can independently access information and generate preliminary work using AI. Doctors must focus on better patient outcomes Turning to healthcare, Mr. Bram argued that doctors must also reconsider how they deliver value as patients gain greater access to health-related information through artificial intelligence. He explained that patients can now search for possible explanations for symptoms and obtain information about medical conditions before consulting a healthcare professional. Rather than relying primarily on their exclusive access to medical knowledge, he believes doctors should increasingly focus on helping patients achieve better health outcomes. “So if you’re a doctor or an accountant and you know that people already can find this value, you need to change your strategy to say, how can I rather profit from what they know?” he explained. He continued: “How do I position such that I can provide them a service that can help them have a better life?” The Hubtel CEO maintained that the ultimate purpose of healthcare should remain the improvement of patients’ well-being, regardless of how widely medical information becomes available. “What will make people’s lives better? What will be the goal? If one wants to live longer, what is the goal of medicine? It’s to have a longer, more fulfilling, healthier life,” he said. His argument centres on how medical professionals could adapt their services to the growing availability of digital information, rather than suggesting that AI-generated information can replace professional diagnosis or treatment. AI already changing how Hubtel operates Mr. Bram’s observations come as Hubtel itself undergoes significant changes in response to artificial intelligence. He disclosed that the company began experimenting with AI in 2022 and established an AI laboratory in 2023. Since then, the technology has influenced how the company performs tasks, manages its operations and prepares employees for changing workplace demands. “We’re restructuring quite a number of things because we can do certain things faster, better, when we are augmented with AI,” he revealed. Mr. Bram also disclosed that Hubtel has not recruited new employees for nearly a year as it reviews its operations and introduces new ways of working. He explained that employees must also adapt their responsibilities to remain productive in an increasingly AI-assisted workplace. “People need to change their roles, what they do on a day-to-day basis. We need to help people transition into this new era,” he said. Despite acknowledging the disruption, he remains optimistic that artificial intelligence will ultimately create more opportunities than it eliminates. Mr. Bram believes human creativity, changing consumer needs and the desire of businesses to expand will continue to generate demand for new products, services and professional expertise. He consequently urged workers and professionals to embrace the changing technological environment and reconsider how they can use AI to improve their productivity and the value they provide. “Disruption now? Forever an opportunity, a big opportunity for us,” he said. “There’s something for us to do as a society. We need to wake up. But if we get it right, with the steps that we are taking already, I think the future will be massively bright.” For him, the challenge is not simply about protecting existing jobs, but preparing people to work differently in an economy where information is becoming increasingly accessible.

items.title: Dalla Ngabou : 7,5 millions de FCFA de fournitures scolaires pour 13 écoles
items.description: La municipalité de Dalla Ngabou a procédé, mercredi 14 octobre 2026, à la distribution de fournitures scolaires au profit des écoles de la commune. Treize établissements élémentaires ont bénéficié de matériel scolaire d’une valeur totale de sept millions cinq cent mille francs CFA. Une initiative saluée par les parents d’élèves. Prenant la parole lors de la cérémonie, le premier adjoint au maire, Cheikh Ngom, a rappelé que l’éducation fait partie des compétences transférées aux collectivités territoriales. Il a souligné que, depuis leur arrivée à la tête de la municipalité, les autorités communales procèdent chaque année à la distribution de fournitures scolaires aux écoles élémentaires de la commune. Cette année, l’enveloppe consacrée à cette opération a été revue à la hausse, a-t-il indiqué. « L’année dernière, on était à six millions de francs CFA et, cette fois-ci, l’enveloppe est portée à sept millions cinq cent mille francs CFA », a expliqué Cheikh Ngom. Il a également précisé qu’en plus des fournitures destinées aux élèves, la municipalité a mis à la disposition des établissements des rames de papier et des cartouches d’encre pour l’impression des épreuves. Au nom des parents d’élèves, Mame Gor Wade a salué cette initiative de la municipalité de Dalla Ngabou. Selon lui, la commune vient ainsi en soutien aux familles en mettant des fournitures scolaires à la disposition de leurs enfants. « Octroyer des fournitures scolaires aux élèves de la commune est un acte de haute portée pour les parents d’élèves, qui sont souvent des populations démunies », a-t-il déclaré. La cérémonie a également été l’occasion pour Mame Gor Wade d’inviter les parents à veiller à la présence de leurs enfants dans les établissements scolaires. Il a déploré le fait que, durant cette période de récolte, de nombreux élèves se trouvent encore dans les champs au lieu de fréquenter les salles de classe. Il a ainsi appelé les familles à permettre à tous les enfants de reprendre le chemin de l’école. Birane DIOP (Correspondant)

items.title: Intersociety claims 7,500 Christians killed in Africa
items.description: A lleges Nigeria accounts for 4,300 deaths in nine months By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The International Society for Civil Liberties and Rule of Law (Intersociety) has claimed that about 7,500 Christians were killed in attacks across several African countries between January and October 10, 2026, alleging that Nigeria accounted for approximately 4,300 of the deaths. The group also claimed that thousands of Christians were abducted and more than 1,000 churches were destroyed or burnt across the affected countries during the period. In a statement, Intersociety Chairman, Emeka Umeagbalasi, said the figures were based on the organisation’s findings on attacks against Christian communities in Nigeria and other African countries. The figures and allegations could not be independently verified. Umeagbalasi claimed that the Democratic Republic of Congo recorded about 2,000 deaths, while Nigeria accounted for between 3,426 and 4,300 Christian deaths in the period under review. He attributed a further 1,100 deaths to Mozambique, South Sudan, Ethiopia, Burkina Faso and other countries. He also alleged that 3,395 Christians were abducted in Nigeria during the period covered by the group’s report. According to him, 343 Christian deaths were recorded between September 1 and October 10, 2026, including 130 in Plateau State and 64 in Adamawa State. He further claimed that 202 people were abducted, 10 churches destroyed, eight pastors abducted and two pastors killed during the period. The group also raised concerns about the reported captivity of 150 Christian schoolchildren, whom it said had been held by Boko Haram since May 2026, and alleged that Christian communities in Kebbi State had faced threats to convert to Islam or risk being killed. Nigeria, DRC figures Umeagbalasi claimed that Nigeria had recorded an estimated 19,810 churches attacked or destroyed since the Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009. He also put the cumulative number of Christian deaths at about 130,893 and the number of abducted Christians at 82,805. The figures were presented as Intersociety’s estimates and were not independently verified. The group alleged that attacks against Christians, their homes, farmlands, places of worship and livelihoods were being sustained by both state and non-state actors. It also accused successive Nigerian governments since 2015 of complicity in the attacks, an allegation that was not substantiated with independently verified evidence in the statement. On the Democratic Republic of Congo, Umeagbalasi said the country had recorded an estimated 2,000 Christian deaths between January 1 and October 10, 2026. He attributed several attacks to the Islamic State-affiliated Allied Democratic Forces and the Islamic State Central Africa Province. Among the incidents cited were an attack on a gold mine on March 11, which he said killed 17 Christians; a raid in Beni in June, in which he claimed more than 20 Christians were killed; and a reported fire outbreak on September 10 that allegedly killed 27 children associated with Our Lady of Mercy Catholic Parish in the Bukavu region. These accounts and casualty figures were not independently verified. Other African countries The group also alleged that Islamic State-linked militants carried out attacks against Christian communities in Mozambique, particularly in Cabo Delgado Province, forcing residents to flee their homes. It cited a reported attack on September 6, 2026, in which Christians were allegedly killed or abducted in Cabo Delgado, followed by an attack in neighbouring Niassa Province in which a Catholic church was reportedly burnt. In discussing Sudan and South Sudan, Umeagbalasi alleged that Christian communities had faced attacks, abductions and restrictions on religious activities. He also cited alleged attacks in Kenya, Ethiopia, Burkina Faso and Uganda, which he attributed to groups including Al-Shabaab, Jama’at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin and Islamic State-linked factions. The group estimated that attacks in countries other than Nigeria and the Democratic Republic of Congo accounted for at least 1,100 Christian deaths during the period. Allegations in Abia In Nigeria, Intersociety raised concerns about alleged criminal activity in parts of Umunneochi Local Government Area of Abia State. Umeagbalasi claimed that 28 human skulls and bones were discovered in the area on September 26, 2026, suggesting they could belong to travellers, farmers and other road users. The identities of the remains and the circumstances surrounding their discovery were not established in the statement. He also referred to alleged abduction camps and previous security operations in the area, including the reported abduction of Methodist Church Prelate Samuel Kanu-Uche and two other clerics in May 2022. The group called for further action by relevant authorities to address insecurity and investigate reported attacks and disappearances. The allegations contained in the report, including claims of official complicity and the attribution of specific attacks to particular groups, were not independently established in the statement. Intersociety’s casualty estimates and other claims require independent verification. The post Intersociety claims 7,500 Christians killed in Africa appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Super Falcons captain Rasheedat Ajibade suffers ankle fracture
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Super Falcons captain Rasheedat Ajibade is facing at least three months on the sidelines after suffering a fracture to her right ankle during Nigeria’s 5-0 victory over Comoros in the 2028 Olympic Games qualifiers on Tuesday, according to ESPN. The Paris Saint-Germain forward sustained the injury in the first half of Tuesday’s second-leg encounter at the Remo Stars Stadium in Ikenne, Ogun State, after a collision with Comoros defender Diore Miriame Kaina Said. Ajibade landed heavily on her right foot and was unable to continue, leaving the pitch on a stretcher before being replaced by Folashade Ijamilusi. According to ESPN, an MRI scan at the hospital confirmed the fracture, with the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) saying the captain would undergo surgery in Paris on Friday. “The MRI showed that she suffered a fracture on her ankle and she saw a surgeon here immediately after,” NFF head of communications Ademola Olajire told ESPN. “But because of her flight back to Paris, she couldn’t wait and I spoke to our team doctor and we understand she’ll be having surgery on Friday in Paris.” Olajire said further updates on the extent of the injury and Ajibade’s recovery would follow after surgery and an assessment by PSG’s medical team. The injury is a major setback for both Nigeria and PSG, with the forward potentially missing several UEFA Women’s Champions League matches and Nigeria’s November international fixtures. Her availability for the Super Falcons’ third-round Olympic qualifier against Morocco in March 2027 could depend on her recovery. Despite the setback, Ajibade reassured supporters that she remained positive about her recovery. “I’m fine and doing well. I’ll be back stronger, for good and for God’s greater glory,” she wrote in a message on her WhatsApp status. “Thank you so much for all your calls and messages. I’m sorry I can’t reply to everyone right now, but once I settle in, I’ll get back to each of you. “I see all your messages, your love and your kind wishes. Thank you, thank you, thank you! God bless you all.” Ajibade’s injury overshadowed Nigeria’s emphatic victory over Comoros, which secured a 7-0 aggregate win and passage into the third round of the 2028 Olympic qualifiers. Toni Payne and Uchenna Kanu each scored twice, while Christy Ucheibe converted a penalty as the Super Falcons produced a four-goal second-half surge to complete the victory. Nigeria had taken a 2-0 advantage from the first leg and will now face Morocco in a two-legged encounter scheduled for March 2027. The Super Falcons are seeking to qualify for a second consecutive Olympic Games appearance after ending a 16-year absence by reaching the Paris 2024 tournament. Ajibade captained Nigeria to a record-extending 10th Women’s Africa Cup of Nations title in 2025 and remains one of the team’s most experienced players. The 26-year-old joined PSG from Atletico Madrid in 2025 on a contract running until June 2027, making the injury a significant disruption to her first full season with the French club. The post Super Falcons captain Rasheedat Ajibade suffers ankle fracture appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ECP rejects Punjab govt's proposal for holding LG polls in April 2027
items.description: ISLAMABAD/LAHORE: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) on Thursday rejected the Punjab government’s proposal for pushing local government polls to April next year. Earlier this month, the electoral body proposed holding local government elections in Punjab on December 14 and sent a draft of the suggested schedule to the Punjab chief secretary for consultation. However, the Punjab government on Wednesday proposed holding the elections in phases on April 4, 11 and 18, citing smog, dense fog and adverse winter weather conditions expected during December and January. On Thursday, the ECP rejected the government’s request. The decision was taken at a meeting chaired by Chief Election Commissioner Sikandar Sultan Raja. The commission was briefed that in response to ECP’s letter on Oct 2 and draft election programme, the Punjab government replied on Oct 14 that due to dense fog and severe cold weather in December and the commencement of Ramazan in February, it wanted to hold local government elections in three phases in April 2027, a handout by the commission said. According to the statement, the ECP termed the Punjab government’s reply “unsatisfactory” and said a consultative process with the provincial government had been completed on Aug 20, in which the provincial government had agreed to hold local government elections in Punjab between Dec 15 and Jan 15, 2027. “Now, the provincial government wants to change the proposed time frame,” the commission said. The statement said that keeping in view its constitutional and legal responsibilities, the ECP had decided to hold local government elections in Punjab and issue the election schedule immediately. It directed its office to immediately present the draft election programme for Punjab for the commission’s approval. The ECP said it had asked the provincial government to provide list of officers to appoint as district returning officers, returning officers and assistant returning officers. Expressing disappointment over non-provision of lists so far, it directed the provincial government to provide the lists within a week. Punjab seeks delay The Punjab Local Government and Community Development Department had written to the ECP on Wednesday seeking to delay the local government polls. The letter, which conveyed the ministerial committee’s decision, cited smog, dense fog and adverse winter weather conditions expected during December and January, followed by the commencement of Ramazan in February, as reasons for not holding the elections as scheduled. The letter said the cabinet’s ministerial committee had held its second meeting on October 5, during which it deliberated at length on the ECP’s draft election schedule. The committee discussed scenarios arising from the likely tough weather conditions and Ramazan, the letter stated. It proposed holding the local government elections in phases to facilitate the effective deployment of election staff and security personnel, the efficient transportation of polling materials, better administrative oversight and improved accessibility for voters. The phased approach would also help avoid adverse weather conditions typically experienced during December and January and the period immediately following Ramazan, the letter said. The letter added that the Punjab cabinet considered the committee’s recommendations early on Wednesday and approved a proposal to hold the elections in three phases on April 4, 11 and 18, 2027, all of which fall on Sundays. The cabinet also decided that the allocation of districts among the three phases may be deliberated and thereafter mutually agreed with the ECP in a dedicated meeting, keeping in view administrative, logistical, security and geographical considerations as well as weather conditions, the letter said. LG polls The last local government elections in Punjab were held in 2015 under the Punjab Local Government Act, 2013 . Polling took place in phases between October and December 2015, and elected councils assumed office in 2017 after indirect elections for mayors and chairpersons. Since then, local body polls in Punjab have experienced repeated delays. The PTI government had dissolved the elected local bodies in April 2019 before they completed their tenure. The move was later struck down by the Supreme Court, which restored them. They eventually completed their term on Dec 31, 2021. Successive provincial governments repeatedly amended or replaced the Punjab Local Government Act. Each legislative change required the ECP to restart preparations, including delimitation and election planning. Changing laws and administrative delays by successive governments contributed significantly to the postponement of the local body elections. Under Article 140A of the Constitution and the Elections Act, local government elections should be held within 120 days of the expiry of local bodies’ terms. Since the councils’ term ended in Dec 2021, elections were due by April 2022, but they have been repeatedly postponed. On October 5, the ECP, in a meeting, upheld that it was prepared to hold local government polls across the province. On August 6, the Punjab cabinet had approved an allocation of Rs12.5 billion for holding local government elections in the province.
